Intended Audience The contents are for users who are: • Involved in payroll processing • Familiar with the use of an internet browser

Note: Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot set global payroll information.

Your organization should already have set up the initial defaults, files, and preferences required for system administration, as well as client information. You should also have general knowledge of accounting processes and payroll processing. Explaining industry- specific topics other than the use of this software product is outside the scope of this document.

Payroll Tax Q Series The system uses Payroll Tax Q Series®, a program from Vertex Inc., to automatically and accurately calculate payroll taxes when users process payroll. In most cases, the system requires only the correct ZIP code in the employees’ record.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information Properly establishing employee payroll files is essential to maintaining accurate records for your client. • Any deductions to take from an employee’s pay—other than payroll taxes—are listed in the employee’s Recurring Deductions form. • Employee debts are tracked using the Employee Loan and Employee Garnishment forms. • The Employee Deduction Arrears form tracks deductions automatically placed into arrears for employees if their wages were not sufficient to cover a benefit deduction.

Settings in Employee Details Each employee record contains personal information for the employee. Users with the appropriate permissions can access Employee Details through the HR menu under HR|Change. Refer to the online help or the Human Resources User Guide to learn about using this form. Name tab: These fields are read-only; use other features to make changes. • Status Date • Type Date • Position • Employer • Employer Start Date • Last Hire Date • Original Hire Date Address tab: This tab contains the employee’s personal address information. • Deliver Check Home Work tab: Some fields can be adjusted on this tab, and others require you to use other features to change the values. • Benefits Thru Date • Term Reason

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 15 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

Pay tab: This tab contains the employee’s compensation data, including Compensation and Allocations. Tax tab: Use this tab to maintain the employee’s present tax filing status. If you need the tax filing status at the time a voucher was produced, you can find the information on the payroll voucher. This tab also includes the Employment Verification data. Deposit tab: All or part of an employee’s net payment can be deposited directly, and even include a balance amount on the paycheck. Other tab: Various additional employee settings.

Deduction Sequencing The order in which deductions are calculated during initialization is simply based on the order in which the deductions appear on the employee’s Recurring Deductions. That order is determined by the order in which benefits—such as 401(k) plans, FSA plans, group benefit plans, garnishments, and loans—are entered into the system. Since group benefit plans are automatically calculated by the system on a periodic basis, they are usually the deduction codes that appear at the bottom of the list in Recurring Deductions. At the beginning of batch initialization, the system adds all scheduled deductions to the employee’s pay voucher regardless of the cash pay available to support the deduction amounts. After all pay and deductions have been added to an employee’s paycheck and the initial tax calculation is complete, the system searches for any vouchers where the sum of the calculated taxes and payroll deductions exceeds the amount of cash pay. In such cases, the system removes or reduces the deductions to the point where the net cash pay calculated on the voucher is equal to or slightly greater than zero. The system performs the following process until the net pay is equal to or slightly greater than zero: 1. Removes or reduces deductions that are currently in arrears and were added to the pay voucher. 2. Removes or reduces employee loan deductions. 3. Removes or reduces other scheduled deductions, beginning with one-time deductions. 4. Removes or reduces deductions that are the result of a benefit billing adjustment. 5. Removes or reduces deductions that contribute to the cost of a group benefit plan, and puts any amount not deducted into arrears. 6. Removes or reduces any voluntary deductions that are set up to go into arrears, and puts any amount not deducted into arrears. 7. Removes or reduces any voluntary deductions that are not set up to go into arrears. 8. Removes or reduces any retirement contribution deductions. 9. Removes or reduces any FSA contribution deductions. If the net pay is still not adjusted, it is probably the result of a manual override made to a tax calculation. In such cases, the payroll processor must manually remove the override and recalculate the batch.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

Working with Recurring Deductions The Recurring Deductions form lists all payroll deductions, with the exception of payroll taxes. Use this form to enter voluntary deductions for the selected employee. For example:

There is no limit to the number of defined deduction codes you can enter for an employee. You cannot enter the same deduction code more than once for the same employee, however, with the exception of loans and garnishments. Note the following: • On the Recurring Deductions form, you can only edit voluntary deductions that are not associated with a plan. • If you enter or select a voluntary deduction with an assigned rebate bill code, an error message displays, “A Third Party Payee can only be applied to a Voluntary type deduction code with no Rebate Bill Code assigned. Check the deduction code settings or apply the Third Party Payee to an applicable code.” Click OK to continue. • If you enter or select a restricted deduction code (that is, a code not submitted on the Control tab in the Client Details form), a warning displays and you cannot save the record, “Warning - is not a deduction code defined on the Client Detail Control tab.” Click OK to continue. Note: Service providers can enable the ALLPAYCODESINT custom feature code on the System Parameters form to override the restriction listed above, so the system imports any deduction codes, including the allowed deduction codes that are defined in the Control tab on the Client Details form. • When the first payroll for a pay period is processed with a zero ($0.00) amount without enough funds to cover a voluntary recurring deduction, the system takes the deduction on the next payroll for the same pay period, if there are funds available to cover it.

To enter voluntary deductions: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. The system displays the current deductions. Note: The Next Pay Date field displays informational date value that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process. 2. You can enter voluntary deductions. For each deduction to take:

•    Enter the deduction Amount. This is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation

Deduction Type Definitions In some forms, deduction types display as abbreviations. • V - Voluntary Deduction • G - Wage Garnishment • L - Employee Loan Payment • K - Pre-Tax Retirement Contribution • KC - Catch-Up Retirement Contribution • KE - Post-Tax Retirement Contribution • KL - Retirement Plan Loan Payment • KR - Roth 401K Contribution • KCR - Roth 401K Catch- Up Contribution • C - Section 125 Plan Contribution • F - Flexible Spending Account • P - Post-tax Benefit

Deduction Methods In some forms, deduction methods display as abbreviations. • F - Fixed • R - (Rate) x (Hours Worked) • L - Tax Levy Reverse Calculation • G - Garnishment • K - Retirement Plan • PG - Percent of Gross Earnings: includes all payments, which are expense reimbursements, fringe benefits, and earnings

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

• PE - Percent of Gross Earnings: includes pay codes with Earning disburse type • PS - Percent of Straight Time: includes pay codes with Straight rate class • U - Union The calculation method determines how the system calculates the deduction amount, or where it obtains the calculation method.

Entering Employee Deduction Details Enter any relevant details for recurring deductions in the Employee Deduction Details form, which you can access by clicking Edit Detail on the Recurring Deductions form. (See Working with Recurring Deductions on page 17.)

To edit a recurring deduction, do the following: 1. Enter the Limit amount, which is the most that the system can deduct in a payroll period. This amount overrides any limit defined for this deduction code. If you do not enter a limit here, then any limits defined for this deduction code apply. 2. Enter the Maximum amount the system can deduct on a monthly, quarterly, yearly, or lifetime basis, as set in the Basis field. Any maximum set here overrides the maximums defined for the deduction code. If you do not enter a maximum here, then any maximums set for the deduction code apply. Note: When a rehired employee’s lifetime maximum deduction amount is reached as based on their past deductions and their rehired deduction amount, the deduction stops occurring. 3. Select the Basis to which the Maximum applies: Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, Lifetime, or Pay Period. Note the following when using the Pay Period option: • Selecting Pay Period processes the deduction once per pay period, which can only be used in conjunction with a voluntary deduction type. (If you select a deduction type for a non-voluntary deduction type, then the Pay Period option does not display.) In addition, there is no requirement for a maximum amount when you set the basis by pay period. • To allow the system to process arrears, if you select the Pay Period option you cannot add an amount in the Maximum field. (The system disables the Maximum field.) • When set to Pay Period in the following scenario for regular, special, or manual payrolls, the system only processes voluntary deductions once per pay period: • The voluntary deduction must be configured in the Recurring Deductions form. • The deduction type must be Voluntary. 4. For Voluntary Deductions, you can select Track Arrears. When you select this option, if the deduction amount for this employee cannot be taken due to insufficient earnings, it will go into arrears. 5. Select Mandatory if this deduction is for goods or services provided to the employee that are a mandatory part of employment. 6. Enter a Start Date; the system begins processing the deduction on or after this date. 7. Enter a Stop Date; the system stops processing this deduction on or after this date.

  1. For Voluntary Deductions, you can enter a G/L Override Acct to use rather than the default account number for this deduction.
  2. The Third Party Payee Code to establish a payment to a designated payee.
  3. Enter the Match Method used to calculate the match, either Flat or Percent.
  4. Enter the Match Amount as either a flat amount or a percentage, depending on the Match Method.
  5. Enter a Match Description to print on the Batch Match Code Summary report.

Setting Up and Tracking Employee Loans Use the Employee Loans form to establish employee loan information, track the payment of the loan, and view loan payments that were deducted from employee paychecks. Outside of this form, you can track arrears against the employee loan using one of two methods, which are described in Tracking Arrears (page 22). When you set up a new loan for an employee, PrismHR automatically generates a unique loan identification number. You then enter the amount, date, and reason (optional) for the loan, as well as the employee’s payment deduction amount and frequency. The Employee Loans panel in the Employee Loans form establishes the information required for the employee loan. Click the Data Import Tool icon ( ) to upload a database file and import data. For more information, see Using the Data Import Tool (page 72).

Note the following: • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Employee Loans form cannot import data using the Employee Loans import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on the Employee Loans form.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

• Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employee Loans form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Employee Loans form. • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employee Loans form can view the Employee Loans import template, but cannot import data.

Setting Up an Employee Loan To set up an employee loan, do the following: 1. Enter an existing Loan Number or click Set up a new loan. PrismHR assigns the loan numbers. 2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. This is the employee who is responsible for the loan. 3. Enter the Loan Date on which this loan was granted. 4. Enter the Loan Amount granted to the employee. This value must be greater than zero. 5. Enter the Reason for Loan. 6. Enter the Loan Payment amount to deduct automatically from each paycheck in order to repay the loan. 7. Select the Payment Frequency for the payroll deduction; the default is once per pay period. 8. Enter the Payback Amount required to consider the loan paid in full, which is the amount of this loan plus interest (if any). 9. Enter the Deduction Start Date on which payroll deductions will begin to pay back the loan. 10. Enter the Deduction Stop Date on which payroll deductions will cease. Note: If you do not enter a Stop Date, PrismHR continues to deduct loan payments until the Payback Amount has been satisfied. 11. Select the Deduction Code used for the employee loan. 12. Enter the G/L Override Account code to which this deduction is credited. This is used only in the Corporate Edition. 13. Enter or select the Payee for the employee loan. Note: Only payees who have the Loans payee type on the Payees form display in the Select Payee list. Also, you can only enter or select a Payee whose Third Party Format for the Processor ID associated with the Payroll Check Account is set to Cachet or –Select– on the ACH Originators form. 14. The Amount Paid field displays the amount that the employee has paid back on this loan to date. If you are creating a record for a loan where the employee has already made some payments, enter the total paid to date in this field. 15. Click Save.

Tracking Loan Payments The Payments panel displays the payment history of the employee loan. It lists the date of payment, the associated voucher, the ACH reference, such as a garnishment, and the payment amount. Note: The ACH file includes the employee loan deduction amount, the routing and account number, and the client ID and employee ID.

Tracking Arrears Use one of the following methods to track arrears on an employee loan: • Deduction Codes form: Enter or select an Employee Loan Deduction code in the Deduction Code field, then select the To Arrears field. For example:

• Control tab on the Client Details form: Enter or select an Employee Loan Deduction code in the Voluntary/Employee Loan Deductions To Arrears field. (Previously, this field was titled Voluntary Deductions To Arrears.) For example:

Note the following when using the arrears feature: • After an employee loan transfers to arrears, it displays on the Employee Deduction Arrears form, which is accessible from the Payroll|Change menu, and on the Deduction Arrears form, which is accessible from the Actions menu on the Employee Details form. • An employee loan in arrears displays in the Payroll Deduction in Arrears Report, which is accessible from the Payroll|Report menu. (See the Payroll Reports Guide.)

After you setup the tracking method, here’s what happens with the arrears based on the Payment Frequency selected in the Employee Loans form: • Once Each Payroll Period (default): Transfers to arrears and deducted from arrears on each payroll for the employee.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 22 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

• Once a Month: Transfers to arrears and deducted from arrears on the next payroll for the employee. After that occurrence, the deduction always occurs on the first payroll of the month.

Recording Partial Arrears Amounts The system records a partial arrears amount in the To Arrears panel (portion that is placed into arrears) or the From Arrears panel (portion of the arrears amount from previous pay period that displays as being deducted) in the Deductions tab on the Payroll Voucher form, if the employee is only paid enough to deduct some of the loan deduction amount. The Loan # column in the To Arrears panel or the From Arrears panel displays the loan number from the Employee Loan form that allows loan arrears to display separately based on the loan number, if an employee has more than one employee loan.

Note: If an employee has multiple loans that transfer to arrears or from arrears with the same deduction code on the same date, the system displays multiple rows (one for each loan) in the Loan # column.

Submitting Employee Wage Garnishments You can enter employee wage garnishments using the Employee Garnishments form. When a company is instructed to garnish employee’s wages, the notice of a garnishment typically includes specific instructions on how to deduct the garnishment. Garnishment checks are printed along with paychecks in a payroll batch to ensure prompt delivery to the payee. The system includes these garnishment calculation features: • State garnishment rules • State tax levies that are not limited by CCPA limits • Pro rata and Equal Share child support calculations • Priority and limit calculation logic when dealing with multiple garnishment types • Garnishment fees set up on rule record, but can be overridden for an individual order • Monthly garnishment fee maximums handled automatically

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

•    State garnishment rules determine if child support arrears should be deducted from supplemental pay
     checks

Note:

• If under the Override Rules section, there is an Override Amount indicated and an Override Start Date and an Override Stop Date is not mentioned, then this override amount will be used to process payroll regardless of the date. • Clicking the fields that display as hyperlinks on this form opens a search criteria form; for example, clicking Payee opens the Select Payee form, where you can select an existing payee. • Information for the following fields does not display for deidentified employees: • Docket Number • Annotation • Case Identifier

The options available on the form vary based on the category of garnishment: • Child Support (page 24) • Spousal Support (page 27) • IRS Tax Levy (page 30) • State Tax Levy (page 33) • Franchise Tax Board (page 36) • Bankruptcy Order (page 39) • Creditor Wage Garnishments (page 42) • Student Loan (page 47)

Child Support The following rules apply to child support garnishments: • The system determines the correct maximum percent of disposable income based on employee details • Disposable earnings can be tailored to state rules • Pro-rata and Equal Share allocations are supported for multiple orders • Portion in arrears can be defined • Current order amount given priority on arrearage amount when calculating multiple orders

Employee Garnishment The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 24 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.
  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).
  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.
  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.
  5. Enter the garnishment’s Order Date. This ensures proper garnishment priority ordering in the system. (Only displays if you enabled the TESTGARNEXT and GARNFTLORDER feature codes).
  6. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.
  7. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.
  8. If you enter a Start Date, the system starts payroll deductions on or after this date.
  9. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.
  10. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.
  11. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.
  12. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules Enter the calculation rules for the child support garnishment.

  1. Enter the Withholding Amount to withhold each pay period for the child support garnishment order. This amount should be the sum of current and past due amounts.
  2. Enter the Portion in Arrears amount to withhold for the child support order to cover the arrearage amount.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 25 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

  1. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.

SDU The system supports the ability to create an ACH file with line items for garnishments. This allows you to submit an ACH file that results in an EFT for all state tax levies. If a garnishment is for child or spousal support and the payee is a state disbursement unit, you can set up EFT for the garnishment on the SDU panel. The SDU panel establishes the appropriate state information required to process the wage garnishment. 16. Enter the Case Identifier recognized by the state disbursement unit for child support orders. This field is required if the payee is set to require the case number. 17. Enter the FIPS Code (Federal Information Process Standard) applicable to the child support entity receiving the transaction. This field will be required if the payee is set up to require the FIPS code and it can require a specific length. 18. Select Medical Support Indicator if the non-custodial parent has family medical insurance through their employer.

Setting Temporary Garnishment Overrides You can establish temporary garnishment overrides based on specified dates by updating the settings in the Override Rules panel.

To set temporary garnishment overrides, do the following: 1. In the Override Rules panel, complete the following fields:

 Field                                    Description
 Override Amount                          Enter the temporary Override Amount to use during the specified date
                                          range.
 Override Start Date                      Enter the temporary Override Start Date.
 Override Stop Date                       Enter the temporary Override Stop Date.
 Suppress Voucher Types                   Select the Suppress Voucher Types, which are the pay types exempt
                                          from this garnishment. This setting is not controlled by the override start
                                          and stop dates. Instead, it applies to the entire garnishment record.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 26 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

 Field                                    Description
 Suppress From Unscheduled                Select Suppress From Unscheduled Payrolls, if the garnishment should
 Payrolls                                 not be taken out of unscheduled payrolls.
 Override G/L Account                     Enter the Override G/L Account that identifies the account number this
                                          garnishment credits.
  1. When you have finished entering the information, click Save.

Payments History The Payments History panel provides a list of garnishments that have been paid to date.

• The table lists the information for each payment: • Voucher Number: Each voucher that has been paid against this garnishment • Pay Date: Date on the voucher • Amount Due: Amount due as calculated on the voucher • Paid On: Date each check was paid • Check Number: Number on the check used to pay the garnishment to the payee • ACH Reference: Reference for the ACH transaction used to pay the garnishment to the payee • EFT/Check$: Amount of each check or transaction • Click Adjust to make an adjustment to the table. This does not affect accounting updates or functions, but can cause an adjustment to the employee’s next paycheck.

Calculation Rules Enter the calculation rules for the state tax levy.

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.
  2. Specify one of these methods to determine the withholding amount: • Enter a Flat Amount to withhold from the employee’s net pay. • Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s: • Gross Pay: all taxable wages • Net Pay: gross pay minus taxes and preceding garnishments • Starting Net Pay: gross pay minus taxes • Subsequent Gross Pay: gross pay minus preceding garnishments
  3. Enter the Exempt Amount, which is the amount of wages that are exempt from the state tax levy. The amount levied will be equal to the disposable income, less the exempt amount.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 34 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

  1. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.
  2. If you are configuring a State Tax Levy garnishment, you may enter the Federal Poverty Guideline amount for the employee’s pay frequency. This field is optional. This field is only visible if you are configuring a State Tax Levy garnishment. The field accepts numeric values and rounds to two decimal places. When calculating garnishment withholdings for a State Tax Levy during payroll processing, the Federal Poverty Guideline (FPG), if present, is enforced to ensure that the garnishment is not withheld in excess of the employee’s Gross Wage - FPG amount.

EFT The system supports the ability to create an ACH file with line items for garnishments. This allows you to submit an ACH file that results in an EFT for franchise tax board garnishments and state tax levies if your organization has selected the Consolidated ACH File Processing Used option in System Parameters. The EFT panel allows you to enter the case identifier for the wage garnishment.

Note: This panel displays only for franchise tax board garnishments and state tax levies where the Payee is a garnishing authority with EFT parameters.

Many states permit submission of tax levies by ACH, and some states require it. In addition, the franchise tax board garnishment can be used for any state.

  1. For state tax levies set up for EFT, enter the Case Identifier. This field will be required if the payee is set up to require the case number.

Creditor Wage Garnishments The following rules apply to creditor wage garnishments: • Majority of states follow CCPA limits • Tips generally not considered earnings • Child support orders take priority • In conjunction with child support orders, garnishment can be taken only if the child support percent of earnings is less than 25%

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 42 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

Employee Garnishment The Employee Garnishment panel maintains the basic information required for the wage garnishment.

  1. Enter the Docket Number assigned by the government agency or court for this wage garnishment.
  2. Select the Category for the type of garnishment being withheld. This determines some of the other panels that display (described below).
  3. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. You cannot change the employee for a existing garnishment.
  4. Enter the Receipt Date on which the wage garnishment notice was received from the issuing authority.
  5. Enter the name of the Issuing Authority that issued this garnishment.
  6. If the state requires you to use an ID other than the docket number, enter it in the State ID# field. This number appears on the checks instead of the docket number.
  7. If you enter a Start Date, the system starts payroll deductions on or after this date.
  8. If you enter a Stop Date, the system stops payroll deductions on or after this date.
  9. Enter the Payee ID to whom amounts withheld for this wage garnishment will be paid. If the payee record is set up to use EFT, the SDU or EFT panel might display.
  10. Enter the Deduction Code used for this garnishment.
  11. Enter an Annotation to print in the Memo field of the check stub. There are two lines available.

Calculation Rules Enter the calculation rules for the creditor wage garnishment.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 43 Chapter 1 Employee Payroll Information

  1. Enter the Total Garnishment amount owed by the debtor to be collected under the garnishment order. If no limit is imposed, enter 0.
  2. Specify one of these methods to determine the withholding amount: • Enter a Flat Amount to withhold from the employee’s net pay. • Enter a Percent and then select whether it should be calculated based on the employee’s Gross Pay, Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes and other garnishments), or Starting Net Pay (gross pay minus taxes).
  3. Enter the Pay Period Limit, which the system uses in conjunction with a Percent calculation to set a dollar limit on the total garnishment amount per pay period.
  4. Enter the Garnishment Fee that is associated with this garnishment, which PrismHR deducts from the employee’s pay each time it processes the garnishment.
  5. Select Non-Consumer Garnishment if this garnishment is a judgment or non-consumer credit garnishment. The system applies the state rules for that type of garnishment.
  6. Select Head of Household if the employee is considered the head of their household for tax purposes. When this is selected, the system takes into account any maximum percentage for garnishments set on the State Garnishment Rules record for the state. If there is no maximum percentage for heads of household, the system uses the standard maximum percent of disposable or gross pay.

Limit Overrides This section only appears when Creditor Wage Garnishment is selected from the drop-down under the Category field. Use the Limit Overrides panel to override any state-level settings as needed. Note that you can only reduce the maximum for this employee’s wage garnishment; you cannot use these fields to exceed state or federal maximums.

  1. Enter the Maximum Percent and specify whether that applies to the employee’s disposable or gross Pay.
  2. Enter the Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier, which is the number of hours to multiply by the employee’s minimum wage to calculate the maximum disposable earnings that the creditor can garnish. (This will be overridden if the garnishment maximum is lower.) For example, if the multiplier is 40, the system multiplies the minimum wage by 40. The resulting amount is the minimum pay that an employee should have after taxes and garnishments. A standard creditor can garnish the amount left after subtracting taxes and the minimum pay amount from an employee’s gross pay.
  3. Select the Minimum Wage Rate Source used to determine the minimum hourly rate for this garnishment.
  4. Select the Hours Calculation Method used to calculate minimum net pay for semi-monthly or monthly pay periods under CCPA rules. • Factored: Multiplies the weekly hours by either a factor 2.16 (for semi-monthly) or 4.33 (for monthly). The factor method can be less accurate due to rounding errors, but some states specify its use. • Annualized: Multiplies the weekly hours by 52 and then divides by number of pay periods in the year. For example, for semi-monthly, the calculation is ( (30.00 x 52)/24 ).
  5. Enter the Maximum Monthly Fee to collect from the employee for the creditor wage garnishment.
  6. Indicate whether Reduce Limit by Fee Amount should reduce the limit by the administrative processing fee for this state. • Yes: The system reduces the limit. • No or Select One: The system does not reduce the limit.
  7. Select the Additional Disposable Deductions that are deducted from gross earnings to calculate disposable income for the purpose of calculating this employee’s creditor wage garnishment.
  8. When an Override State Code is selected for an employee, the employee creditor wage garnishment will follow the State Garnishment Rules for the selected Override State on the Employee Garnishments form and not the SUTA state. This field is optional. For example, if an employee is working in NY with NY SUTA and has a creditor garnishment with GA selected for the Override State Code field on the Employee Garnishments form, then creditor garnishment for that employee will be calculated based on State Garnishment Rules for GA instead of NY. The creditor garnishment will now follow the withholding limits

Employee Deduction Arrears Use Employee Deduction Arrears to hold a deduction in arrears whenever an employee’s wages are not enough to cover a benefit deduction. This holds the deduction in arrears until the next pay period when the employee is paid. The system then attempts to take the deduction again. If the wages are still not able to cover the deduction, the deduction amount accumulates as long as it is scheduled to be taken. The benefits billing for that period is also sent to Deduction Arrears. Only benefit deductions are sent to Arrears.

Note: You can only use this form to change existing arrears record information, not create new records. The system creates Employee Deduction Arrears records during payroll batch processing.

An arrears record only exists if a deduction is held in arrears for that employee. You can adjust this record by changing the deduction amount or forgiving a deduction by deleting a line item. It is not possible to add a deduction to this form. Once the deduction from arrears is applied to a paycheck, the arrears record becomes unavailable for viewing. In addition, you can: • Initialize outstanding amounts for employees by creating one or more one-time deduction records. • Update an existing record by adjusting the arrears amount on a line or deleting the entire line.

Note: Make sure the benefit deduction is properly reconciled before clicking Delete as the deduction cannot be restored.

To access this form and change employee arrears: 1. Click Payroll|Payroll Change| Employee Deduction Arrears. The form displays with the Employee field link. 2. Specify Employee information by: • Entering the Employee name, ID, or Social Security number. • Clicking the Employee link or pressing Ctrl+Enter in the search field to open the search selector. If the employee has a history of arrears, the system displays this information. Note: The Next Pay Date field displays informational date value that helps you to quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process. 3. You have these options:

Defining Employee Position Rates You can pay the employee or bill the client at different rates based on the employee pay rates and positions by using the Employee Position Rates form.

Note: For example, if an employee should typically be paid $10.00 per hour when working in the retail position but $15.00 per hour for PTO, enter the employee’s ID, the position code, and 10.00 for the Standard Pay Rate, then enter the PTO Pay Code in the table and 15.00 for the Pay Rate and the appropriate Bill Rate.

To define employee position rates, do the following: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. If any employees have position rates defined, they display in the list on the right; you can select one to edit or enter a new one. 2. Enter the Position Code for the position that applies to this position rate. 3. If you enter a Standard Pay Rate, it overrides the pay rate for this employee for the position. 4. To pay or bill different rates based on pay code and pay rate: a. Enter the Pay Code for this position. The Pay Description displays. If you enter a code that is not defined for the client, the system displays a warning message to confirm that you want to use that code. b. Enter the Pay Rate that overrides the Standard Pay Rate. Premium pay rules apply. c. Enter the Bill Rate for this employee performing in this position. If you don’t enter a rate, the system, uses the standard billing rate. 5. Click Save.

Reversing an Employee Payroll Voucher Use the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form to reverse an employee’s payroll voucher. You can reverse a payroll voucher if it was issued in error and it has not yet been cashed or deposited. Important! The system prevents you from reversing an adjustment voucher that was created by reclassifying a direct deposit. (Reversing these adjustment vouchers could create a check for a negative amount.) In addition, you cannot reverse payroll vouchers when a direct deposit is sent to a check using the Reclassify Direct Deposit form. In this scenario, you cannot reverse these types of adjustment vouchers using the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form. If you try to perform this function a message displays, “You may not reverse this adjustment voucher.” When you void the original voucher in this scenario, the following happens: • The system also voids the adjustment voucher created by sending a deposit to a check. A warning message displays to alert you while the system validates the voucher number, “This voucher had an adjustment voucher created by sending direct deposits to a check. If you void this voucher then the other voucher will be voided also.” • If all the ACH deposits were sent to a check, then the system does not prompt you to draft from the employee’s account. However, if only some of the ACH deposits were sent to a check, then the system prompts you about reversing the remaining deposits, “This voucher contains ACH items, some of which were converted to a check. Reverse the remaining ACH amounts (drafted from the employee’s account)?” If you select Yes, the system creates an ACH journal after the voucher is voided to recover the amount of the deposit that was not sent to a check. • If you choose to draft the remaining deposits from the employee, the system prompts whether you want to put the reversal on hold pending recovery of the ACH. If you select Yes, the system does not post the reversal for the original voucher and does not create the reversals for the adjustment voucher until later when you confirm the pending reversal.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 63 Chapter 3 Reversal and Void Processing

Note: The process to reverse a payroll uses the same method described above, but the system does not provide any prompting.

To reverse an employee’s payroll voucher, do the following: 1. Go to the Payroll|Action menu and select Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal. 2. Enter a voucher number from any year or select the Voucher Number. Note the following: • Vouchers from the current year display in the Search list when you select Voucher Number. To display vouchers from a previous year, select a year in the Pay Period field and then click Search. • To reverse a voucher for a previous year, you must manually enter the Voucher Number. • If the system displays a message that informs you that the date was changed to today, click OK. • If you select a voucher from a different quarter, the system warns you when it changes the void date to today. This is because there can be tax implications. Click OK, then proceed. • If you selected a voucher than includes ACH direct deposit, the system asks you for additional information; see Reversing a Voucher that Includes ACH on the facing page. • If the system displays a message that informs you that the maximum days for an ACH Reversal for the checking account is exceeded, then you can choose to either continue or stop the reversal. Click Yes to continue processing the reversal or click No to stop the reversal process and clear the form. • If you are in different time zones when processing voids, you can enable the system-level custom feature code, UNRESTRICT-VOID-DATE, to edit the Reversal/Void Date. Important! This is a global setting, so if you enable the UNRESTRICT-VOID-DATE custom feature code it impacts the Reversal/Void Date field for all users who have access to process voids. Note the following if you enable the UNRESTRICT-VOID-DATE custom feature code: • After you either dismiss or accept any prompts that are part of the standard voucher reversal, the Reversal/Void Date is available for editing. • If you select a voucher with a current or future pay date, the Reversal/Void Date is available for editing.

  2. Indicate whether the system should use Today or the Pay Date as the date for the reversal.

Reversing a Payroll You can reverse all the vouchers in a payroll batch at once using the Payroll Reversal form. This is a full batch reversal: • All vouchers, including direct deposit, will be voided. Any garnishments will also be reversed. This occurs because any garnishments sent using ACH/EFT are not voided in the system. (Adjusting the garnishment record is a manual process for these items.) • The credit will be exactly the reverse of the original invoice; there are no calculations. • Any Client Bill Pending transactions will not be reinstated; be sure to confirm them when you complete the reversal. • Any manual checks posted during the batch will not be reinstated as open. The will be voided with the rest of the batch. • You cannot reverse payrolls that contain HSA ACH transactions. In this case, a warning message displays, “This payroll contains an HSA ACH transaction which will not be reversed with this process. If you have questions regarding this transaction you should cancel the reversal and check with your manager.”

To reverse a payroll: 1. Select Payroll Reversal from the Payroll|Action menu. 2. In the Select a Payroll field, enter the payroll batch you need to void. The form populates and also displays notices. 3. Enter the Void Date (the default is today’s date). 4. Enter the Void reason. For example:

  1. If you need to exclude any miscellaneous vouchers from the batch reversal, remove the checkmark from the Include in Reversal checkbox. For example:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 68 Chapter 3 Reversal and Void Processing

  1. Click Refine/Review Voucher Selection Before Reversal to review the vouchers in the payroll batch. For example:

    If you want to exclude some pay vouchers from the batch reversal, remove the checkmark from the Include in Reversal checkbox. Excluded vouchers move from the list on the left to the list on the right.

  2. When you are ready, click Void Batch.

  3. The system displays the Processing Voucher Reversal form while it processes the reversal.

  4. Respond to any messages that display.

  5. When the Close button is enabled, the reversal is complete. You can close the form and return to the Batch Reversal form.

Note: All dates and times in PrismHR are Central Time.

Voiding Payroll Batch or Voucher You can void payments in PrismHR, either a single check or a whole batch, using the Void and Reissue Checks form. During this process, the system voids the original check and issues a new check number that is effective on the date it was processed. Important! You cannot void and reissue a reconciled or an escheated check. If a check is set to R (reconciled) status or E (escheated) and you try to void and reissue it, an error message displays. For example, the following error message displays if you try to void and reissue a reconciled check, “This check is already reconciled and cannot be reissued.” Also, if you enter a voided check number in this form, an error message displays, “This check is already voided and cannot be reissued.”

To void payments and reissue a check: 1. Access the Void and Reissue Checks form on the Payroll|Action menu.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 69 Chapter 3 Reversal and Void Processing

  1. Enter or select the original voucher in the Payroll Number field and note the Check Number and Pay Date (for example, check number 8216, and pay date 02/02/2024). Note: Enter or select the Bank Account associated with the original check number to display other data, including the pay date information.

  2. Click Void and Reissue Checks.

  3. After the system voids and reissues the check, access the Payroll History form on the Payroll|View menu.

  4. Select the Payroll Number where the original check was processed. The Payroll Summary form displays.

  5. Select the Summary icon ( ) next to the Payroll Number. The Payroll Reports form displays.

  6. Locate the voided and reissued payment and select the Open File icon ( ). A browser window opens.

  7. Select Open file to download the file. The reissued check displays a new check number and pay date in the Time Sheet Report. Note the following: • You cannot void and reissue a reconciled check. If a check is set to R (reconciled) status and you try to void and reissue it, the following error message displays, “This check is already reconciled and cannot be reissued.” Also, if you enter a voided check number in this form, an error message displays, “This check is already voided and cannot be reissued.” • Employees who are paid using pay on-demand processing have an invoice amount that is debited on the ACH file. However, if you void the pay on-demand voucher, the invoice amount displays as a credit on the ACH file. Note the following: • If you run the pay on-demand process (that is, you generate a file) and then you complete a void, no changes occur in the history file. • If you do not generate a file and a void occurs, then the system does not include the voucher in the next file creation.

Using the Data Import Tool The Data Import Tool lets you upload data and import it into the system. The Data Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back Office menu. For example, the following form displays after you access the Data Import Tool and select the Department Codes import template option:

Note the following: • The list of Import Template options display in alphabetical order.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 72 Chapter 4 Import Processing

• You can also access the Data Import Tool by selecting its link on the Benefit Imports & Reporting landing page. (You must have either Full or Inquiry access set in your user role for the Data Import Tool (HRPY.WORK*DATABASE.IMPORT.ENTRY). Otherwise, this link does not display.) Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you select the import template that you want on the Data Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields. In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing, whose link resides on the Data Import Tool form, to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type. Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file: • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.” • If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

Using the Sample Header File Before starting the import process, you can first download a sample header file by clicking that link on the Data Import Tool form after selecting an import template option or from a local form that displays the Import icon ( ), such as the Departments form. For example:

Note: The header file is in .csv format. You can save the file in .csv or .txt format. After you click the Download Sample Header File link, the system downloads or prompts for download a sample header file that displays columns and headers that match each column and description for the import template option. Also, the file displays a title that matches the selected option. Note: The sample header file is only available to users who have access to the selected import template option.

Importing Client Details Special Delivery Instructions You can import special delivery instructions for clients to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 100 Chapter 4 Import Processing

To upload and import client details special delivery instructions, do the following:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.
  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Client Details (Special Delivery). When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) You can enable one of the following fields during imports: • Replace existing data: Replaces existing data with data included in the file but does not remove data that is not included in the file. For example: • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes. • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system keeps the location 2 delivery method data. • Remove existing data (default): Removes existing data that is not included in the file for that client. For example: • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes. • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system removes the location 2 delivery method data. • Keep existing data: Prioritizes keeping existing data and adds new data included in the file. (That is, if data exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.) For example: • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system keeps the existing data, not the data included in the file. • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the location 2 delivery method data remains the same in the system. The layout requirements are:

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 101 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Field Description Category Description • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • All Locations: Indicates if special delivery method applies to all locations. • Location Code: Indicates location code for this special delivery. • Company Override Method: Indicates special delivery methods defined in your system. • Days In Transit: Indicates special delivery method’s number of days in transit. • Bill Event Codes: Indicates ID of billing event that the system uses to track this special delivery method. If there is no charge for the special delivery method, leave this field blank. • Special Bill Amt: Indicates override for the standard billing amount for this client. • Create Spec Sheet: Indicates that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. (Do not use this option if a special sheet is not necessary.) • Method Active: Indicates status of this special delivery method. • Method Until: Indicates date when the special delivery method should stop being used for the client. • Special Message: A special message that prints on the special delivery sheet. • Name: Indicates name that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • Address: Indicates address that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • Address 2: Indicates second address line that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • City, State, Zip Code: Indicates city, state, and zip code that should appear on the special delivery sheet. • Delivery Sheet Format: Indicates special delivery sheet format used to ensure that the address on the printed special delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

Leave this option unchecked to add this information to existing employee dependent records, including duplicates. When this option is checked, the validation logic evaluates any previously identified dependent record not included in the current import file to determine if that dependent record has current coverage or prior coverage history. Additionally, an informational message stating, “Required fields may vary based on client setup for New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides” displays. • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have current coverage or prior coverage history: The record is skipped and the following error message displays: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID [Dependent ID Number] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with it.” A variation of this same message displays when multiple dependent records with current coverage or prior coverage history must be skipped for the same employee: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID’s [Dependent ID Numbers separated by a comma] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with them.” • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have no current coverage or prior coverage history associated with it: The record is deleted. This validation works similar to the validation logic used when you attempt to manually delete a dependent with coverage history from the system. In that instance, a message displays indicating that you cannot delete the record but you can mark it Inactive.

Required Fields Validation When fields are configured as required fields on either the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form or the New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides form, validations are in place to ensure correct data is passed and required fields are not missing or invalid during the File Upload process.

l   Birth Date - Must have valid date format.
l   Gender - Must have valid value (i.e., M, F, X, or D).
l   Relation - Must have valid value. The system uses the Relation Codes specified here to validate
    against: Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Global) > Relationships.

Missing Data Checks: If the following fields are configured as required and the field values are missing, an error message displays on the Messages tab of the Data Import tool for each missing value. l Social Security Number l Birth Date l Gender l Relation l Address (Address Line 1, City, State, ZIP Code)

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Field Description Category Description • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • Employee Identifier (required): Either the SSN, Employee ID, or the Employee Number of an employee who works for the client and belongs to a pay group included in the payroll batch (can be a terminated employee). If needed, you may enter more than one line for an individual employee. Note: Only the last four digits of the SSN display when you review the information on the File Content tab. • Deposit Status (required): Indicates the following:

                                •     For active (A) deposit status, the system generates an ACH entry
                                      for the voucher.
                                •     For inactive (I) deposit status, the system produces a paycheck
                                      during payroll processing for the net amount of the pay voucher.
                           •    Pay Types to Deposit (required): Indicates the deposit pay types that
                                the system directly deposits, which include the following:
                                •     All (RVS): All voucher types
                                •     Regular (R): Only regular checks
                                •     Vacation (V): Only vacation checks
                                •     Supplemental (S): Only supplemental checks
                                •     Reg & Vac (RV): Regular and vacation checks
                                •     Reg & Sup (RS): Regular and supplemental checks
                                •     Sup & Vac (SV): Supplemental and vacation checks
                           •    Suppress Account Number Print: Prevents the system from printing the
                                employee’s bank account number on the direct deposit advice. The
                                allowed values are Y or N.
                           •    Type (required): The bank account type for the deposit transaction,
                                which includes the following:
                                •     C: Checking
                                •     S: Savings
                                •     HE: Employee checking
                                •     HES: Employee savings
                                •     HC: Client checking
                                •     HSC: Client savings
                                Note the following:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 116 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Field Description • An employee or client cannot have more than one type of HSA deposit. (They can deposit to a checking or savings account, but not to both accounts.) • A type that begins with an “H” always designates an HSA deposit. • Transit Number (required): The nine-digit ABA Transit Number of the receiving bank or other financial institution. • Account Number (required): The account number associated with the transit number where the money is deposited. (This number is alphanumeric with a maximum of 0-9 characters.) • Pay Type (required): The deposit pay types for the data on the specific row. (You can select different pay types for different accounts.) The pay types include the following: • All (RVS): All voucher types • Regular (R): Only regular checks • Vacation (V): Only vacation checks • Supplemental (S): Only supplemental checks • Reg & Vac (RV): Regular and vacation checks • Reg & Sup (RS): Regular and supplemental checks • Sup & Vac (SV): Supplemental and vacation checks • Method (required): The method used to determine the deposit amount. The allowed values are F, P, or B. (Note: For service providers, additional values are FS and PN.) • Amount (required): The direct deposit amount that is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the deduction code. Working with Imported Address Validation If the import file includes an address that fails validation or USPS-accepted address status, the system displays a dialog during the import process, Database File Import dialog entry, so you can either replace the incorrect address with a validated version or skip (keep) the current address. Note: A prompt displays in this instance, “Click Replace to use the suggested address or Skip to not import the employee’s address.” When this prompt displays during the import process, do one of the following: • Click Replace with New to update the address in the import file. (Note: To apply the correct address information to all address information that displays in this prompt, select Apply to all, then click Replace with New.)

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 127 Chapter 4 Import Processing

• Click Skip to keep the current address. After you make a selection, the dialog closes and a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully uploaded and ready to be imported.” Click OK. (Note: Any skipped addresses do not display and any replaced addresses display in the File Content tab in the Data Import Tool.) After you click Import and the import finishes, a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully imported. View report for details.” (Note: Any skipped addresses display the “Skipped with a Comment” import status.) Note the following: • The Database File Import dialog entry does not display in the following instances: • When the address in the import file is a valid address with no address suggestions (this is equivalent to entering an address in the Employee Details form when no dialog displays suggestions to update the address). • When the fields in a row in the import data display an error (for example, characters instead of numbers in a zip code). • The Database File Import dialog entry does display when the address in the import file is a valid address and there is a suggested update (for example, address line 1 is 555 Elm and the suggested address is 555 Elm Drive).

Updating ZIP Codes Importing ZIP codes adds them to the benefit plan record, but it does not update the ZIP code records at the system-level. You must enter All ZIP codes at the system-level to attach them to a benefit plan. System-level zip code records always display City & State information in the table. For more information, refer to “ZIP Codes” in the System Administration Guide.

To import and update offer types:

  1. To access this form, click (Back Office). In the Operations|Import menu, click Data Import Tool.
  2. Select Offer Types in Import Template. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data. Category Description • Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the benefit plan. • Plan Description (required): Description of the benefit plan. • Insurance Class (required): Indicates the type of coverage this plan provides. • Offer Type (required): Indicates the offer type that classifies the benefit plan.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

  1. Click Download Data File to download the sample header file. The header file contains the four columns in the File Format tab. Fill in the necessary data for all the Benefit Plan IDs to update the Offer Type to build your Import file.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 145 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Note: If you want to update the Offer Type for all Benefit Plan IDs in bulk that do not have an associated
offer type, select Prepopulate file (all plans with BLANK Offer Type). The system downloads a .csv file to
your system that is pre-populated with data from the Group Benefit Plans for all plans with a BLANK offer
type. (If you do not select this field, the system downloads the file with headers only.)
  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.
  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.
  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File displays in the File Upload dialog box.
  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.
  5. Click Close in the File Upload dialog box.
  6. The uploaded Import File name displays in the File Name field on the form. The content of the file displays in the File Content tab. Errors, if any, display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.
  7. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR.
  8. Click Report to display the Imported Offer Types Report. The Import Status column indicates whether the offer type for that plan ID was imported. If not, then the Messages tab states the reason why. Once the import is successful, the system updates the Offer Type field on the Group Benefit Plans form with the plans contained in the Import File.

Category Description • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • Position Code (required) : Abbreviation for the position. • Position Name (required): Name that defines the position. • Position Classification (required): Identifies the job classification. • Position Description: Description for this position. • Supervisory: Indicates a supervisory position. • Tipped Position: Indicates that the position allows tips. • GL Segment 1: Code that defines the G/L account number segment instead of the department or division code. This information is included in the MasterTax RTS file and the Employer and Client LA quarterly files in place of the position’s description. If you do not define a SOC code for the position, the files include the description. • Indiana Seasonal Employee Code: A two-digit code if the position is seasonal and located in Indiana. This code is required for SUI electronic filing in Indiana. • Obsolete: Indicates the position is no longer used. • TTO Code: Indicates a valid Tipped Taxable Occupation Code that applies to an eligible tipped position, which complies with the tips requirements of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

Importing Worksite Locations You can import changes to worksite locations to reduce the amount of manual work required. Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import worksite locations: 1. Select Client. 2. From Client|Change, select Worksite Locations.

  1. On the Worksite Locations form, click Import to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.) The Worksite Locations import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Positions form.

    You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) You can enable the Keep existing data for fields not in the import file field, so optional fields in the Worksite Locations import template will keep their existing data during imports. (If you do not enable this field, the system overwrites optional fields with no data during imports.) Important! When you enable Keep existing data for fields not in the import file in the Worksite Locations import template, the Address entry validation dialog and the File Content tab display blank information for fields not included in the import file, but the import keeps the original information entered on the Worksite Locations form. Working with Imported Address Validation If the import file includes an address that fails validation or USPS-accepted address status, the system displays a dialog during the import process, Database File Import dialog entry, so you can either replace the incorrect address with a validated version or skip (keep) the current address.

Note: The address information consists of the street, city, zip code, geocode, county, state, latitude, and longitude. When this prompt displays during the import process, do one of the following: • Click Replace with New to update the address in the import file.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 175 Chapter 4 Import Processing

 Note the following:
•    To apply the correct address information to all address information that displays in this prompt, select
     Apply to all, then click Replace with New.)
•    Clicking Replace with New updates all data with the contents of the data file and removes existing data
     for that worksite location if there are any blank fields in the import file.

• Click Skip to keep the current address. Note the following that happens if you click Skip: • The system does not apply the latitude and longitude to the address, which is required for the onboarding process. • The system does not import any data in the import file. After you make a selection, the dialog closes and a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully uploaded and ready to be imported.” Click OK. (Note: Any skipped locations do not display and any replaced locations display in the File Content tab in the Data Import Tool.) After you click Import and the import finishes, a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully imported. View report for details.” (Note: Any skipped locations display the “Skipped with a Comment” import status.)

Using the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool You can use the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool to quickly import a list of employees to transfer to new clients. Note the following: • This tool is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Mass Employee Transfer Import form. • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Mass Employee Transfer Import form displays the form in read- only format. • Users who do not have access to a particular client as configured in Client Access Groups cannot transfer employees into or out of the client using the Mass Employee Transfer Import form. • This process accomplishes the same results as executing the standard employee transfer process using the Transfer Employee to New Client form. (See Transferring Employees to New Clients.) The Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back

Office . For example, the following form displays after you access the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 176 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you open the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields. In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type. Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file: • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.” • If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.
  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.
  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.
  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.
  5. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.
  6. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process. While processing the uploaded file, the following validation occurs: • If any mandatory field is missing from the file, the system displays an error message, “ is a required field.” • If the system does not associate the Employee ID with the From Client field, it displays an error message, “Employee not located in client .” • If the values in the Pay Group, To Retire Plan, To Position, and To Location fields are not valid for the To Client record, then the system displays an error message, “Record . is not on file in <field’s filename>.” • In the Termination Reason field, the system identifies a valid value only if the REASON.CODES contain “Termination.” If you provide any other value, the system displays an error message, “ is not a valid Term Reason Code.”
  7. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR. After the import finishes, the following occurs: • If Transfer YTD Check Stubs is enabled, the program transfers the YTD check stubs. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is enabled, the program terminates the employee on the original client using the corresponding Termination Date and Termination Reason from the upload file. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is disabled, the program does not terminate the employee on the original client. • If Terminate Benefit Coverage Today is enabled, the program terminates the employee’s benefit coverage. • If the uploaded file contains a mix of employees who are successfully validated and employees that fail the validations, those employees that are successfully validated are transferred appropriately and the employees that fail validation are documented in the error log and are not transferred or terminated.
  8. Click Report to view the transaction report. This report contains the following information: • Successfully transferred employees display “Success” in the Import Status column. • Employees that failed validation and could not be transferred display “Skipped” in the Import Status column. The “Comments” column for the failed transfer employees displays the error message for whichever failed validation event prevented the transfer.

Managing Batches for Check Import Process Use the Check History Import form for batch management for the check import process. All processes required for check imports can be only accessed from this form using a wizard which takes you step by step through the check import process.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import. Important! If you have employees listed in several clients and employers, you might need to complete a successor wage import before processing a check history import. Note the following instances when you should perform this action: • An employee is listed in the same employer for multiple companies as an active employee: Since this makes a difference for taxes, it affects how the limits are honored. The employee is listed within the same employer, so the system pushes the taxes that were previously processed at the first company to the taxes on this import, so they are over the limit and not including any charges. • An employee is listed in two different employers: The voucher honors the limit for each, so the system does not display any of the taxes over the limit but instead collects those taxes as well. Note: This is typically correct, but if a client only collects the taxes under one employer and the employee is listed in two employers and you do not want to account for taxes under both employers, you can use successor wages to account for those wages. With successor wages in place, the system will not collect taxes under both employers.

      1. Include OASDI taxable amounts on the vouchers - This is the default option where Employer paid OASDI taxable amounts are included on all vouchers in this check import batch.
      2. Do not include - Select this option if you do not want to include Employer paid OASDI taxable amounts included on all vouchers in this check import batch.
    3. Employer FUTA (Tax Code 00-17), select one the of the following:
      1. Include - By default, calculation of employer FUTA tax is included on all vouchers in this batch.
      2. Suppress - Select this option if you want to suppress the calculation of the employer FUTA tax on all vouchers in this batch.
  2. Under the Upload File section complete the following if you want to upload the checks from a file. Skip this section if you only want to enter check history manually.
    1. Click Upload File to upload a check import batch file in a .txt or .csv format. A dialog box opens.
    2. Click Choose File to select the check import batch file from your system in a .txt or .csv format.

Note: When importing a .csv file, you do not need to remove the headers.

c. Click Submit to close the dialog box. The file uploaded now shows on the screen.

Warning - Uploading a replacement Check History Import file You may need to upload a replacement check history import file if you have imported a wrong check history import file or the check history import file is badly formatted and so on. If you try to upload a new check history import file when a check history import file has already been uploaded using the import utility, and to prevent unexpected data loss, you will receive the following pop-up message: Checks have already been imported from a file. If you proceed, the previous imported checks will be cleared and you will lose any corrections you have made. Manually entered checks will be retained. Do you want to clear the existing imported checks and start over? • Click Yes to upload a new check history import file. The file upload pop-up appears. • Existing checks uploaded earlier using the import utility are not cleared until you select the replacement check history import file and click Next. • Checks that were entered manually will be retained.
