Check Import Batch Status Report This report displays the summary information for all check import batches.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on the Check History Import Batch Status Report form.

To access the form, on the Back Office menu, under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import Batch Status Report. You can also access this menu from the Check History Import form. On the Back Office menu, under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import. Click Batch Status Report in the Tools section on the top right.

To generate a summary of all check import batches: 1. Select a Batch Type:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 195 Chapter 4 Import Processing

     •    All
     •    Completed
     •    In Progress
2. Click Generate Report. The Check Import Batch Status Report opens in a new window.
3. Click the XLS link to download the report.

Note the following: • If you select All in the Batch Types field, the report displays all check history import batches under any status (including In Progress and Completed), sorted by Batch ID. For check history import batches created in PrismHR the following batch statuses are available: • 1 - Import Setup • 2 - State & Code Setup • 3 - Enter Check History • 4 - Review & Fix Data • 5 - Calculate Taxes • 6 - Import Complete • If you select Completed under Batch Type, the report displays all completed check history import batches from PrismHR, sorted by Batch ID. • If you select In Progress under Batch Type, the report displays all check history import batches from PrismHR that are in progress, sorted by Batch ID.

Report Output This report contains the following columns:

Column Name Column Description Batch ID This is the check history import batch number. Batch Name This is the name of the check history import batch. Created In The application where this check history import batch is created. Batch Status The status of this check history import batch. Client ID The client ID (or multiple IDs) for whom the check history import batch is created. Note: The space limitations in this column truncate multiple IDs. Download this report to ensure you can view all IDs included in this column. Status Date The date on which this check history import batch was last processed.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 196 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Column Name Column Description Processed By User ID The user ID of the person who last processed this check history import batch. Number of Vouchers The number of vouchers contained for a completed check history import batch only. If the check history import batch is in progress, then this field will remain blank. Total Pay The total pay for a completed check history import batch only. If the check history import batch is in progress, then this field will remain blank.

State & Code Setup This is the second screen of the check import wizard. Use this form to set up the State Tax Rules for the selected check import batch and Code Translation Tables for Earnings, Deductions and Taxes for the check import batch selected in the Import Setup screen. Note the following: • The State & Code Setup option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. • You can only access this screen when you click Next on the Import Setup screen. • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function. • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

This form has the following two sections: • State Tax Rules • Code Mapping

Setting Up State Tax Rules You will need to have state tax rules setup for each state that appears in your imported data either using the check import utility or manual check entry. You can set up the state tax rules for each state from the State Tax Processing Rules link under Tools section in the Check History Import form. If the rules are not set correctly for any of the states that appear in your imported data, you will see errors/discrepacies later in the workflow.

To set up the State Tax Rules for the selected check import batch: 1. If you are importing checks from an import file, then the system will automatically load the default State Tax Rules for all the states contained in the imported spreadsheet. This will ensure that you can set up all the required state tax codes correctly to prevent future errors. The following fields appear in an inline grid along with the values imported for each field:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 197 Chapter 4 Import Processing

•    State - all the states codes contained in the original import file are listed here.
•    State Income Tax Shelter Flag
•    SUTA Shelter Flag
•    SUTA Taxable Limit
•    SUTA Tax Rate (%)
•    Employee SDI Shelter Flag
•    Employee SDI Taxable Limit
•    Employer SDI Taxable Limit
•    Employer SDI Tax Rate (%)
•    Misc Employer State Taxes
  1. You can click a state link above to open the State Tax Rules form for the state in a modal. • The Rule Type section will not be visible. • The Rule Type will be set to Batch as you are accessing this form while processing this check import batch. • The Batch ID will be pre-populated which you cannot change. • The corresponding Batch Name will be displayed. • The Batch Status will display State & Code Setup which is the screen from where you are accessing the State Tax Rules form. • You can edit all the fields on this State Tax Rules form including the State Code. You cannot save this form unless a State Code is selected. • Click Save to save the changes and you will return to the State Tax Rules Section. The changed values will reflect on the inline grid. • Click Delete to delete the state tax rules for the selected state. • Click Cancel to close the form. All changes will be lost. • Click Close to close the form. Changes are saved and reflect in the inline grid.
  2. Click Copy All from Default to copy the default state tax rules to the state tax rules form for the batch. The changed values will reflect on the inline grid. You can use this option to
  3. Click Copy State to Default to copy the state tax rules for this batch to the default state tax rules.

Setting Up Code Mapping For each code that appears in the import spreadsheet, choose the corresponding code in your PrismHR system. Make sure to choose codes with the same tax- settings, or the totals will not match.

If you are importing from a file, then the system will load the codes for Earnings, Deductions and Taxes from the imported spreadsheet. If the imported codes are already contained in your PrismHR code translation tables,

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 198 Chapter 4 Import Processing

they will also reflect in the appropriate table. If not then you will need to manually provide the PrismHR code so that the system can calculate the Earnings, Deductions, and Taxes appropriately. As you already get to see the number of foreign codes that you need to translate (if any), the chances of getting errors is reduced and you can complete the process faster.

Earnings

To map the Imported Pay Codes, complete the following: a. Enter the corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Imported Pay Code OR b. Click the Map to Prism Pay Code link and search from the Select Pay Code dialog box. c. Check the Pay Code Description to confirm that you have selected the correct Prism Pay Code for the corresponding Imported Pay Code. d. In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Imported Pay Code from the Select Pay Code dialog box.

Deductions

To map the Imported Deduction Codes, complete the following: a. Enter the corresponding Prism Deduction Code for the Imported Deduction Code OR b. Click the Map to Prism Deduction Code link and search from the Select Deduction Code dialog box. c. Check the Deduction Code Description and the Deduction Type to confirm that you have selected the correct Prism Deduction Code for the corresponding Imported Deduction Code. d. In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Deduction Code for the Imported Deduction Code from the Select Deduction Code dialog box.

Taxes

To map the Imported Tax Codes, complete the following: a. Enter the corresponding Prism Tax Code for the Imported Deduction Code OR b. Click the Map to Prism Deduction Code link and search from the Select Deduction Code dialog box. You can use the Paid By filter to narrow down your search for the correct Prism Tax Code. c. Check the Tax Code Description to confirm that it is the correct Prism Tax Code for the corresponding Imported Tax Code. d. In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Tax Code for the Imported Tax Code from the Select Tax Deduction Code dialog box. e. You have the option to select if the Prism Tax Code selected is Sheltered or not from the drop-down under the Sheltered? column.

Enter Check History This is the third screen of the check import wizard. Use this screen to manually enter a check. Skip this step if you do not need to enter checks manually. Note the following: • The Enter Check History option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. • You can access this screen from the State & Code Setup screen or from the Check History Entry screen after you have manually entered a check for this check import batch. • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function. • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites. • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form. If you previously manually entered checks for this check import batch, they display on this screen in an inline grid. The inline grid displays the following columns: • Document ID • Employee ID • Employee Name • Client ID • Check Number • Pay Date • Work State • Gross Pay • Total Deductions • Total Taxes • Net Pay

To post the External Third Party Checks Journal: 1. Select a Days Back option to display only the journal data pertaining to that selection, such as 1 Month (default), 2 Months, 3 Months, or 1 Year, or select Show All to display all data. 2. If you want to select: • All transaction dates, select the Select All checkbox in the header row. • Specific transaction dates, select the individual checkboxes beside each of the transaction dates. 3. Performing Slavic 401K Imports You can upload a retirement plan’s database file and import its contents using the Slavic 401K Import form. After a successful import, the process updates employee deferral changes.

Using the Slavic 401K Import Form Use the Slavic 401K Import form to import data from an uploaded database file.

This form consists of the following fields:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 216 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Fields Description

Plan ID Select the Plan ID. After selecting the ID, the system displays the following message: If no Match eligibility rules are found, the Import defaults the “Eligible For Match” field to Y and uses the effective date for the “Match Starts On Date”. If it finds a “Match Starts On Date” less than the effective date, it will set the “Eligible For Match” field to Y and it will use the effective date. Loan Payment Cycle Select one of the following loan payment cycles: • Per Pay Period (default): Loan payment cycle will be paid per pay period. • Monthly: Loan payment cycle will be paid in monthly increments. (This payment cycle can only be selected for new enrollments.) Note: If you select the Monthly loan payment cycle option, observe the following: • The loan payment cycle option automatically reverts to the Per Pay Period option when the employee has an existing retirement enrollment record. • If you are creating a new retirement enrollment, then the record reflects Monthly as the loan payment cycle option; therefore, the loan period entered from the import is honored. • If this is an existing record, it retains the original loan payment cycle value. If the original value was set to Monthly and the import runs with that option set to Per Pay Period, the original value remains set to Monthly.

Carry Forward Existing Deselecting this field prevents the system from carrying forward Amounts if NOT in the existing amounts during the import process. (Note: This field is Import? selected by default.) Data Filename File you uploaded for import, which must be in .csv format, displays in this field. (The filename displays after completing Step 1 in the Import process.) Error Count Total number of errors after the file imports. Any errors encountered during the process display in the window below this field. Imported Records Number of records imported.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 217 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Fields Description

Error Message Displays the error occurred during import process. Note: While performing the Slavic 401K import process, the following validations has been added with regard to the prohibit deductions on the Retirement Plans form: • On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Employee Deferral Deduction Code or the Employee Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type D in column D of the import file on the Slavic 401K Import form, then during the import process, an error message, “Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row .” displays and the import process fails. • On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Roth Post-tax Deduction Code or the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type R in column D of the import file on the Slavic 401K Import form, then during the import process, an error message, “Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row .” displays and the import process fails.

Uploading/Importing a Retirement Plan Clicking Start Import in the Slavic 401K Import panel uploads a retirement plan’s database file and import its contents.

Before You Begin Before you start this process, ensure your database file is set up as follows: 1. Set up an Excel spreadsheet with the following columns: • Column A: Company ID • Column B: Social Security Number formatted as a text field without dashes; for example, 111223333 • Column C: Effective Date in MM/DD/YYYY format • Column D: Deferral Type specifying D as “Pre-Tax” or R as “After Tax” • Column E: Contribution Type specifying 1 as “Flat Amount” or 2 as “Percent” • Column F: Amount specifying Populate if Contribution Type = “1” (no commas) • Column G: Percent specifying Populate if Contribution Type = “2” 2. Do not include a header row. 3. Save the file in .csv format. Also, ensure the employee is employed by the client and enrolled in the retirement plan you want to import.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 218 Chapter 4 Import Processing

Uploading/Importing a Database File To upload a database file in .csv format and import its data, do the following in the Slavic 401K Import panel: 1. Click Plan ID and select the appropriate ID. A dialog displays as described in the table above. Click OK to close the dialog. 2. Click the Loan Payment Cycle option. 3. Click Start Import to upload a database file, then click Choose File and browse to the file. Click submit. 4. The data file imports and a confirmation dialog displays. Click Close. 5. The imported data filename displays in the window, along with any errors encountered. 6. Click Clear to remove information from the window and repeat the process for another retirement plan, or click Close to close the form. The import process accepts Post-Tax Elections (P) in the import file as well. Please note the following while importing new retirement plan elections on this form: l You can now import elections for Post Tax deferral types when Post Tax elections are not prohibited by the Retirement Plan setup. l You can now import elections for standard pre-tax deferrals when Employee Catch-up Deduction Code is

 flagged as prohibited. Please note that no Catch-up amount for pre-tax elections are recorded.

l You can now import elections for Roth deferrals when Roth Catch-up Deduction Code is flagged as

 prohibited. Please note that Catch-up amount for Roth elections are recorded.

l However, you cannot import elections for Post Tax deferral types when Post Tax elections are prohibited

 by the Retirement Plan setup.

Calculating an Employee’s Pay You can calculate the pay for an employee using the Pay Check Calculator form. Note: The Pay Check Calculator form uses either the Deduction Period or manually-entered deductions in the Deductions panel when calculating taxable amounts, but it does not do both. For example: • If the Deduction Period is set, the system ignores manually-entered entries in the Deductions panel for taxable wage calculations.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 220 Chapter 5 Other Processing

• If the Deduction Period is blank, the system recognizes manually-entered deductions for taxable wage calculations. One example for using this form is when the client does business in a state where the law requires that the employee receive a final check upon termination. You can calculate the net amount of the check after all taxes and deductions. Important! PrismHR strongly recommends that you communicate any pay check calculations and final employee check distributions with your payroll departments as soon as possible to ensure that all payroll process issues are taken into account.

Note: To restrict user access to only the calculation function, open the appropriate User Role and set the form access to Inquiry. Users with that user role will be able to perform calculations but cannot create vouchers or checks.

Use the Net Pay option in the Calculation Type to calculate the net pay for the employee. This does not initialize a voucher; use it to simply calculate the employee’s net pay amount; see Calculating Net Pay below.

Calculating Net Pay Using the Pay Check Calculator, you can calculate the net pay for an employee. This does not initialize a voucher; you would use it to calculate the employee’s net pay amount.

To calculate net pay: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. The Pay Check Calculator panel displays the employee’s ID, name, and standard pay period (pay group). 2. Select the Deduction Period that applies to the check, if any. Recurring deductions for that period display in the Deductions panel after you enter hours or amounts in the Gross Pay panel.

  1. The Gross Pay panel initially lists the default pay codes for the client. You can enter values in those fields, and add additional rows as needed. • Select the Pay Code. • Enter the Charge Date. • Select the Position the employee worked. • As appropriate for the client, select the Shift or Project. (These columns are hidden if they are not specified in the Client Details > Time Sheet tab.)

Note: The Shift and Project drop-downs display up to 1000 codes. If the code you need is not in the drop- down, click the link at the top of the column to search for the appropriate code.

•    Enter the Hours/Units to be paid.
•    The Pay Rate defaults from the employee’s information, but you can edit it if appropriate.
The system calculates and displays the Extended Pay.

Note: The system pulls the deductions from the employee’s Recurring Deductions record. If a new deduction is not yet included in that form, it is not listed here.

  1. The Deductions panel lists the employee’s deductions associated with the selected Deduction Period, if any, after you enter gross pay. You can make any edits and additions as needed, otherwise continue to the next step. Each existing Deduction displays, as well as the Deduction Amount Calculated. If you need to enter or edit deductions: • Select the Deduction, if needed. • Enter an amount in Deduction Amount Entered to apply an amount for a new deduction or change the amount for an existing deduction. If you override the deduction amount, the Deduction Amount Calculated value changes to reflect the override amount you entered. If you edit 401(k) or Section 125 deductions, the tax amounts adjust to reflect the new sheltered earnings.

  2. The Taxes panel displays the taxes to be deducted from the employee’s paycheck after you enter gross pay.

  3. The Pay Summary panel displays the totals from the other panels and the calculated net pay.

Net-to-Gross Calculator The Net-to-Gross Calculator is helpful when you are calculating special bonus checks or duplicating a check that has been issued manually by the client. The calculator computes the gross amount that, after taxes and deductions, results in the amount of the check. For example, without the calculator, you might issue a check for a net amount of $100.00 and then guess at the gross amount, estimate the appropriate taxes, and then continue to recalculate and rerun the numbers until the guessed gross amount is accurate (or close enough). Using the Net-to-Gross Calculator, you enter the amount of the check that the employee will receive or has received and select the deduction period that should be included in the calculation, if any. The system performs a reverse calculation to determine the exact gross amount that, with taxes and deductions, ends up with the net payment of the target amount.

To use the net-to-gross calculator: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. This is the person receiving the check. 2. Enter the Pay Date for the check issue date. This must be after the last processed payroll batch pay date. If this payment should be attached to a batch (such as an Other Payments Batch), enter the pay date of the batch. 3. Select the Voucher Type: Regular, Vacation, or Supplemental.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 223 Chapter 5 Other Processing

  1. Select the correct Pay Period that applies to the payment. The system calculates taxes based on the pay period. If you select a different pay period than should apply, the calculated taxes will not match the taxes on the initialized voucher, which results in a voucher without an even net payment amount.

  2. If appropriate, use the Deduction Period to indicate the deduction period that the system should use for calculating standard deductions, benefits, and garnishments. Do not select a period if you do not want to include those in the calculation. (The deduction period does not apply to the supplemental voucher type.)

  3. The Estimated Periods Remaining is important for calculating amounts such as FSA or HSA contributions. It is the number of benefits deduction periods remaining, and the system calculates the default value based on the next scheduled regular batch. Edit the value only as needed.

  4. If appropriate, select the employee’s Work Shift. If the work shift code has a differential that is included in the pay code, the calculator uses the differential in the gross pay calculation. If not, you do not need to select anything.

  5. Enter the appropriate Pay Code. The pay code must apply to the selected voucher type. If you want to add this payment to an Other Payments Batch, you must enter a pay code with a fixed pay calculation.

  6. The Payroll Number defaults to the next regularly scheduled payroll batch for the selected employee. If you want to use a special batch, such as one for bonuses, you would first create one in Payroll Control and then enter that batch number in this field. Note that the system only adds the voucher to the specified payroll batch if you select the Write Batch checkbox after getting the calculation results.

  7. Enter the Target Net Pay amount, which is the final net payment amount of the check.

  8. Press Tab. The system runs the calculations and displays the results.

  9. Review the gross pay amount, deductions, tax withholding amounts, and so on. • If you want to use the Net-to-Gross Calculator to make a payment to the employee within a regularly scheduled payroll batch, select Write Batch and then click Save. The system tells you the number of the batch where the payment is included. This option does not add the payment to a manual or special batch. • If the regular payroll batch that you want to include the payment in is still in time sheet entry status, the system adds it to the payroll. • If the regular payroll batch that you want to include it in has been initialized (calculated), then the payroll processor needs to recalculate the payroll to include the payment.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 224 Chapter 5 Other Processing

•    Because other changes could occur to the employee’s record that would affect the results of this
     payment (for example, changes to deduction amounts or tax withholding information), the payroll
     processor should review the results of the payment amount to ensure that the results are the same.

• If you used the calculator only for estimation purposes, click Clear. To remove an item in the Net-to-Gross Calculator, go to Payroll|Change|Batch Payments. Find the item that you want and click Delete.

Tracking Payments to Employees Use the Manual Check Entry form to track a payment made manually by the client to an employee. The manual check process generates a voucher that the system includes in the client’s next payroll batch, then updates the payroll registers when the payroll processor posts the batch. After completing a manual check entry, you can create a zero-dollar, non-negotiable pay stub by accessing the voucher from either the Process Payroll form or the Employee Voucher form. (This feature is only available for new payrolls, not previously processed payrolls.)

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 225 Chapter 5 Other Processing

Note: Only service providers are allowed to select a bank account number in the Bank Account field, so this field does not display for Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors. Instead, the bank account number defaults to 999 in the background when WSMs and WTAs are processing this form.

To track payments to employees, do the following: 1. Click New to create a new manual check entry, or enter or select the Reference number to view an existing entry. This is a unique internal identifier, and not the same as the check number. Note the following: • If you edit an existing manual check entry, you can click the Show Details button to see the voucher information, which consists of the pay summary, deductions summary, and tax summary, along with the gross pay, deductions, taxes, and net pay. • If you enter or select an existing manual check entry that was created by processing a backdated leave request, the Backdated Leave Request attribute displays in the upper-right corner. (This is helpful in determining whether a manual check entry is for a backdated leave request.) 2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 3. Enter the Check Date. The default is the current date. When your organization processes the payroll that includes this check, the pay date on the manual check voucher will be set to the date as the payroll batch for tax liability purposes. The period start and end dates remain the same. 4. The system populates the Voucher number. 5. Select the Voucher Type that was issued to the employee: Regular, VOID, or Supplemental. 6. Enter the Bank Account from which the check was drawn. If you select an account that will not credit the client back for the amount of the net check, the system warns you and gives you the opportunity to change or confirm the account. 7. Enter the Check Number that the client issued to the employee. Note: When working with existing manual check entries, you can update the check number if it is still in Pending status. (This option is not available if the entry is in Initialized or Posted status.) 8. Enter the amount of Tip Gross Receipts to record if you require allocated tip calculations. 9. Select a Pay Period to use in calculating taxes for the pay amount: Weekly, Biweekly, Semi-monthly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Annually. The system uses the default value of the employee’s pay group. 10. Select the Deduction Period for which the system should calculate standard deductions and benefits. If you do not select a deduction period, the system does not include any standard deductions. 11. Enter the Work Shift applicable to the payroll voucher, if any. 12. Enter the Period Start Date. 13. Enter the Period End Date.

Creating and Deleting Invoices for Miscellaneous Charges Use the Miscellaneous Invoice form to create an invoice for stand-alone, miscellaneous charges. You can also delete pending records (those records that have not been processed) and process locks using this form.

To create an invoice for miscellaneous charges, do the following: 1. Enter the Bill Date for this invoice. 2. Select Suppress ACH if this invoice should not follow ACH rules established for this client. 3. For each event code: • Select the Event Code to bill. The Description displays. • Enter the units and rate to bill, or the total amount: Enter the Billing Units and Bill Rate. The Amount To Bill populates automatically. Enter the Amount To Bill. Typically, you would enter Billing Units of 1, and then the Bill Rate populates with the same value as the Amount To Bill. • Enter the Location code. This is required for sales tax calculations. (Note: If the client is set to ACH by Location, you must enter a Location code.)

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 228 Chapter 5 Other Processing

•    Enter the Division, Department, Shift, or Project information, as appropriate. (Note: If the client is set to
     ACH by Division, you must enter a Division code.)
•    Enter the Cost.
•    Enter a Comment that explains the invoicing of the event code.
  1. Click Save.

Note: If the client is set to ACH by Location or ACH by Division and has missing or incomplete banking information, an error message displays and will not allow you to save the invoice. (You must review the client’s ACH setup and make the appropriate updates.)

Importing Miscellaneous Invoices Data You can access the Miscellaneous Invoices import template in the Data Import Tool from this form to import

stand-alone, miscellaneous charges data by clicking Import . The Miscellaneous Invoices import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display.

Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Miscellaneous Invoices import template option. Note the following when importing Miscellaneous Invoices data: • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Miscellaneous Invoice form cannot import data using the Miscellaneous Invoices import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form. • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the Miscellaneous Invoice form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Miscellaneous Invoice form. • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Miscellaneous Invoice form can view the Miscellaneous Invoices import template for Miscellaneous Invoice, but cannot import data. • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data. • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company. • You can group the lines into one invoice if they are for the same client and date and are in consecutive lines in the file. However, if there are records for the same client and date that are not next to each other in the input file, the system does not group them in the same invoice because the program processes the lines one at a time.

Recalculating Workers Compensation for a Payroll

Recalculate Workers Compensation (WC) with the Recalculate Work Comp for Payroll form when changes have occurred to a client’s WC carrier, or when accrual rates were not updated before payroll was posted. This process recalculates WC accrual for a single payroll and updates payroll vouchers and employee WC registers. PrismHR includes a process to recalculate WC taxes in payroll vouchers. Taxable and tax amounts are recalculated, and other WC parameters on pay vouchers are updated, such as WC policy and rate. All the steps originally used to assign values for WC are employed when a voucher is initialized, but current settings are used. This provides a way to correct values that were set up incorrectly for WC when a payroll batch was originally posted. Registers do not need to be rebuilt after running this process, because they are automatically updated when the vouchers are processed. This process recalculates WC accrual (cost) values and does not impact billing. The rates in effect on the voucher pay date are used. This utility will not change employee information set up in Employee Details, but will only change WC cost numbers on reports run from Operations Management. This data will not flow through to the profit report.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To recalculate workers compensation for a payroll: 1. Click Payroll. 2. From Payroll|Action, select Recalculate Work Comp for Payroll. 3. Choose a payroll from Select a Payroll. 4. Click Recalculate. The system asks you to confirm this step. 5. Click Yes.

   Workers Compensation is then recalculated using the current values of these parameters:
       l   JOB.CODES (Job Master Classification)
       l   JOB.CODE.MASTER (Work Comp Class)
       l   EARNING.CODES (Factor, WC Taxable, Pay Class, Rate Class, Comp State)
       l   CLIENT.MASTER (W/C Policy, Work Location based W/C Clac?, Service Type)
       l   WC.RATES (Gross Rate)
       l   WC.POLICIES (Suppress G/L Accrual, Suppress Tria Premium, Rate Template)
       l   WC.MODS (Use override rates)
       l   STATE.CODES (W/C Wage Basis, W/C Wages Sheltered, Week ends on Day, Rate/Hundred)
       l   LOCATION.CODES (W/C Policy, Work Comp State)

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 236 Chapter 5 Other Processing

Identifying Gross Pay/Negative Hours Less Than Zero The Negative Pay Report, available from the Payroll|Report menu, allows you to generate a report that lists all employees whose gross pay is less than zero or have negative hours. (This might occur as an adjustment mechanism for the client.)

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 238 Chapter 5 Other Processing

To run this report, do the following: 1. Select Negative Pay Report in the Reports menu under Payroll|Report. 2. Enter or select the Payroll Number. 3. Click Run. During a short delay, the system builds the data. Processing Pay On-Demand Payments Using the Pay On-Demand feature, you can pay employees in real time without having to wait for an ACH transaction. This process uses pay cards to pay employees off-cycle for instant payment. The most common uses for this feature are: • Paying someone quickly for hours missed • Paying a terminated employee’s wages on the same day they are terminated To generate a file for processing payments, use the Pay On-Demand Processing, which is available on the Operations|Action menu. For example:

Note: Only service providers can run pay on-demand files to pay employees. However, worksite managers are also allowed to set up pay on-demand accounts and process pay on-demand payrolls.

Voiding Pay On-Demand Payments Employees who are paid using pay on-demand processing have an invoice amount that is debited on the ACH file. However, if you void the pay on-demand voucher, the invoice amount displays as a credit on the ACH file. Note the following: • If you run the pay on-demand process (that is, you generate a file) and then you complete a void, no changes occur in the history file. • If you do not generate a file and a void occurs, then the system does not include the voucher in the next file creation.

Panel Column Descriptions Employee Tax • Tax Deduct Code: Distinct system-generated tax code that identifies Federal, State, and Local tax withholding. • Tax Description: Description of the tax deduction code, which you can define and modify in the Tax Deductions form on the System|Change

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 258 Chapter 6 Inquiries

Panel Column Descriptions menu. When the system generates a new tax, you might want to modify the description. • Exempt Earnings: Any earnings that are considered exempt and excluded from taxable wages. Exempt earnings vary between Federal, State, and Local tax rules, which you can configure in PrismHR. • Sheltered Earnings: Earnings that are a portion of wages not subject to a specific tax. This might vary between Federal, State, and Local tax withholdings. Also, they can reflect multiple types of income deferral including contributions to retirement, section 125 deductions, and other various methods. Refer to your Federal, State, and Local tax laws to determine sheltered earnings for each tax deduction. • Taxable Earnings: Total wages that are considered taxable for the voucher (excluding Exempt and Sheltered earnings). • Taxable Over Limit: Taxable wage limits vary by tax deduction. This value reflects the amount of wages that are over the wage limit and therefore not taxable. • Tax Withheld: Calculated tax amount to be withheld from the employees’ wages based on the taxable wages that are not over the limit. • Tax Basis: Identifies whether the taxable wage type is reported on the Employer (P) or Client Level (C). You can define this setting on the State Rules form, which can be overridden in various ways. Note: There might be scenarios where an employee is paid with both cash and non-cash pay codes and there is not sufficient cash to cover the tax deductions in full, which are listed on the voucher as Uncollected Medicare | OASDI (see Uncollected Social Security and/or Medicare). Filing Status This panel reflects the employee’s tax filing information used to calculate the taxes for the voucher. The information included is listed below: • Tax Authority ID. • Tax Authority Name (Description). • Filing status. • Allowances (if any). • Override type (if any). • When an override is present, the Override amount indicates the value that determines the tax amount in the Employee Tax section of the voucher.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 259 Chapter 6 Inquiries

Panel Column Descriptions • Annual pay periods reflect the number of pay periods that calculate the taxable wages to determine the withheld tax.

Employer Tax This panel reflects the accrual tax values as outlined below. Note: Tax Deduction Code|Description|Exempt|Sheltered|Taxable|Taxable Over Limit remains the same as outlined in the Employee Tax panel, although the amounts might vary based on Federal, State, and Local tax laws. You will notice a difference in the tax deduction codes between employee and employer taxes as well. • Tax Accrued: Displays the tax liability amount accrued for the specific tax code. (Many tax rates are configurable in PrismHR.) • Tax Basis: Identifies whether the taxable wage type is reported on the Employer (P) or Client (C|CL) Level. You can define this setting on the State Rules form, but it can be overridden in various ways. When SUTA is reported on the worksite level, the tax basis report displays as CL. Otherwise, Client-reported taxes display as C. • Client Reporting Only: Certain states set SUTA rates on the PEO level, but the PEO is required to report on the Client level. When you select the Client SUTA Report Only option on the State Rules form, the Client Reporting only field on the Employer Tax panel displays Y.

Taxable Billing The Taxable Billing (w/ Shelters) and Taxable Billing (w/o Shelters) panels (with and without display the amounts billed to the client based on the current billing template Shelters) assigned to that client. The billing template allows flexibility in how you choose to bill your client on wages with sheltered earnings. (Refer to the PrismHR Billing User Guide for information on how to use the Billing Templates form to define methods for billing clients.) Taxable Billing (w/ Shelters): Reflects the billed amounts for each tax deduction when the billing template includes the Discount Shelter option. (Sheltered earnings are reduced from the taxable earnings to calculate the bill amount.) Taxable Billing (w/o Shelters): Reflects the billed amounts for each tax deduction when the billing template does not include the Discount Shelter option. Sheltered earnings do not display, and the taxable earnings include sheltered wages to calculate the bill amount.

Chapter 8 Troubleshooting These are procedures for dealing with uncommon payroll administration situations.

Understanding Payroll Error Messages 289 Time Sheet Errors 289 Calculation Errors 291 Posting Errors 304 Time Sheet Import Issues 305 Common Issues with FLSA Rulesets 309 FLSA Ruleset Not Applied to Any Employees 309 FLSA Ruleset for Tipped Employees Not Applied 310 Apply FLSA Ruleset to Employees Added by Time Sheet Import 311 FLSA Ruleset for Biweekly Payroll 311

Understanding Payroll Error Messages Error messages alert the users when PrismHR has insufficient or incorrect information to properly process a payroll batch. Resolve the issue to proceed; some issues might require that the user have specific permissions.

Time Sheet Errors These errors occur during time sheet entry and finalization steps of payroll processing. Refer to the appropriate procedure to resolve the issue.

Pay Method Not Setup THE CURRENT PAY METHOD HAS NOT BEEN SETUP IN THE PTO ABSENCE CODE FORM FOR THE [NNNN] ABSENCE CODE. IN THE LEAVE PROCESSING SECTION OF THE PTO ABSENCE FORM THE SECTIONS PAY METHOD AND LEAVE OFFSET PAY CODE MUST BE COMPLETED BEFORE PROCESSING CAN CONTINUE.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 289 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open PTO Absence Codes (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 3. Select the Absence Code. 4. Select Enable in ESS to allow employees to request paid time off for this absence code in Employee Portal (EP). Selecting this option enables the other fields, which control the behavior of the EP time off request feature, and also makes the absence code available to employees in EP. 5. For each pay method used by the client: • Enter the Pay Method, which is how the employee is paid. • Enter the Leave Offset Pay Code, which is the pay code that will be reduced by the number of hours of paid time off. For example, if it is set to REG, the system reduces the REG hours for the employee. 6. Click Save.

Pay Rate Change Not Approved YOU MUST FIRST CONFIRM THE PAY RATE CHANGE BY CLICKING ON THE CURRENT PAY RATE. THIS WILL DISPLAY THE PAY RATE ASSIGNMENT FORM WHICH WILL ALSO ALLOW YOU TO ASSIGN HOURS TO THE NEW PAY RATE IF REQUIRED. ONLY [NNNN] WERE ABLE TO BE UPDATED. PLEASE CHECK ANY ERROR DETAILED. THERE WERE [NNNN] EMPLOYEES THAT FAILED DUE TO A PAY RATE CHANGE ISSUE. THE EMPLOYEE IS [NNNNNN].

To resolve this error: 1. Click the red indicator in Summary Time Sheet Entry to open the New Pay Rate Assignment form. 2. Enter the Hours worked at the new rate (second row) and then press Tab. The Hours at the original rate (first row) adjust automatically so that the sum equals the Target Hours. 3. Click Accept. The system returns you to the Summary Time Sheet Entry form, and the indicator changes to green .

Outstanding PTO Leave Request EMPLOYEE [NNNNNN] HAS AN OUTSTANDING PTO LEAVE REQUEST THAT NEEDS TO BE COMPLETED. ONLY [NNNN] WERE ABLE TO BE UPDATED. PLEASE CHECK ANY ERRORS DETAILED.

To resolve this error: 1. Click the red indicator in Summary Time Sheet Entry to open the Leave Request Assignment. 2. Review the information in the form. • Enter the correct hours in the Leave to Time Sheet column. The system adjusts the hours for Reduce Pay Code and To Leave Pay Code. • (Optional) Enter any Notes.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 290 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Click Accept. The system returns you to the Summary Time Sheet Entry form and adjusts the employee’s hours. The indicator changes to green .

Open Employee Details (found in the HR menu under HR|Change). 3. Enter the Employee ID. 4. Select the Tax tab. 5. Review the information submitted by the employee, listed in the New Hire Tax Forms panel. 6. Set up the Local Tax Filings as required by your organization. 7. Select Handled for every item in the New Hire Tax Forms panel. 8. Click Save.

GeoCode Not Assigned GeoCode not assigned to {######}, {Employee Name}. Please go to the Employee Details and update the address information to provide a GeoCode. There is no GeoCode for the employee, so the system cannot calculate some of the taxes.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Employee Details (found in the HR menu under HR|Change). 3. Enter the Employee ID. 4. Select the Address tab. 5. Enter the address information, ensuring that the GeoCode populates. 6. If appropriate, enter the Override GeoCode. 7. Click Save.

Invalid Federal Filing Status Invalid Federal Filing Status for {nnnn}, {Employee Name}. Please go to the Employee Details and provide a Filing Status.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Employee Details (found in the HR menu under HR|Change). 3. Open the employee record specified in the error message. 4. Select the Tax tab.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 296 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Enter the correct information in the Federal Tax Filing panel (Federal Filing Status, Federal Allowances, and so on as required for the employee).
  2. Click Save.

State Filing Status Missing FILING STATUS MISSING, EMPLOYEE ID {######}, STATE {NN} The employee does not have a filing status for the state in which he or she works. Adjust the filing status for this employee.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Employee Details (found in the HR menu under HR|Change). 3. Enter the Employee ID. 4. Select the Tax tab. 5. Enter the correct information in the State Tax Filings panel (State, Filing Status, Allow., and so on as required for the employee). 6. Click Save.

Cannot Adjust Deductions CANNOT ADJUST DEDUCTIONS ON VOUCHER #{######} FOR {NNNN NNNN} The system cannot properly calculate the deduction amount for the employee’s voucher. Check the employee’s deductions to see if there is a deduction scheduled that exceeds the employee’s payment.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Recurring Deductions (found in the Payroll menu under Payroll|Change). 3. Enter the Employee ID. If there are any deductions scheduled and they are in excess of the amount the employee will receive, click Save. See Working with Recurring Deductions on page 17 for details. 4. Open Scheduled Deductions. If there are any deductions scheduled and they are in excess of the amount the employee will receive, click Save.

Cannot Determine Retirement Plan CANNOT DETERMINE RETIREMENT PLAN YEAR & PERIOD You might see this error message for the first payroll processed in the new year or for a new client. You or your system administrator must establish a plan year and period for your organization’s retirement plan.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 297 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

To resolve this error: 1. Open Retirement Plan Years (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the Plan ID. 3. Complete the other fields as needed. See the “Retirement Plan Years” topic for descriptions of those fields. 4. Click Save.

Retirement Plan Match Rules Not Set Up RETIREMENT PLAN MATCH RULES NOT SETUP FOR PLAN {NNNN} The retirement plan match rules are not set up for the indicated plan.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Retirement Match Rules (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 3. Enter the Benefit Group ID. 4. Select the Retirement Plan. 5. Select the Effective Date. 6. Complete the other fields correctly. See “Retirement Match Rules” in the Benefits Administration User Guide for descriptions of the fields. 7. Click Save.

Cannot Read FLSA Ruleset CANNOT READ FLSA RULESET {nnn} The FLSA ruleset specified in the error message is defined for the client but does not exist.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Client Details and select the Payroll tab. 3. Enter a valid FLSA Ruleset ID; click the field to use the search and find the ID.

Note: If the FLSA ruleset that you require for the client does not exist, create it using the FLSA Ruleset form and then specify the ID as described above.

  1. Click Save.

Invalid Work Week Ending Day INVALID WORK WEEK ENDING DAY FOUND ON CLIENT MASTER

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 298 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

This error message displays if the client has an FLSA ruleset defined in Client Details but no corresponding day.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Client Details and select the Payroll tab. 3. Select the FLSA Work Week Ends On day. 4. Click Save.

W/C Rates Cross-Reference Not Found {Employee Name} WC.RATES.XREF RECORD {rate template ID}.{state code}.{wc code} NOT FOUND

There is no workers’ compensation rate defined for this employee’s position classification on the rate template associated with the client’s policy.

Note: If the rate template ID was not included in the error message, you can find the client’s policy in the Client Details > Benefits tab. You can find the rate template for that policy in W/C Policies.

To resolve this error: 1. Open W/C Classification Rates (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Select the Rate Template. 3. Select the State. 4. Enter the Class Code. 5. Enter the Effective Date. (The effective date must precede the pay date.) 6. Enter the Gross Rate, which is the workers’ compensation insurance premium’s gross rate as a percentage; for example, enter 1 for $1.00 per $100 wages. 7. Complete the other fields as required. 8. Click Save.

Note: The following section only applies to On-Prem customers who are still using HRPyramid. If this does not solve the problem, check the W/C policy information in the Client Details Benefits tab. If the Use Rate Templates option is not selected and your organization is set to Use Legacy W/C Rate Tables in the System Parameters, then you need to set the rates in the backend system for PrismHR. 1. In the backend system (HRPyramid), select System Administration > File > W/Comp Setup Menu (Traditional) > W/C Classification Rates. 2. Enter the State postal code. 3. Enter the Class Code. 4. Enter the Effective Date.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 299 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Enter the Class Description if it did not populate based on the class code you entered.
  2. Enter the Gross Rate.
  3. If necessary, click F5-Rate Override and then enter any overrides for the policy. Click F2-Accept when finished.
  4. If necessary, click F6-Other and enter the other information. Click F2-Accept when finished.
  5. Click F2-Save.

W/C Billing Modifier Cross-Reference Not Found {employee name} W/C BILLING MODIFIER X-REF RECORD NOT FOUND FOR CLIENT IN STATE {NN} There is no workers’ compensation modifier cross-reference record file available for the client in the state mentioned in the error message.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open the W/C Billing Modifiers form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 3. Enter the two-character State Code. 4. Enter the Effective Date or select the existing date. This must be before the pay date and not have a date later than it. 5. Enter other information as required. 6. Click Save.

No Valid Workers’ Comp Codes Match {EMPLOYEE NAME} None of the valid Workers Comp Codes listed for Client were found to match code {NN}.####. Please either select another Job Code/WC Code or Update the Valid W/C Classes list. There are valid workers’ compensation codes set at the client level and the code shown in the error is not in the list. (Authorized W/C classes are an optional setting and typically used only when the client has a policy that excludes certain codes.)

To add the missing code needs to the list of authorized W/C classes: 1. Open Client Details (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 2. Open the Actions menu and then select W/C Classes. The Authorized W/C Classes form opens. 3. Enter the W/C Code from the error message.

Employer-Based W/C Modifier Cross-Reference Not Found {Employee Name} Employer Based W/C Modifier XRef not found for company (##) for Employer (##) state (NN). To correct this error, go to Employer/Change/Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers. If this State/Company should NOT use Employer-Based accruals, either the W/C Policy is defined incorrectly or the wrong W/C Policy is on the Company Master

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 300 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

There is no workers’ compensation modifier cross-reference record file available for the employer and state mentioned in the error message.

To resolve this error: 1. Open Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers (found in the Back Office menu under Employer|Change). 2. Enter the Employer ID. 3. Enter the State code, or select it from the drop-down. The drop-down lists states with defined rates at the top. 4. Enter the Effective Date, or select an existing date. 5. Enter the Discount/Debit. 6. Enter the Modifier. The system calculates the Effective Rate. 7. Enter any policy overrides, if appropriate. See “Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers” in the Employer Administration User Guide for information on the fields. 8. Click Save.

Cannot Find W/C Class {EMPLOYEE NAME} The W/C Class for Position Classification [wc code] for the state of {NN} and employee [employee ID] cannot be found. Check the Time Sheet and Employee Details to ensure the correct Position is assigned to the employee, and correct it in both places if it is incorrect. If the Position assigned to the employee is correct, the state and W/C Class code are most likely missing or incorrect on the Position Classification assigned to the employee’s Position, which can be updated at System | Change | Position Classification. or {EMPLOYEE NAME} The W/C CLASS for Position Classification [wc code] in the state of {NN} cannot be found. Position = [position ID] Voucher# [######] This employee’s position classification does not have a workers’ compensation classification for this state.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure that the position code and W/C Class in Employee Details and the Time Sheet match. 2. If that does not solve the problem, open Position Classifications (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 3. Enter the Position Classification. 4. In the table, click + to add a new row. 5. Enter the State code. 6. Enter the W/C Class Code.

Note: If the system displays a message such as “Record {NN.####} is not on file WC.CLASS.CODES”, you need to enter the W/C classification for that state.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 301 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Click Save.

Comp Code Does Not Have Rate on Template Client ### Employee: ### Voucher ### Error: The Comp Code NN.#### does not have a rate on the bundled sheet NNNN. Processing cannot continue. The processing for this employee will stop. The bundled billing template assigned to the client uses default rates and does not have a rate for the W/C code specified in the error message. You need to enter a rate for that code, or a default rate.

Note: If the Default Rate is greater than zero, the system uses it for any Workers’ Compensation code not listed in the table. If there is a value in this field and no value in the W/C Code field, there may be billing errors; use the Default Rate with care. If you leave the Default Rate blank, users entering data for clients with this billing template see messages that the listed Workers’ Compensation code does not have a billing amount. The system continues to display this message until you update the bill template for the code or enter a default amount.

To resolve this error: 1. Open Billing Templates (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the Template ID indicated in the error message. 3. Go to the Bundled Rate Maintenance panel and do one of the following: Enter the rate information for the W/C Code from the error message: • Enter the W/C Code. • Enter the Min Admin Fee amount to use. This overrides any amount entered on the client record, except for special rates. The system discounts the minimum fee by the special discount rate. • Enter the WC Def Bill Rate, which is the default billing rate for the W/C Code. Enter the Default Rate to apply to all W/C codes not defined in the table. This is useful for “one-price-fits- all” clients. Please read the note above before using the Default Rate field. 4. In the Coverage Details panel, enter the correct Existing Effective Date. 5. Click Save.

G/L Accounting Not Set Up The G/L Accounting has not been setup for {item} {###} on G/L Template “{nnnn}” Voucher: ###.###. Cannot assign accounting. The G/L account information has not been set up in the G/L template for the specified item.

To resolve this error: 1. Open G/L Setup Maintenance (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the G/L Template code. 3. Select the G/L Type where the information is missing. 4. Enter the G/L account information for the item mentioned in the error message.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 302 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Click Save.

Related Topic “G/L Setup Maintenance” in the PrismHR Accounting User Guide

Account Not Valid in G/L Chart Account NNN.####-###-### is not valid in GL.NNN file. Unable to open GL.ERRORS file. Error will ONLY DISPLAY This error occurs if your organization is not using the G/L auto-build feature and the account number is not currently in G/L Chart of Account Maintenance. Your organization can either add the account to the G/L chart or enable the auto-build feature.

To add the account to the G/L chart: 1. Open G/L Chart of Account Maintenance (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the Account Number from the first line of the error message . 3. (Optional) Enter an Account Description. 4. Click Save.

To enable the G/L auto-build feature: 1. Open System Parameters (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Go to the Global Accounting panel at the bottom. 3. From the Accounting Interface Type drop-down, select the appropriate accounting system that includes “Build Account #s”. 4. Click Save.

Related Topics “G/L Chart of Account Maintenance” in the PrismHR Accounting User Guide “Global Accounting” in the PrismHR System Administration Guide

No Valid Billing Template Client {NNNN} Employee: Voucher: ERROR: NO VALID BILLING TEMPLATE ON CLIENT MASTER The billing template has not been designated for the client. You or your system administrator needs to define it.

To resolve this error: 1. Make sure the correct client record is shown near the top of the page. If not, click on it and then select the correct client. 2. Open Client Details (found in the Client menu under Client|Change).

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 303 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Select the Billing tab.
  2. Enter the Billing Template ID.

Note: Make sure that the Billing Template has rates that apply to the client. If not, you cannot calculate a payroll for the client until you add the appropriate rates to the template: see “Billing Templates” in the Billing User Guide.

  1. Click Save.

Debit Account Not Found DEBIT ACCOUNT NOT FOUND FOR BENEFIT PLAN ID {NNNN} There is no debit account defined for this benefit plan. To apply it to the record, you or a benefits administrator must update the benefit plan.

To resolve this error: 1. Open Group Benefit Plans (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the Benefit Plan ID. 3. In the Corporate Account panel, enter the Debit Account. 4. Click Save.

Posting Errors These errors occur during the posting (finalization) step of payroll processing. Refer to the appropriate procedure to resolve the issue.

Third Party Checking Account Not Set Up Third Party Checking Account {####} - Account owner name and address not setup! The account shown in the error message does not have a name and address defined in the Print Parameters panel of the Bank Accounts record. The information is required for third party check printing, which is turned on.

To resolve this error: 1. Open Bank Accounts (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the Account ID from the error message. 3. In the Print Parameters panel, enter the Bank Account Name, Bank Account Address, and City, State & ZIP Code. 4. Click Save.

Client Status Does Not Allow Finalizing a Payroll Client status does not allow for finalizing a payroll.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 304 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

The client’s status is currently of a class Pending, Inactive, or Client Cancelling (Pre-Termination). The system requires that the class of the status be Active to finalize the payroll. After determining that this is the appropriate action to take, a user must set the client status back to one that indicates they are Active to post the payroll.

To resolve this error: 1. Open Client Status Change (found in the Client menu under Client|Action). 2. From the New Status drop-down, select a status that indicates the client is Active. 3. Enter the Effective Date for the change in status. 4. Click Save.

Batch Not Yet Initialized Batch has not yet been initialized. An error occurred between initialization and finalization that prevented finalization from completing, although in Process Payroll it looks like the user should be able to click the Finalize icon . Re-initialize the payroll and then proceed as normal. Please note that this error displays only in Process Payroll. It does not display in SuperBatch.

Time Sheet Import Issues These are common issues related to time sheet imports. Refer to the appropriate procedure to resolve your problem.

Related Topic Apply FLSA Ruleset to Employees Added by Time Sheet Import (page 311)

Time Sheet Import Has No Records If you process an import and it seems to complete successfully but there are zero errors and no details, there is probably an issue with the file type in the Payroll Import Definition.

To resolve this error: 1. Open Payroll Import Definition (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Make sure the file type of your import file matches the import definition file type.

For example, if the definition specifies a tab-delimited text file (TXT) and your file is a comma-separated value file (CSV), then the system could not import data because the format is wrong.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 305 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

Amount Did Not Import Examples of scenarios where you might have an amount that does not import are: • All data imports except for expense amounts • One pay code will not import • Some amounts import and others do not, even with the same pay code You might see an error that reads, “No hours for employee N#####, paycode NNNN on line #.” Typically this is caused when the file includes $ or , in the amount fields. In the example below, the Bonus amounts will not import because they each include one or both of those characters. The Regular pay will import correctly. Tab-Delimited File with $ or , in the Amounts

Edit the import file to remove any dollar signs or commas, save the file, and re-import it. All of the amounts shown below will import correctly. Tab-Delimited File with Correctly Formatted Amounts

Cannot Find Data Import File “Cannot find the data file nnnnn. The data import failed” It is likely that there is a space in the file name. The system cannot read the file if its name includes a space. To resolve this error, remove the space from the file name and then re-import the file.

Pay Code Will Not Import There are a couple reasons why the pay code might not import. Use one of the following procedures to resolve the issue.

Pay Code Field Is Not Mapped If the import file has a pay code that does not exist in PrismHR, you might see an error message such as: “Earning code nnnn on line # is invalid.”

To resolve this error:

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 306 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Open Pay Import Definition (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change).

  2. Enter the Definition ID for the used for the file.

  3. Map the pay code in the Import Translation Table panel: • In the Foreign Code field, enter the pay code as it is written in the file; for example, Expense. • In the HRP Code field, enter the matching pay code in PrismHR; for example, EXPS. • If appropriate, indicate whether the pay code represents paid time off using the PTO Type Flag drop- down.

  4. Click Save.

Mixed Mapping There is a conflict between the mapping methods in the file and import definition. There are three basic methods for importing: • Mapping • Matching • Matching for more than 10 codes Mapping This method works directly with your file and the import definition. You match the column numbers directly to fields. Mapping Columns to Fields

Matching This method not only looks at your file and uses the import definition, but it also needs to look at the Client Details to know what to match for pay codes.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 307 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

For example, if your import file looks like the one shown below: Matching File Example

The Import Field Definitions match the values in columns 4, 5, and 6 to the values from the Client Details Time Sheet tab for Pay Code 1, Pay Code 2, and Pay Code 6. Matching Import Definition Example

Matching for more than 10 Codes This method is an extension of the basic matching example above. It uses the matching example for what is available on the Client Details Time Sheet tab, and then uses the translation table to import an eleventh code. For example, if your import file looks like the one below: Matching File Example for more than 10 codes

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 308 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

The Import Field Definitions match the values in columns 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 to the values from the Client Details Time Sheet tab for Pay Code 1, Pay Code 2, Pay Code 6, Pay Code 7, and Pay Code 8. It then assigns matches the value in column 9 to the pay code specified in the Import Translation Table. Matching Import Definition Example for more than 10 codes

Common Issues with FLSA Rulesets There are some issues with FLSA Rulesets that users sometimes encounter.

FLSA Ruleset Not Applied to Any Employees 309 Define Ruleset for Client 309 Check Position for FLSA Exempt 310 FLSA Ruleset for Tipped Employees Not Applied 310 Apply FLSA Ruleset to Employees Added by Time Sheet Import 311 FLSA Ruleset for Biweekly Payroll 311

FLSA Ruleset Not Applied to Any Employees There are a couple of reasons why the FLSA ruleset would not be applied to employees: the FLSA ruleset is not set up on the client, or the positions assigned to the employees are marked as FLSA exempt.

Define Ruleset for Client 1. Open Client Details (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 2. Select the Payroll tab. 3. Enter the FLSA Ruleset that applies to the client.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 309 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Click Save.

Check Position for FLSA Exempt 1. Open the Positions form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 2. Enter the Position Code for the employees who are not having the FLSA ruleset applied. 3. Look at the FLSA Exempt option.

  1. If the position should not be FLSA exempt, you need to enter a Position Classification that is not flagged as FLSA exempt; “Positions” and “Position Classifications” in the Human Resources User Guide.

FLSA Ruleset for Tipped Employees Not Applied The system only applies a FLSA Ruleset for tipped employees if the position is set as a tipped position.

To make sure the position is marked as tipped: 1. Open the Positions form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 2. Enter the Position Code for the employees who are not having the FLSA ruleset applied. 3. Make sure that the Tipped Position option is selected.

Payroll Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 310 Chapter 8 Troubleshooting

  1. Click Save.

Apply FLSA Ruleset to Employees Added by Time Sheet Import If you import a time sheet, the FLSA ruleset is not applied to the employees’ hours until the payroll is calculated (initialized).

FLSA Ruleset for Biweekly Payroll If you have a biweekly payroll, then applying the FLSA ruleset requires that you enter the hours in a specific way: • If the FLSA ruleset calculates on the hours worked in a week, then you need to enter the hours for each week in the pay cycle separately. • If the FLSA ruleset uses a daily calculation, then you need to enter hours in the timesheet by the day that it was worked.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Payroll Processing Guidelines

Chapter 1 Payroll Processing Guidelines PrismHR offers unique workflow management systems for processing payroll, designed to expedite the payroll process.

Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls You can use the Payroll Control form to establish essential information for processing payroll in PrismHR. There are three types of payrolls that users can process: regularly scheduled, manual, and special/unscheduled batches. You determine the payroll type using the Payroll Type field. PrismHR uses the parameters defined in the Payroll Control form to automatically schedule the next batch. • Regularly Scheduled: Following the successful completion of a payroll, PrismHR automatically creates a new Payroll Control record for the next regularly scheduled payroll. The regularly scheduled payroll includes time sheets for each employee scheduled to be paid in the payroll. Payroll processors can add or delete time sheets as necessary.

Note: When deleting a payroll, Full access users have the option of copying saved entries, which can be applied to a new payroll without having to re-import or re-enter the data. After clicking Yes in the first two confirmation dialogs that display when you click Delete in the Payroll Control form, a third confirmation dialog displays, “Do you want to keep the keyed entries and apply them to the new payroll?” Click Yes to copy all saved entries and charge dates (including entries in the deduction columns) into a new payroll batch. Clicking No produces a blank timesheet. (Previously accepted Pay Rates and Leave Requests remain unchanged.)

In addition, if you try to delete a payroll where a reverse wire transfer journal exists an error displays, “Payroll can not be deleted as the ACH journals have already been created.” • Special/Unscheduled: Enter a payroll for specific pay groups. • Manual: Enter a supplemental or unscheduled payroll for one or more employees.

Note: You can also use the form to view in progress or past payrolls. However, you cannot edit posted payrolls, and you cannot create regularly scheduled payrolls.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 Payroll Processing Guidelines

Identifying the Payroll and Type You can identify the payroll and type in the Payroll Control panel. This panel also displays the current status. For example:

To identify the payroll and type: 1. If necessary, select the Calendar Year in which the payroll batch occurs. The default is the current year. 2. Select an existing payroll or create a new one: • Click New Payroll to create the new payroll. The system automatically generates a payroll number. • Click Payroll Number and then select the payroll you want to edit. The Payroll Control form populates with the information for that payroll. If the payroll is not finalized, you can make edits as needed. 3. The Payroll Type indicates the type of payroll. • If you are creating a new payroll, select either Manual or Special. • If you are editing an existing payroll, you cannot change the type. 4. If you select Manual as the Payroll Type, select the Reason, so you can track the reason why the client is processing manual payrolls. (This field only displays if you select Manual as the Payroll Type.) Note: The Reason field is required if the Require Manual Payroll Reason field on the System Parameters form is enabled. 5. If appropriate, enter a Description that identifies this payroll. Note the following: • When administering payrolls, you cannot enter or select any International Employees (set on the Address tab in the Employee Details form, see Establishing and Maintaining Employee Address Information) in the Employee panel. • For completed regular payrolls, you can click View Timesheet to see the time sheet information. (This link is not available for incomplete payrolls.) • For payrolls in the Wire Transfer Pending status, you can click the Reset Wire Transfer link to set the payroll back to Payroll Pending Review status. See Processing Payroll: Wire Transfer Pending Status on page 68. • Select the Pay Group link in the Related Actions section to access the Pay Groups form, where you can set up a group of employees who are all paid on the same day.

Identifying Payroll Processing Information You can identify the payroll processor and establish the payroll date and time information in the Payroll Processor panel. For example:

  1. If available, enter the user ID of the Payroll Processor for this payroll. The system defaults to the processor specified in the Account tab of Client Details.
  2. Enter the Pay Date on which to process the payroll. The Quarter End Date, Year End Date, and G/L Period for the payroll display. Note: When you set a manual payroll to Pay On-Demand on the Payroll Options form and configure that payroll on the Payroll Control form, the system automatically sets the Pay Date to the current date since the employee will be paid today (instant payment). The following happens: • If you try to change that automated Pay Date the system displays a warning, “This is a Pay On-Demand payroll so the Pay Date must be the current date.” (Click OK to continue.) • If you enter or select a Pay Date that is not the current date and then select the Pay On-Demand field on the Payroll Options form the system displays a warning, “Pay On-Demand payroll must be paid using the current date. By selecting this option the pay date is updated to today.” (Click OK to continue.) After you click Accept and return to the Payroll Control form, the system automatically changes the Pay Date to the current date.
  3. Enter the Remote Cutoff Date by which the client must report time data. Note: The Remote Cutoff Date and Remote Cutoff Time fields only apply if the client enters their own time sheets; this is indicated on the Client Details Control tab.
  4. Enter the Remote Cutoff Time.
  5. Enter the Delivery Date on which the payroll checks should be delivered.
  6. If you are entering a Manual payroll, you can select the Override Pay Period to use as an alternate period to the one defined for the pay group.

Cloning Previous Payrolls You can clone a previous payroll using the Clone Last Batch form, accessed from the Payroll Control Actions menu. 1. Click New Payroll in Payroll Control. 2. Open the Actions menu and select Clone Last Batch. The Clone Last Batch form opens.
