Setting Special Processing Options You can set special processing options as needed for all employees included in the payroll batch using the Payroll Options form. To access the options, open a payroll in the Payroll Control form and then select Options from the Actions menu. For example:

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 1 Payroll Processing Guidelines

To set special processing options: 1. Select ACH in the Suppress ACH field to prevent the generation of direct deposit transactions. (Employees normally paid by direct deposit will receive paper checks instead.) For example, you might select this option when the client wants to deliver live checks for year-end bonuses. Note the following: • This field applies only to employee ACH processing. It does not suppress electronic billing. • If you select Suppress ACH with Pay On-Demand selected, an error message displays stating that they cannot be enabled for the same payroll. • If you create a manual payroll with Pay On-Demand selected and then apply a Payroll Option Template with Suppress ACH selected within a timesheet, an error message displays stating that they cannot be enabled for the same payroll and the system does not apply the Payroll Option Template.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 17 Chapter 1 Payroll Processing Guidelines

  1. Select the ACH Earn Type Limiter to specify the voucher types that will be processed as ACH transactions. Voucher types that you do not specify will be processed as paper checks. This overrides the settings defined in the Employee Details Deposit tab. • Blank: All checks (regular, vacation, and supplemental) • R: Only regular checks • V: Only vacation checks • S: Only supplemental checks • RV: Only regular and vacation checks • RS: Only regular and supplemental checks • VS: Only vacation and supplemental checks
  2. Select Suppress Other Earnings from the Suppress Earnings drop-down to prevent payment for other earnings.
  3. From the Suppress Deductions drop-down, select what payroll deductions (other than payroll taxes) to suppress for this payroll batch, if any. For example, you might need to suppress retirement deductions from bonus pay if employees opt not to have it deducted. Note the following: • When you run a supplemental batch, the system ignores voluntary deductions. • The system sends benefit deductions to arrears.
  4. Select Suppress Arrears to prevent the deduction of any amounts in arrears.
  5. Select Suppress Garnishments to prevent garnishment deductions.
  6. Select Suppress Benefits Calculation to suppress withholding of any benefits deductions and benefit accruals/arrears calculations. If you suppress benefits for this payroll batch, the system does not calculate benefits for the pay period, and therefore no benefit deductions go to arrears.
  7. Select Suppress Benefits Update to suppress the benefit update step that updates benefit-related deduction amounts on employee standard deduction records. The system normally updates the benefits on the employees’ standard deduction schedules according to the parameters set at the system level. For example, if you change the amount of the employees’ contributions on the Group Benefit Plan, the system updates the employees’ standard deduction schedule to reflect the change. Use the Suppress Benefits Update option to suppress that update.
  8. Select Suppress Benefit Adjustments to suppress the processing of benefits adjustments.
  9. Select Suppress Client Approval to except the payroll batch from the approval process. The payroll batch processes as if the client company does not use approvals.
  10. Select Suppress Client Bill Pending to suppress client bill pending for this batch.
  11. Select Suppress Loan Payment to suppress the loan payment from calculating and processing in the current payroll.
  12. Select Suppress Manual Checks to prevent a manual check from processing in the next regularly scheduled payroll and instead process it through a separate, special batch. (Note: This functionality is available for Scheduled and Special batches, but does not apply to Manual batches.)

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 Payroll Processing Guidelines

  1. Enable Force Time Off Accruals to override standard time off accrual functionality for payrolls that are not yet initialized and are set to the Manual or Special/Unscheduled payroll type on the Payroll Control form. Note: Enabling Force Time Off Accruals allows you to select specific time off plans for forced accrual in the Time Off Plans panel.
  2. Select Suppress Payday Notifications to suppress payday notifications at the batch level for regularly scheduled payrolls.
  3. Select Delivery Method Override to enter or select a delivery method in the Select a Delivery Method dialog box that displays. This will display on the payroll’s delivery sheet and delivery fee after payroll completes. Additionally, the system considers the Delivery Method Override field as a true override for the entire batch and when the override is set, no other delivery fees are applied.
  4. Select Delivery Message Override to enter a message in the Special Message field that will display on the payroll’s delivery sheet after payroll completes.
  5. Enter the Federal Tax Rate - Supplemental Pay, which is the rate to use as the federal tax percentage rate for all supplemental pay. This overrides the aggregate method.
  6. You can override the state tax percentage rate for all states, or for specific states. • All states: In the field, enter the State Tax Rate - Supplemental Pay, which is the rate to use for all supplemental pay. This overrides the rate for all states. • Specific states: In the table, enter the two-character State Code for each state that should use an override state tax rate, as well as the Supplemental Rate to use for each state.
  7. For a manual or special/unscheduled batch, enter the FSA Override Calculation Date that the system should use as the scheduled pay date for FSA calculations.
  8. Select FSA Reimbursement Batch to specify that this is a standalone payroll batch used only to process FSA reimbursements (must be defined in System Parameters).
  9. Enter or select the Benefit Calculation Date to override the actual pay date as the basis for benefit calculations that use an as of date.
  10. Select Force Retirement to Zero to set all retirement deductions to zero for the employees included in the payroll batch.
  11. Use the Show Future Dated Checks On ESS drop-down to indicate whether employees can view paychecks in the payroll that have future dates in Employee Self Service or Employee Portal (EP). This overrides the global setting. • Yes: Checks in this payroll batch with dates in the future display. • No or Select: Future checks do not display.
  12. Select Recalculate Overtime if the payroll batch should recalculate overtime rates. This option is available only for new payrolls. Note: Enabling or disabling the Recalculate Overtime field in this form automatically sets the same status in the Recalculate Overtime field on the Batch Payments form.
  13. Select Replaces A Scheduled Batch to run this as an unscheduled payroll batch in place of a regular one.

You must select this option when you first create the payroll; the system applies the default hours when it creates the new time sheets. If you save the payroll without selecting this option, and then select it later, the employees’ hours remain zero.

  3. Click Accept. You return to the Payroll Control form.

Adding Employees to a Payroll Use the Add Employees to Payroll form to add employees to the payroll batch. You can only add employees that do not already belong to any of the pay groups scheduled in the payroll; for example, if you want to process a check for an employee in the current batch who belongs to a different pay group. The forms also filters out any employees whose hire date is after the end of the pay period. Note: Select Quick Load to open the Regular Payroll Control Quick Load form, where you can add multiple employees to a pay group at once. (See Using Regular Payroll Control Quick Load.) When you add an employee, you must specify the pay group to associate with the employee for the payroll batch. PrismHR uses the pay group to assign the period start date, period end date, deduction period, period number, and optional alternate pay period to the employee.

To add employees to a payroll: 1. Click the Actions menu in the Payroll Control form and then select Add Employees to Payroll.

When to Use This Feature Some clients with multiple locations, with pay groups defined for each location, have employees who work for more than one location during the pay period. For example, during the current pay period, Mark works twenty hours at the Main Street location and twenty hours at the South Street location. The system associates an employee with one primary pay group, and Mark is assigned to the Main Street pay group. • Without this feature, Mark would need to be paid for twenty hours within his normally scheduled batch. • If you use this feature, you can associate Mark with South Street’s pay group for the purpose of paying him the hours worked at their location.

Benefit and Deduction Considerations When you add an employee to a batch, the employee’s payroll voucher is treated as a supplemental pay voucher for deductions calculations, regardless of the type of pay found on the voucher. As such, standard deductions are not deducted. However, deductions that normally would be taken from a supplemental pay voucher—a retirement plan, garnishment, or deduction in arrears—will be deducted. In the example, Mark’s standard benefit deductions would be taken on the payroll voucher paid in his regular pay group batch. If the pay is not sufficient to cover all scheduled benefit deductions, the balance goes into arrears. When the remaining twenty hours are paid in the batch to which Mark was added, PrismHR takes the deduction amounts in arrears on that paycheck.

Processing History The Processing History displays all processes performed on the payroll batch, if the payroll processor has run any. It shows each Processing Step, as well as the Date, Time, and User ID, and denial Details for each step.

Note: All dates and times in PrismHR are Central Time.

Panel Description • If a user’s role is set to Inquiry for the forms available as quick links, that user can click these links but is unable to make updates in the forms. • If a user’s role is set to Deny for the forms available as quick links, these links do not display.

Processing Steps Guides you through the payroll process by displaying which parts of the process are complete. (Click the icon next to an uncompleted step to proceed.) After you click an icon, the associated form or processing dialog displays where you can update or view information to complete the step. For example, when you click the Time Sheet icon ( ) the Time Sheet Entry form displays, where you can finalize this step. (Note: Click Return to return to the Process Payroll form.) After you successfully complete a step and return to the Process Payroll form, the system dims the step and displays “Complete.” The system highlights the next step, so you can continue the process. In addition, if there are any pending approvals for the payroll you can select Pending Actions to view pending approvals for you, pending approvals for others, and pending backdated leave requests. (Backdated leave requests are those whose dates occur before the current timesheet’s pay period start date.) Note: The system uses Restartable Payroll as the default payroll process, which replaced the Legacy Payroll process. The Restartable Payroll process picks up the calculation process when the last successful employee is calculated. (The Legacy Payroll process is still available, if you need to resolve payroll issues. However, if you need to use the Legacy Payroll process, you must enable the LEGACY-PAYROLL-GLOBAL custom feature code on the System Parameters form.) In addition, when processing payrolls where the Maximum ACH Amount is set on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the Restartable Payroll and Legacy Payroll features prevent submitted payrolls (those whose status is set to INITPEND), that exceed a set ACH amount, from processing until they are approved by a Billing Representative. These submitted payrolls are those where the payroll processor clicks Yes when the “You cannot make any changes once you submit payroll for processing. Are you sure you want to submit?” message displays. (Note that this message does not display when payrolls are submitted in SuperBatch.) Payroll Overview Displays multiple views and filtering options to filter the employee table, which provides a high-level view of the selected payroll. To complement the data tables, charts display to help visualize the data. You can filter both the

In addition, you can search for employees and select an option on the Actions menu to update employee records directly from this panel. Note: Each time you select a different filter, the system refreshes the information that displays in the chart and the employee table. Use the following options to filter information in the Payroll Overview panel: • View: Select the view to display in the first menu. For example, select Employees in Payroll (default) to view the employees in the selected payroll. Selecting Payroll Summary displays the employee vouchers associated with the selected payroll. Note: You can only use Employee search to search for information that displays in the table. • Categories: In the second menu, select the category to display (default is Status/Type for Employees in Payroll and Check/Deposit for Payroll Summary). For example, select Locations for the Employees in Payroll category to filter employees by their locations. • Filter: In the third menu, All (default) displays all the items that pertain to the selected category. For example, if you select Locations in the category menu and All as the filter, all the employee locations display. Note: The Variable Salary filter option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. • Review: Select the review type, which opens the associated form. For example, if you select Payroll Vouchers, the Payroll Summary form opens for the selected payroll. • Charts: Select a bar in the chart to display the employees in the table below that pertain to that category. (The system dims the other bars.) To remove a bar from the chart display, select that bar in the legend. (The system dims it in the legend.) To redisplay it, simply click the dimmed item in the legend. (Note: Selecting items in the legend only affects the display in the chart and does not affect the table data.) • Employee search box: To perform a search, enter the employee name or ID, then press Enter or Tab, or click the search icon ( ). The results display in the table below the search box, including the employee name and ID, status/type, and pay group. Note: If you select Payroll Summary in the first View drop-down menu and then perform a search, the system updates the totals count and gross pay in the results.

Errors and Warnings Displays errors and warnings, which helps you address issues that prevent payroll processing from completing. Click the download icon ( ) to download these messages to a .CSV file. For example, a warning message displays when calculating payroll if an employee has a gross pay greater than zero but has zero net pay, “Warning: Employee Voucher has gross pay with zero net pay.” Note the following: • All errors and warnings that occur during and after payroll process calculation display the employee’s last name, preferred name instead of their last name, first name, if applicable. (If the employee does not have a preferred name, then their last name, first name displays.) • You cannot process a payroll that contains a deidentified employee. An error message displays, “Employee: can not be paid as they are de-identified.” Remove the deidentified employee and process the payroll again.

Processing a Payroll The steps involved in processing a payroll are: 1. Entering Time Sheets (page 123) (see the section after the SuperBatch topics) 2. Calculating Payroll Vouchers (page 35) 3. Reviewing Payroll Reports (page 64) 4. Finalizing the Payroll (page 66) 5. Generating Payroll Reports (page 68)

Payroll Calculation Logic The payroll calculation process includes the gross wages and calculates the employee contribution based on the Benefit Rules and value assigned to the Benefit Plan for Gross % of Wages. On the Benefit Rules form, if a benefit plan uses the Percent of Gross Wages value, then while calculating the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium, if Max Contribution has been defined for any Benefit Rule, then it will ignore the Max Contribution value. You must also set The Contribution rule amounts made by Company or Employee field to Employee for the payroll process to include gross wages. The logic to determine the Percent of Gross Wages being used is as follows: • If the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form uses the Percent of Gross Wages value, then: • the value in the Percent of Gross Wages field on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form will be used to calculate the Percent of Gross Wages or else it will use the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form to calculate Percent of Gross Wages. • If the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form does not use the Percent of Gross Wages value, then: • the value in the Percent of Gross Wages field on the Benefit Rules form will be used to calculate the Percent of Gross Wages or else it will use the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form to calculate Percent of Gross Wages. The payroll calculation is as below: • Once the Percent of Gross Wages value has been determined, this value is used to calculate the Contribution Amount for the Employee portion of the premium. • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is not being considered, then the Contribution Amount is calculated for the Employee portion of the premium based on the Benefit Rule grid. • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is less than the Calculated Contribution from the Benefit Rule grid, then the Percent of Gross Wages is used as the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium. The dependent premium is calculated in full by the benefit rule. • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is greater than the Calculated Contribution from the Benefit Rule grid, then the Calculated Contribution is used from the Benefit Rule grid as the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium.

Calculating Payroll Vouchers To begin the payroll calculation process, click the Calculate icon ( ) for the payroll. (Note: The time sheet entry must be complete to enable payroll calculation.)

Note: The Security Notification dialog displays if you have made changes to sensitive employee information prior to calculating payroll.

During the payroll calculation process, PrismHR creates a payroll voucher for each employee to be paid in the current payroll as follows: • Calculates full gross-to-net earnings • Posts any other earnings combined with selected time sheet earnings to one of up to twelve payroll vouchers that could be created for an individual employee • Calculates and processes scheduled deductions • Calculates and takes payroll taxes • Processes any active tax calculation overrides or deduction overrides

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 35 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

•    Creates billing vouchers
•    Calculates accounting
•    Calculates benefits and benefit deductions
•    Accrues paid time off registers, if any
•    Applies FLSA ruleset, if applicable

Note: If the pay date is on or before today’s date, you might be prompted to enter an authorization code; see Authorization Code for Backdated Payroll on the facing page.

When the calculation begins, the Calculating Payroll form opens. When the Close button is enabled, the calculation is complete. You can close the form and return to the Process Payroll form.

Note: All dates and times in PrismHR are Central Time.

Note: When your client is set up for Worksite Payroll Approval and Self Service, the Self Service Restrictions are set to either Print or Select/Null, and the ACH status on the Billing tab on the Client Details form is not set to Wire Transfer Client, the following message displays for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors who are calculating payroll: To move into the payroll approval status and generate the approval email, click Yes. To bypass the payroll approval step and move the payroll to the next step, click No. In addition, this message displays for all users calculating payroll when the client has enabled payroll approval and the ACH status is not set to Wire Transfer Client. If there were any errors, they display at the bottom of the Process Payroll form in the Errors and Warnings panel. You must resolve these errors before you can proceed to the next step. If warning messages display, payroll calculation does not fail but not resolving them could cause accounting issues. For example, if the employee’s recorded timesheet hours are incorrect, warning messages similar to the following would display:

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 36 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

Note: If you enabled the Enable payroll live check calculation warning field on the System Parameters form and the system will create live checks during payroll processing, a warning message displays during payroll calculation, “Warning: there are live checks.” In addition, helpful messages display in this panel that clearly define what needs to be fixed to successfully process a payroll. For example:

Note: You can download the errors, warnings, and messages that display in this panel to an Excel spreadsheet by clicking the Errors and Warnings Download icon ( ). After calculating a payroll, the following dialog displays: “Do you want to send the payroll approval to the client?” Click one of the following options: • Click Yes to send the approval notification email to the client. • Click No to disregard sending the approval notification, which closes the dialog. The payroll’s batch status then updates to Calculation Complete and allows users to post the payroll or recalculate and submit it for approval.

Authorization Code for Backdated Payroll If the system is configured to require an authorization code when the pay date is on or before the current date, the system prompts you for that code.

  1. Enter the Authorization Code. If you do not know the code, contact your payroll manager or system administrator.
  2. Click Accept. The system proceeds with the calculation.

Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers Use the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers form to recalculate taxes on prior payroll vouchers for tax codes. if • it was calculated incorrectly earlier OR

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 37 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

• there has been a change in the minimum wage levels, which affects all hourly employees whose current wage matches an amount you designate OR • there has been a change in the wage level of the individual employee, for example getting a raise or a promotion etc.

To access the form, click Payroll. Under Payroll|Action, select Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers.

Note: You can access historical reports by selecting Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers Report History.

• This only displays historical previews of reports where Update Tax was enabled. • It will also show if any warnings were generated on the Job Control while processing. The Include SUTA/FUTA Successor Wages field should be Yes for this to work.

To recalculate taxes on vouchers: 1. Select a Tax Type and complete the applicable sections for each from the following options: • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - Unemployment on page 38 • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - Miscellaneous on page 44 • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - Medicare on page 51 • See Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers - OASDI on page 56 2. Click Preview Changes - a job progress window opens. If there are any errors, make the required changes and redo the process. 3. Click Close to close the job progress window, and see the changes in the tax amounts to be made for each employee in the preview pane. Only the first 100 records show up in the preview pane. Click the Download Report link to download this report. 4. Click Cancel if you do not want to recalculate the tax code on the vouchers. 5. Click Update Tax to update the changes to tax calculations on vouchers.

Note: When the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers process is run, and an employee has taxable wages with overlimit wages to the SUTA state being processed that have been backed out via tax adjustment before running the utility, the adjustment will continue to occur. Each occurrence will be reported in the processing reports, on-screen process log report, and the Job Control Status report, including the PDF and XLS versions, with the following message stating Employee XXXXXX in company XXXXX has 0.00 Gross Taxable with an Overlimit amount >0.00, resulting in a negative tax amount. Additional adjustment may be required.

 Include SUTA/FUTA            Select from the following options:
 Successor Wages
                              •       No - This is the default option. When set to No, the recalculation utility
                                      will only look to actual vouchers on the employee record to determine
                                      tax amounts. Successor wage tax amounts will not be recalculated. If you

                                      utility when successor wages are not included.
                              •       Yes - When set to Yes, the recalculation utility will include the successor
                                      wage and tax amounts in the results of the voucher recalculation utility.
                                      If successor earnings were entered for FUTA, and you are adjusting FUTA
                                      rates, the state will be determined based on the current home work
                                      location for the employee in the recalculation process. For example, if an
                                      employee has FUTA successor earnings and works in NY which has a
                                      FUTA rate increase, those wages would be included in the rate
                                      adjustment. If that employee has a home location of FL, the wages would
                                      not be included.

                              Note: When recalculating taxes on vouchers to include successor wages,
                              you cannot adjust the wage limit to be less than the successor wage
                              amount. The successor wages would need to be adjusted manually. If you
                              try to adjust the wage limit to be less than the successor wage amount
                              when recalculating taxes on vouchers to include successor wages, the
                              following sample error will generate notifying you that the employee has
                              successor wages in excess of the taxable wage limit.

                                          Error: Employee T16129 in company 925 has Successor Earnings in
                                          excess of the taxable limit. Cannot adjust that amount.

Recalculating Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages Use the Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages form to recalculate the overtime payroll wages that are exempt from income tax for employees in the state of Alabama for a client. This process will not modify any existing payroll voucher data including exempt earnings, taxable earnings, and tax withheld for AL Income Tax 01-20. This recalculation will provide a report of the recalculation results. The recalculated values will be applied to MasterTax reporting, W-2 reporting, and Report Center reporting of actual exempt hours and wages for AL Overtime Income tax exemption. Tax adjustments will be required if the recalculated values do not align with the payroll data when it was processed. The Alabama income tax exemption applicable to overtime wages ended on June 30, 2025. For any wages earned in June 2025 but paid in July 2025, the Alabama Overtime exemption will be honored. Exempt overtime wages earned on or before June 30 but not paid until July 2025 may be reported on the July 2025 Form A-6 or the September Form A-1 if quarterly filing.

After running the Recalculate AL Overtime utility, you can leverage Report Center to review the employees taxable wages with the exempt overtime amounts. The batch cannot be finalized until the Calculation and Review processes have been successfully completed. After resolving any errors, you must recalculate the batch.

Finalizing the Payroll When you are sure all the information for the payroll batch is complete and accurate, finalize the payroll by clicking the Finalize icon ( ). During the Finalization process, PrismHR gathers the data from the vouchers created during the calculation of the payroll and finalizes each item to the appropriate register. The system creates a permanent record of the payroll within its files. Once the payroll is finalized, PrismHR considers it to be complete and creates another payroll for this client and pay group. The system cannot calculate or finalize more than one payroll for the same client at the same time.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 66 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

Reports and invoices designated to be printed at the completion of the payroll print immediately to your designated printer. The system sends checks and direct deposit advices, as well as any garnishment checks, to a print file. Note the following: • If you pass the ACH threshold limit during payroll processing a message displays in the job progress window on the Process Payroll form. In addition, the following warning displays in the Errors and Warnings panel after payroll calculation finishes, “The payroll is over the ACH threshold limit. You must clear the ACH hold before payroll displays in the ACH file. Delaying this action could delay releasing funds to employees.” (If the ACH threshold limit is null, the message and warning do not display. However, if the ACH threshold limit is set to at least zero (0), the message and warning do display if the payroll is over the limit.) • If you have a payroll where all employees receive live checks but the client is paying their invoice using ACH and that invoice exceeds the ACH threshold limit, the system displays a warning during calculation and finalization. At that time, the funds for the client are put on hold if the fees to be taken from the client are over the threshold limit.

Finalizing Payroll for Self-Service Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors Self-service worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors who are restricted from finalizing and printing payroll can indicate that they are ready to send the payroll to a service provider for finalization when they finish reviewing the payroll. After self-service worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors successfully calculate a payroll (the payroll must be in INITWARN or INITOK status) the following message displays, “Are you sure you want to submit the payroll for processing?” Make either of the following selections to continue: • Yes: The system moves the payroll to the next status and becomes visible to service providers in SuperBatch. In addition, making this selection dims/locks the Time Sheet Entry and Payroll Calculation icons and updates the Payroll Calculation icon’s text for all user types depending on the payroll status: • INITWARN: Payroll Calculation: Complete with Warnings, Submitted • INITOK: Payroll Calculation: Complete, Submitted Note: Selecting Yes does not allow self-service worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors to edit the payroll any further without a service provider resetting it back to them to any status before payroll calculation. After a service provider changes the payroll status back to any status with “TS,” the Time Sheet Entry icon becomes available to worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors once again. In addition, if the status is set to TSOKCOMP, the Payroll Calculation icon becomes available. • No: The system moves the payroll to the next status and is not visible to service providers in SuperBatch. In addition, making this selection updates the Payroll Calculation icon’s text for all user types depending on the payroll status: • INITWARN: Payroll Calculation: Complete with Warnings, Not submitted • INITOK: Payroll Calculation: Complete, Not submitted Note: Selecting No requires recalculation to submit the payroll for processing.

Recalculating Overtime in a Payroll These instructions explain how to recalculate overtime for a payroll in PrismHR.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 72 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

Overview In this example, the process calculates any additional overtime for hourly salespersons that were: • Paid weekly on an hourly basis • Paid a bonus or commission on the first week of each month for sales in the previous month

The calculations are based on regulations defined in the Code of Federal Regulations, Title 29, Part 778 published by the Department of Labor (DOL) because the employees were paid overtime on weekly pay cycles based on a fluctuating work week. When the company pays the commission that covered the prior pay periods, the company must recalculate the overtime, incorporating the paid commission amounts and paying the overage to the employee at the same time as the bonus or commission. For example: • An employee has earned $384 in bonuses or commissions for a four-week period. • You must pay their bonus or commission in a payroll type of Special (created in Payroll Control) and enter the bonus or commission amount on the Batch Payments form for that payroll. • The employee is due overtime compensation after 40 hours. • During the prior four-week period, the salesperson worked 44, 40, 44, and 48 hours.

Therefore, the salesperson is due additional compensation weeks 1, 3, and 4. They are not owed any additional compensation for week 2 because they did not work overtime. Based on the following formula (described in Part 778 of the regulations), the employee is due additional compensation of $4.36 each for week 1 and week 3: • $384 (bonus/commission) / 4 (weeks) = $96 • $96 / 44 (hours worked that week) = $2.18 • $2.18 / 2 = $1.09 • $1.09 x 4 (overtime hours) = $4.36 additional compensation

Using the same formula above, you would pay an extra $8 for week 4 in which the employee worked 8 overtime hours.

Enter the Routing Code for the financial institution (also known as the transit number). The other information populates. 3. Select PayCard (Automove). This indicates that your organization uses the account for pay cards that can automatically be replaced by a checking account. 4. Select Debit Card Update. This indicates that this routing code supports debit cards and requires an update to the issuer for use of a new card.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 79 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

  1. If you track debit card updates, the Debit Card Track option displays. Select this option if this financial institution tracks a debit card ID. The system then requests the debit card ID at ACH entry.

  2. Click Save.

Pay Card for Employee You need to set up each employee with the pay card.

To set up employee pay cards: 1. Open Employee Details (found in the Back Office menu under HR|Change). 2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 3. Select the Deposit tab. 4. Ensure that the Status fields are set correctly.

  1. Enter the Direct Deposit Information: • From the Type drop-down, select Checking. • Enter the Transit Number (routing code). The Bank Name displays. • Enter the employee’s Account Number. • Select the appropriate option from Pay Type (typically All). • Select the appropriate option from the Method drop-down (typically Remaining Balance). • If appropriate, enter values in the Amount and Limit fields. • From the Status drop-down, select Deposit Active.

  2. Click Save.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 80 Chapter 2 Processing Payroll

The account displays in Employee Portal (EP) as a Pay Card account.

Direct Deposit Settings The employee can go into EP and change the direct deposit settings. For example, they might want to send some or all of their pay to a checking account. 1. The employee logs into EP. 2. They navigate to their direct deposit settings (your organization determines the menu path). 3. The employee clicks Add Account and then enters their account information. They must define a checking account.

  1. The employee saves their changes. The account is added to the list as Pending.

The checking account is in prenotification status.

Once it passes pre-note, the system deactivates the pay card and distributes the employee’s pay to the new account. Until that time, the system continues to pay the employee via the pay card.

Processing Pay On-Demand Payments Using the Pay On-Demand feature, you can pay employees in real time without having to wait for an ACH transaction. This process uses pay cards to pay employees off-cycle for instant payment. The most common uses for this feature are: • Paying someone quickly for hours missed • Paying a terminated employee’s wages on the same day they are terminated To generate a file for processing payments, use the Pay On-Demand Processing, which is available on the Operations|Action menu. For example:

Voiding Pay On-Demand Payments Employees who are paid using pay on-demand processing have an invoice amount that is debited on the ACH file. However, if you void the pay on-demand voucher, the invoice amount displays as a credit on the ACH file. Note the following: • If you run the pay on-demand process (that is, you generate a file) and then you complete a void, no changes occur in the history file. • If you do not generate a file and a void occurs, then the system does not include the voucher in the next file creation.

Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch SuperBatch, a payroll processing hub, helps payroll processors oversee each payroll assignment without adding extra work or time. Using a streamlined workflow, you can accomplish all your payroll tasks—entering time data, checking for errors, finalizing and printing—directly from the SuperBatch. For example:

Note: When there is a long list of payrolls the automatic refresh causes the screen to “bounce” and does not return you to the payroll where you were working. To stop this automatic refresh, click the Stop Timer ( ) icon at the top of the form. Clicking this “hourglass” icon stops the timer until you click the icon again. (The icon changes to indicate a start/stop status.)

Working with SuperBatch SuperBatch allows you to quickly process a large volume of payrolls accurately. In addition, you can view and download any warnings (yellow triangle) or errors (red triangle) in the payroll by clicking the icon. A Payroll Warning or Payroll Errors message displays where you can click Reset Payroll to restart the payroll or click Print

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 100 Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch

to open a report in .csv format, so you can view the warnings or errors and quickly address issues that prevent payroll processing from completing. Note: All errors and warnings that occur during and after payroll process calculation display the employee’s last name, preferred name instead of their last name, first name, if applicable. (If the employee does not have a preferred name, then their last name, first name displays.) The contents of the SuperBatch form are specific to your user ID. Client payrolls assigned to you that remain incomplete as of the Cutoff Date Up To are the only ones that appear on your SuperBatch form. The basic flow of using SuperBatch appears below.

Using the Filtering Options You can use the filtering options in the enhanced version of SuperBatch to limit the payrolls that display: • Cutoff Date Up To: Includes all incomplete payroll batches that require payroll processing and are due on or before that date. (The default is the Friday of the current week.) Note: You can adjust the lookback period the system uses for the Cutoff Date Up To date by enabling the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code on the System Parameters form. However, note the following when using the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code: • Enabling this custom feature code displays the SuperBatch Lookback Period field on the System Parameters form, where you can adjust the date. • The default for the SuperBatch process is the standard 95-day lookback period. • If you enable this field but do not enter a numeric value, the system defaults to the standard 95-day lookback period.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 101 Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch

•    If you remove the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code, the system hides the SuperBatch
     Lookback Period field and reverts to the standard 95-day lookback period.
Note the following about the Cutoff Date Up To filtering option:
•    The system selects all payrolls by the cutoff date, not the pay date.
•    When the Cutoff Date Up To date is greater than the current date, the system selects all payrolls with a
     pay date greater than or equal to today's date (minus 95 days), plus all payrolls from the current date to
     the entered pay date.
•    When the Cutoff Date Up To date is less than the current date, the system selects all payrolls with a pay
     date greater than the entered pay date (minus 95 days).
•    Payrolls will always display for the Cutoff Date Up To date minus 95 days. For example, if the date
     entered is 100 days in the past, the system displays payrolls 195 to 100 days in the past.

• Payroll Processor: Payroll representative who is the current active user. In addition, this filter allows you to select all payroll processors. (The incomplete payroll batches assigned to that payroll processor display.) Important! If you enable Manager Only Views All SuperBatch Payrolls in the Global Configuration form, Payroll Processor users are only able to view their assigned payrolls and cannot use the SuperBatch Payroll Transfer functionality. • Self Service: The client processes all or some steps of their own payrolls. Calculating Payroll Vouchers To begin the payroll calculation process, click the Ready for Calculation icon on the ribbon. All payrolls ready for calculation display. Note: Time sheet entry must be complete to enable payroll calculation. The SuperBatch form allows you to calculate more than one payroll at a time. Also, the calculation takes place in the background, so you can work on other payrolls while the system calculates the payroll batch.

While PrismHR calculates the payroll, the icon displays. During the payroll calculation process, PrismHR creates a payroll voucher for each employee to be paid in the current payroll as follows: • Calculates full gross-to-net earnings • Posts any other earnings combined with selected time sheet earnings to one of up to twelve payroll vouchers that could be created for an individual employee • Calculates and processes scheduled deductions • Calculates and takes payroll taxes • Processes any active tax calculation overrides or deduction overrides • Creates billing vouchers • Calculates accounting • Calculates benefits and benefit deductions • Accrues paid time off registers, if any • Applies FLSA ruleset, if applicable

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 109 Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch

After the payroll calculation process, the relevant icon displays:

    Payroll calculation completed successfully and is ready for client approval. You can proceed to the next
step. (See Using SuperBatch on page 100.)

     Payroll calculation completed with errors. The errors need to be resolved and the payroll recalculated
before you can proceed.

If warning messages display, payroll calculation does not fail but not resolving them could cause accounting issues. For example, if there are obsolete Position, Department, Division, or Project codes associated with an employee’s timesheet details, warning messages display.

Calculating Payrolls After payrolls are enabled, click Ready for Calculation in the ribbon, which displays all payrolls ready for calculation (identified by icon). For example:

Do the following: • To calculate a single payroll, select the checkbox for the payroll you want to calculate, then click Calculate Selected. • To calculate multiple payrolls, either select the checkbox for each payroll you want to calculate or click Calculate All to calculate all payrolls listed. After clicking a calculation button, the system opens the Calculate All Payrolls form, which displays all payrolls eligible for calculation. Click Continue to proceed. The system makes the calculations. You can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Note: If there are pre-validation errors for a payroll, then the system will not calculate it. You will need to resolve any issues with the payroll to proceed.

Displaying Warning Messages If there are warnings in the payroll batch, you can review them. These are items that do not prevent the posting of the batch; for example, an employee in the batch who has no hours in the time sheet.

Performing Error Review If PrismHR encountered errors during the payroll Calculation process, the icon displays. Click this icon to review any messages from the system regarding the errors it encountered. Once you have taken the proper steps to correct the error situation, you must calculate the batch again. The batch cannot be finalized until the Calculation and Review processes have been successfully completed. After resolving any errors, you must recalculate the batch.

Performing Payroll Batch Approval Payroll approval is an option available anywhere payroll is processed, such as during SuperBatch calculation and Process Payroll calculation, that allows the payroll processor and client to communicate electronically regarding the approval of a calculated payroll. Once the payroll processor has calculated the payroll, PrismHR automatically sends an e-mail notifying the client that the payroll is ready for their review and approval. There are two payroll approval processes you can use: • Standard payroll approval process: Once the payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. Using the Payroll Approval form, the approver reviews the payroll and can either approve or deny it. If the payroll is denied, the approver must provide a reason. (See Processing Standard Payroll Approval on page 148.) • Multistep payroll approval process: You must setup a minimum of two payroll approval steps before the payroll is finalized (that is, after calculation). For example, you can use this process so an assistant manager

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 114 Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch

can perform the initial payroll approval, and then a general manager can perform the final review and
complete the approval. (Note: Only service providers can setup a multistep payroll approval process.) (See
Processing Multistep Payroll Approval on page 152.)

Note the following: • Only specified approvers can approve/deny a payroll and view reports. During a SuperBatch payroll calculation, approvals are generated after the approver selects Reviewed OK during that process. • You cannot bypass payroll approval if the client is set up for wire transfer on the Client Details > Billing tab. Instead, the system automatically sends the approval notification email after you calculate the payroll. • If the client is not set up for wire transfer, service providers can bypass payroll approval from the Process Payroll form. • When processing payrolls where the Maximum ACH Amount is set on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the Restartable Payroll and Legacy Payroll features prevent submitted payrolls (those whose status is set to INITPEND), that exceed a set ACH amount, from processing until they are approved by a Billing Representative. Note: To use the Legacy Payroll feature, you must enable the LEGACY-PAYROLL-GLOBAL custom feature code. Once notified, the client can log in and review the payroll using the Payroll Approval form, then either accept the payroll or explain what changes are required. (See Processing Standard Payroll Approval on page 148See Processing Standard Payroll Approval on page 148See Processing Standard Payroll Approval on page 148 or Processing Multistep Payroll Approval.) After the client approves the payroll, you can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Handling a Denied Payroll If the client requires additional changes, the client approval icon displays as “Payroll has been denied approval by client.” 1. Click the icon to review the client’s explanation in the Payroll Message. (You can review the worksite manager’s or worksite trusted advisor’s detailed comment on why the payroll was denied. In addition, click Print to view the comment in report format, where it can then display as a PDF or you can export it to XLS format.) 2. After reviewing the explanation: • Click Close. You can return to handle the issue at a later time. • Click Reset Payroll. The payroll returns to the Ready to Calculate status, so that you can make any changes that are required. 3. After you reset the payroll, make the required changes and run the calculation again. 4. Review the payroll reports. 5. The client will review the payroll again. • If the client rejects the changed payroll, return to step 1. • If the client approves the payroll, you can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Finalizing Payroll When you are sure all the information for the payroll is complete and accurate, finalize the payroll by clicking the Payroll is ready to finalize icon ( ). The SuperBatch form allows you to finalize more than one payroll at a time. For example:

During the Finalization process, PrismHR gathers the data from the vouchers created during the calculation of the payroll and finalizes each item to the appropriate register. The system creates a permanent record of the payroll within its files. Once the payroll is finalized, PrismHR considers it to be complete and creates another payroll for the client and pay group. The system cannot calculate or finalize more than one payroll for the same client at the same time. Reports and invoices designated to print at the completion of the payroll print immediately to your designated printer. The system sends checks and direct deposit advices, as well as any garnishment checks, to a print file.

Finalizing a Single Payroll Once it is enabled, click the Payroll is ready to finalize icon ( ) for the payroll.

Finalizing Multiple Payrolls In the SuperBatch form, some users can select and finalize multiple payrolls. See the System Administration Guide to learn about the settings required to access this feature.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 116 Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch

To finalize multiple payrolls, do the following: 1. Click Finalize All at the bottom of the SuperBatch form. The system opens the Finalize All Payrolls form, which displays all payrolls eligible for finalization.

  1. To remove a payroll from the list, click the x at the far left of the line. This allows you to finalize only the payrolls that you are ready to process.
  2. Click Continue to proceed. The system finalizes the payrolls. You can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Note: If there are errors for a payroll, then the system will not finalize it. You need to resolve any issues with the payroll to proceed.

Printing and Mailing Payroll Batches The final payroll batch steps are to print and mail the batch documents, including the billing invoice, reports, direct deposit advices, and paychecks. The Print/Mail feature provides a method of tracking the payroll batch through the actual mailing of the batch documents. The handling of these documents depends on your organization’s procedures. The documents for payroll batches that have been posted and have the Status MAIL are ready to be bundled and processed for mailing. Checks can be “set aside” indefinitely until you are ready to print them if your organization prints the checks.

Note: Users can specify what prints for a client during the payroll process on the Client Details Payroll tab.

Setting Up the Payroll Batch Shipping Mode Setting the shipping mode for the payroll batch allows you to click the Print icon during the printing and mailing process (known as the Autocomplete feature), so you can select when and how to ship the payroll batch.

To set up the payroll batch shipping mode, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change select System Parameters. 3. Enter ALL as the Automatic Mail Code. (Note: An Automatic Mail Code is an existing delivery code to set automatic mailing capability when shipping items in a payroll batch.)

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 117 Chapter 3 Using SuperBatch

When a delivery method code is entered in this field, the system sets all payrolls that use the same delivery
method to Mailed. Payrolls with different delivery methods must have their status manually set to Mailed.
For example, if USPS is entered as a code, the system sets all payrolls sent by US mail to Mailed. Payrolls
sent by FedEx must have their status manually set, which logs the tracking number or other information.
Enter ALL to set all payrolls to Mailed status, regardless of the delivery method.
  1. After clicking the Payroll is ready to finalize icon ( ) in the SuperBatch form, the payroll automatically completes.

To submit an employee’s retroactive time sheet entry, do the following: 1. Select the Payroll # in the Time Sheet Entry form. 2. Select the Employee from the list in the Time Sheet Entry form. 3. The Detail Time Sheet Entry form displays. Click the New Retro Pay Entry option from the Entry field. 4.   1. After clicking Yes, the Retroactive Time Sheet Entry form displays.

Importing the Data File If a client is set to use a time sheet import on the Client Details Time Sheet tab, use Time Sheet Import to import the data file.

  1. In the Time Sheet Entry form, click Time Sheet Import . The Time Sheet Import form opens.

Chapter 5 Processing Approvals When events take place that could potentially require an approval, such as a new hire or a payroll, PrismHR determines if there is a policy in place for the particular approval type. • If there is no policy definition, then the system immediately updates the database with the new hire or other information. • If there is an approval policy, then the system generates an approval event. If the first step for the approval is assigned to a particular user, then an e-mail is sent to that user. In addition, when the user logs in, the dashboard alerts the user of any pending approvals. Approvals Pending is found in the Client menu under Client|Action.

Approvals Pending The Approvals Pending form lists any pending approvals that are assigned or available to you. • An approval that is assigned to a particular user can only be acted upon by that user. • Approvals are available to a user if one of the user’s roles matches the role applicable to the current approval step.

Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) You can act on approvals listed in the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel. • Standard Approvals: see Human Resources User Guide or Approvals Guide • Payroll Approvals:

Approvals Pending (Available to You) To act on an approval that is available to you, “grab” the approval. The system assigns the approval to you. 1. Within the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel, click the desired Approval Type. The Approval form opens. You can click Show Audit History to display the history of users involved in processing the action. 2. Click Grab. The selected approval type now appears in the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel. There are two methods available to process an approval:

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 146 Chapter 5 Processing Approvals

• Click the Approve icon (blue checkmark) for the Approval Type you want to approve. Click Yes in the confirmation message that displays to continue with the approval. An approval confirmation displays at the top of the form. • “Grab” the approval: 1. Within the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel, click the desired Approval Type. The Approval form opens. You can click Show Audit History to display the history of users involved in processing the action. 2. Click Grab. The selected approval type now appears in the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel.

Note: You can open the pending approval in Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel and click Return to Queue. The approval pending item is then returned to the Available to You queue for you or another user to access later.

Related Topics Overriding Global Approval Policies in the Human Resources User Guide Setting Global Approval Policies in the System Administration User Guide or Approvals Guide

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 147 Chapter 5 Processing Approvals

Processing Standard Payroll Approval Once the payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. Using the Payroll Approval form, the approver reviews the payroll and can either approve or deny it. If the payroll is denied, the approver must provide a reason. (You can view the Worksite Payroll Approval comment when the Worksite Manager or Worksite Trusted Advisor denies a payroll.) For example:

Note: For information about how to setup and process a multistep payroll approval process, which involves setting up a minimum of two payroll approvers, see Processing Multistep Payroll Approval.

Setting Up Standard Payroll Approval Before calculating a payroll for standard payroll approval, ensure you have setup payroll approval.

Setup standard payroll approval by doing the following: 1. Enable the Standard option in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form. 2. Click Save. 3. Setup at least one worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor who has Payroll Approver as their HR Role on their user record.

Processing the Payroll After setting up payroll approval and before finalizing payroll approval, there are two methods you can use to process the payroll:

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 148 Chapter 5 Processing Approvals

• SuperBatch calculation: When you calculate a payroll with worksite approval setup using the SuperBatch form on the Operations|Action menu, the approval is generated after you select Reviewed OK during the Review step. Selecting this button triggers the approval and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. • Process Payroll calculation: When you calculate a payroll using the Process Payroll form on the Payroll|Action menu for a client with worksite payroll approval, the following message displays, “Do you wish to notify the client that this batch is ready to approve?” If you select Yes, the system starts the approval process and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. If you select No, the system bypasses the approval process and moves the payroll forward to the next status. You must recalculate the payroll, if you need to begin the approval process. Note: If the client is set to Wire Transfer for payroll processing, this choice is not available and instead, the payroll advances immediately to Client approval pending status if worksite approval is established.

Finalizing Standard Payroll Approval This part of the payroll approval process is usually performed by the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor. Although a service provider can also perform the payroll approval, usually that only happens when the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor is not part of the approval process or has made a verbal approval.

To complete the payroll approval process, do the following: 1. The Payroll Approval form displays the information for review. 2. Review the reports for the payroll by selecting them from the View Report/Analytic drop-down: • Approval Payroll Reports: Opens the Approval Payroll Reports form, which lists all the available payroll approval reports. Click the Open File icon in the Job column to view the report listed in the Report Title column. (.) • Employees in Payroll: Lists the employees in the payroll batch. This report provides a summary of the employee voucher, including all pay and deductions. • Payroll Register Report: Displays the Payroll Register Report. This report displays information for each employee on the report, as well as the current, month-to-date, quarter-to-date, and year-to-date values for pay, deductions, taxes, and paid time off. • Check Journal Report: Allows you to run the Payroll Check Journal Report. This report provides employee payroll check details. • Deduction Register Report: Lists all payroll deductions and the amount the employer contributes.

Processing Multistep Payroll Approval Using the Multistep payroll approval process, you must setup a minimum of two payroll approval steps before the payroll is finalized (that is, after calculation). For example, you can use this process so an assistant manager can perform the initial payroll approval, and then a general manager can perform the final review and complete the approval. Note: As done in the original payroll approval method, service providers can still approve payrolls and override the approval steps. This payroll approval process consists of the following procedures: 1. Setting up multistep payroll approval. (Note: Only service providers can setup a multistep payroll approval process.) 2. Processing the payroll. 3. Finalizing multistep payroll approval. Note the following about processing multistep payroll approvals: • Approvers who are waiting for their step to become available can still review the payroll approval reports on the Payroll Approval form, but they cannot approve or deny the approval until it’s their turn. (The buttons remain inactive until their turn is available.) • Multistep payroll approval is not available for self-service payroll. If you select Self-Service Payroll on the Payroll tab in the Client Details form, an error message displays, “Multistep Worksite Payroll Approval is not supported with Self-Service Payroll. You must choose another Worksite Payroll Approval Type to continue.”

Overview of the Multistep Payroll Approval Process Once the payroll processor calculates the payroll, PrismHR sends a message to the first payroll approver that the payroll is ready for review and approval. Using the Payroll Approval form, the approver reviews the payroll and can either approve or deny it. If the payroll approval is denied, the approver must provide a reason. (You can view the Worksite Payroll Approval comment when the Worksite Manager or Worksite Trusted Advisor denies a payroll.) For example:

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 152 Chapter 5 Processing Approvals

After the next approver submits approval (and is the final approver), you can proceed to the next step of the payroll process.

Setting Up Multistep Payroll Approval Before calculating a payroll that should have multistep payroll approval, ensure you have setup at least two or more payroll approval steps.

Service providers can setup multistep payroll approval by doing the following: 1. Enable the Multistep option in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form. After selecting this option, an informational message displays, “Approval Steps must be defined under Approval Policies to fully activate Multistep Approvals. If steps are not defined, this setting will work the same as Standard worksite payroll approval.” Click OK. 2. Click Save. An informational message displays, “Approval Steps must be defined under Approval Policies to fully activate Multistep Approvals. Would you like to define them now?” Click Yes. (Note: If two or more approval steps are not defined under Approval Policies, the setting works the same as Standard worksite payroll approval.) 3. The system redirects you to the Approval Policies form, which displays on the HR|Change menu. Now that you have set up the client, the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option displays in the Approval Type field. (Note: Prior to setting up the client, the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option is not available on this form.) 4. Select the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option, then setup at least two payroll approval steps in the Step panel and click Save. (Note: If you only setup one step and click Save, a message displays, “A minimum of two steps are required for Payroll Approval (Multistep).” Click OK and setup the second step.) Note: You must setup at least one user with the HR Role (worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor) or A/M Role (service provider) that was selected on the Approval Policies form, so the system generates the approval to a user.

Payroll Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 153 Chapter 5 Processing Approvals

Processing the Payroll After setting up payroll approval and before finalizing payroll approval, there are two methods you can use to process the payroll: • SuperBatch calculation: When you calculate a payroll with worksite approval setup using the SuperBatch form on the Operations|Action menu, the approval is generated after you select Reviewed OK during the Review step. Selecting this button triggers the approval and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. For example:

• Process Payroll calculation: When you calculate a payroll using the Process Payroll form on the Payroll|Action menu for a client with worksite payroll approval, the following message displays, “Do you wish to notify the client that this batch is ready to approve?” If you select Yes, the system starts step one in the approval process and updates the payroll status to Client approval pending. If you select No, the system bypasses the approval process and moves the payroll forward to the next status. You must recalculate the payroll, if you need to begin the approval process. Note: If the client is set to Wire Transfer for payroll processing, this choice is not available and instead, the payroll advances immediately to Client approval pending status if worksite approval is established.

Finalizing Multistep Payroll Approval This part of the payroll approval process is usually performed by the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor. Although a service provider can also perform the payroll approval, usually that only happens when the worksite manager or the worksite trusted advisor is not part of the approval process or has made a verbal approval.

To complete the multistep payroll approval process, do the following: 1. The Payroll Approval form displays the information for review. 2. Review the reports for the payroll by selecting them from the View Report/Analytic drop-down: • Employees in Payroll: Lists the employees in the payroll batch. Click the employee ID to view the Employee Details. • Payroll Summary: Summarizes the vouchers in the payroll batch. Click the voucher number to view the voucher details.

  4. If the next approver submits approval (and is the final approver) and clicks Submit, the system proceeds to the next step of the payroll process.

Establishing Workers’ Compensation Insurance Policy and Carrier Information If your organization services clients with employees in various states, be sure to use the correct workers’ compensation (W/C) policies for each state where you do business. Use the W/C Policies form to establish workers’ compensation insurance policy and carrier information.

Policy Information Use the Policy Information panel to maintain basic information about the W/C insurance policy.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 Payroll Code Files

Field Description Policy ID Workers’ compensation insurance policy ID. Description Description of the insurance policy. Policy Start Date Date when coverage begins under this policy. This is the beginning of the policy year. Policy Type Select Primary if the policy is maintained by the PEO. Select Individual if the policy is carried by the client. Rate Template ID If you use a table-based approach for maintaining W/C insurance rates, enter the appropriate rate template ID. Suppress Billing Select this option to suppress billing in cases where the client pays the policy premiums. Suppress G/L Accrual Select this option to suppress the generation of a general ledger account for any pay associated with this policy. Company Select this option to use client-level W/C accrual modifiers when Mod/Discount calculating W/C liability for this policy. Select the type of voluntary deduction on this panel. • Maximums: Set the maximum amount to be deducted from an employee’s check during a specified period. • Limits: Set payroll batch limits for this deduction code. • Other Processing Parameters: Miscellaneous settings specific to different circumstances. Creating a New Deduction Code Setting Up Basic Deduction Code Information Select the parameters that define the new code in the Deduction Codes panel.

To set up basic deduction code information, do the following: 1. Enter or select the code in the Deduction Code field. (When creating a deduction code, use something brief but descriptive, such as LIFE for life insurance.) If you select this field, a selector form displays where you can search for a specific deduction code or its description or select a code from the list that displays. When this form opens, the description, deduction type, and obsolete date display. To filter the search further: • Select a Deduction Type (the default is All). • To display only obsolete codes, select Yes in the Obsolete field (the default is No). (Note: Codes with an obsolete date earlier than the current date do not display in the selector form.) To refresh the list, select Reset Search and Filters. 2. Enter a more detailed Description of the deduction code. 3. Select the Deduction Type. If you select Voluntary, the Voluntary Classifications panel displays. Important! Some deduction types and calculation methods are not compatible with each other. If you make an incompatible selection, the system displays a validation message. For example, if you first select a deduction type and then make a calculation method selection that is incompatible with the deduction type, the following message displays, “That method is invalid for this Deduction Type.” (The reverse applies if you first select a calculation method.) The message includes a warning that changing an existing deduction type or a calculation method may adversely affect any employee records that have already been setup. (If you are unsure whether or not to continue, check with your local system administrator or contact PrismHR Customer Support.) For proper reporting on W2 forms, do not set up Roth retirement contributions using the Post-Tax Retirement Contribution deduction type. Note: A warning displays if you try to update the Deduction Type for an existing Deduction Code, which results in the following after clicking OK and saving the record: • You cannot delete or update a Deduction Type after the system processes an updated Deduction Code through a complete payroll process. • A tool tip displays next to the Deduction Type field, “This deduction has already been applied to a payroll voucher. The type can no longer be adjusted and the code can no longer be deleted.” • The Deduction Type field and Delete button are disabled. 4. Select the Calculation Method used to calculate the payroll deduction amount for this deduction code. For example, you can use the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option to associate a non-qualified deferred compensation (NQDC) plan that the client set up with another company, where a percentage of the commissions is deferred, reducing taxable earnings. (This deduction code functions similar to a pre-tax deduction.) Note the following when using % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes:

% of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) If the Calculation Method is set to % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types), use the Exclude Ded. Type Code panel to exclude pre-tax benefit deduction types for plans that require contributions to be calculated as a percentage of gross earnings, such as COPERA. For example:

Note the following when using % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types): • You can select one or more deduction type codes to exclude. However, you must select at least one deduction type code. • You must set the Deduction Type field to Voluntary or Pre-Tax Retirement Contribution. • You can enable the 403(b) Retirement option and select multiple voluntary classifications in the Voluntary Classifications panel. However, observe the following when making these selections: • You cannot enable more than one “retirement” voluntary classification. • You cannot enable both Section 125 and Section 132. • If there are no matching Deduction Types, the system calculates the deduction on full gross earnings. • Selecting a deduction code with % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) and for all excluded Deduction Types ensures payroll processing subtracts the sum of all matching deduction amounts from gross earnings before calculating the deduction. • A deduction code set to % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) and a Deduction Type set to Voluntary excludes the deduction amount and treats the deduction code amount as pre-tax when you enable Voluntary Classification 409(a). • A deduction code set to % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) and a Deduction Type set to Voluntary excludes the deduction amount and treats the deduction code amount as post-tax when you do not enable Voluntary Classification 409(a).

Configuring Maximums and Limits If necessary, use the Maximums and Limits panels to establish the maximum deduction amounts and the deduction limits for this deduction code.

Setting up Maximums You can define monthly, quarterly, and annual maximums. Payroll automatically tracks the amount deducted from an employee’s pay during the period and stops making the payroll deductions once the maximum is reached. Enter maximums only when the maximum amounts apply to most employees.

To set up deduction maximums, do the following: 1. Set the time period in the Basis field. 2. Enter the Maximum amount that the system will deduct during the selected Basis. You can define maximum amounts for a specific employee on the employee’s Payroll Deduction form, which overrides the amount in this field.

Setting up Limits You can define limits for the deduction. Since PrismHR only checks limits during batch payroll processing (as opposed to when you enter an online pay check), you can specify only pay periods supported during batch payroll processing. Enter limits only when the limit amounts apply to most employees.

Note: The payroll period used as the basis for defining a limit displays in the Cd and Period fields.

To set up deduction limits, do the following: 1. Enter the deduction’s Limit amount for the payroll period. The value in the Limit field defines the maximum amount that PrismHR can deduct for this code during a payroll period. You can also define limits for a specific employee on the employee’s Payroll Deduction form, which overrides the value of this field.

Daily Overtime Rules Use the Daily Overtime Rules panel to define the parameters for daily calculations. 1. For example, 8. • In the Pay Excess Hours with Pay Code field, enter the pay code used to pay employees who work overtime at this level. • The daily level premium pay rule only applies if the weekly hours worked are less than or equal to the number of hours entered in the If Hours Worked for Weeks Are Less Than or Equal To field. 2. Rule for Calculating Premium Pay for Consecutive Days Worked: • Enter the minimum number of consecutive days employees must work in one week to receive the premium pay in the When Consecutive Days Worked in a Week is GT field. • Enter the number of hours worked on a daily basis for this level in the When Hours Worked Those Days Are Greater Than field. • In the Pay Excess Hours with Pay Code field, enter the pay code used to pay employees who work overtime at this level. • The daily level premium pay rule only applies if the weekly hours worked are greater than the number of hours entered in the If Hours Worked for Weeks Were Greater Than field. 3. Click Save.

Pay Class Select the Pay Class for this payment, which determines the tax liability. All classifications except for Expense Reimbursements are considered taxable. Payments classified as Non-Cash Fringe Benefit, Reported Tips, and Memo are considered non-cash. Most pay codes define payments made to employees for services rendered (amounts earned). You would classify such payments as Earnings. In some cases, however, you might want to include amounts on a payroll voucher that are not amounts “earned” by employees as part of their normal hourly wages or salary.
