Field Description Include in Variable Salary Pay Select to include this pay code in the employee’s Variable Salary pay. Important! You must enable all pay codes within a payroll as Include in Variable Salary Pay, so the system performs the correct calculation. If you need to pay an employee with a mix of variable salary and non-variable salary pay codes, you must pay the non- variable salary pay codes in a different payroll batch. In addition, if you need to pay an employee with a mix of Pay Types for the variable salary pay codes, you must pay each Pay Type in a different payroll batch. The Variable Salary pay method accurately tracks the hours that employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this pay method to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes. Important! When using Include in Variable Salary Pay, the pay codes paid to the employee must be set to Regular for the Pay Type. In addition, you must enable the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code on the System Parameters form to include the pay code in the employee’s Variable Salary pay. Unpaid Variable Salary Time Select to reduce an employee’s Variable Salary pay by the percentage of unpaid hours assigned to the Unpaid Pay Code (default is disabled). For example, if an employee makes $3000 per pay period and they submit 100 hours, where 90 hours are worked and 10 hours are unpaid. This indicates that the employee’s wages should be reduced by 10 hours, so the system reduces the wages for the pay period from $3000 to $2700. This calculation works as follows: $3000/10 hours of unpaid time is $300, so $300 is subtracted from the gross pay. (On the voucher, the Unpaid Time hours display as the number of hours in the time sheet entry for the unpaid pay code, but the unit rate and amount display as zero (0).) Note the following: • The Unpaid Variable Salary Time field only displays when the Include in Variable Salary Pay field is enabled for the pay code. • The system still allocates wages for the reduced amount, except the pay is reduced by the unpaid hours.

Creating Weighted Average Calculations for Pay Codes Your organization can create weighted average calculations for pay codes using the Weighted Average form. For example, California requires that employees be paid at their “regular rate” when using state-mandated paid time off. Other states, such as Arizona, permit a regular rate calculation rate. Weighted averages are used for either pay codes that are set to include hours/amount paid in overtime calculations or those that include amount paid only:

When applied to a pay code, it provides a weighted average of pay over a specified time frame. You might use weighted averages when improving calculations for FLSA. Use weighted average calculations when you need to: • Tie FLSA logic into weighted average pay code logic to pick up minimum wage rates when performing calculations. • Look at previous periods for compliance. (Typically, you would use lookback periods for salaried employees.) Please note that you should use caution when using the pay code for tipped employees with pay rates below minimum wage. Currently the calculation does not gross all such rates up to the minimum wage. Also note that

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 43 Chapter 1 Payroll Code Files

weighted averages do not include system-calculated shift differentials within the payroll that the pay code is used.

  1. Select Calculated Weighted Average Pay Rate to indicate that the pay code will use a calculated weighted average pay rate.
  2. The Exclude FLSA Exempt Employees field is a checkbox. This field is un-checked by default. You can check it and click Accept to enable this option. • When unchecked, any FLSA exempt employee will have their pay rate recalculated when paid with applicable pay codes. • When checked, no FLSA exempt employee will have their pay rate recalculated. The pay rate will default to their standard hourly pay rate.
  3. Enter each required pay period weighted average calculations:
    1. Select the Pay Period: weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, or monthly. The work week method can be used only with weekly and biweekly pay periods.
    2. Select the weighted average Method:

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 44 Chapter 1 Payroll Code Files

     •    Work Week: Based on a single payroll and the pay period is divided into seven-day increments. The
          weighted average is determined for the week encompassing the charge date.
     •    Pay Period: Based on a single payroll. The weighted average is determined for all charge dates
          within the payroll.
     •    Look back, full periods: Based on all vouchers with both a period start and period end date within
          the lookback period of the weighted average pay code’s charge date.
     •    Look back, period end: Based on all vouchers with a period end date within the lookback period of
          the weighted average pay code’s charge date.
c. If you selected a look back method, enter the Lookback Period number and then indicate whether the
   period is Days or Months.
  1. Click Accept.

Chapter 2 System-Level Setup It is important that you maintain payroll records properly, and understand how these files fit into PrismHR‘s processing scheme. Determine the best way to enter data into the payroll management files.

Maintaining Bank Accounts Use the Bank Accounts form to maintain the information for the accounts at financial institutions used in PrismHR.

Entering Bank Account Information Enter the basic information about the account in the Bank Accounts panel. For example:

Note: The 00 Checking Account is a special purpose account, the master account for all transactions. Each file header shows the 00 Checking Account as the main file header, with the funds being transferred into the account from whatever checking account the individual ACH shows it is processed. This adds a level of abstraction to the process, but allows a single account to process all the ACH clearing with only summary transactions from each of the actual checking accounts.

To maintain account information: 1. Enter or select the bank Account ID for this account. You can enter numeric or alphanumeric characters in this field, or a combination of both.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 46 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

Note: If a bank Account ID has already been used to process a transaction, you cannot delete it when one or
more of the following conditions exist:
•    The system created an ACH file with the bank Account ID.
•    The system processed cash receipts using the bank Account ID.
  1. Enter a Reference for the name of the financial institution where this account is maintained, as well as any other information. For example, Payroll Cash Account at Fleet Bank.
  2. Enter the Bank Name.
  3. Enter the Bank Address, which is the street or mailing address.
  4. Enter the City, State & ZIP Code.
  5. Enter the Transit Number assigned to this financial institution. This number prints on checks drawn on this bank unless you enter a different number in Transit Number (Chks) below.
  6. Enter the client’s Account Number at this financial institution. This account is debited when an offsetting settlement entry is created.
  7. Enter the Fractional Transit number that appears on checks. This number is the same for all checks drawn on a unique checking account, typically in the format NN/NNN.
  8. Enter the Check Title.
  9. Enter the Transit Number (Chks) that print on checks drawn on this bank. If this field is left blank, PrismHR uses the Transit Number value.
  10. Select Use Positive Pay if this account uses Positive Pay Files. You must also define the layout using the Positive Pay Setup form (see Positive Pay Setup on page 52).
  11. Enter the Acct Sys ChkID Number. This is the code your accounting software associates with this account and PrismHR uses for reconciliations or receipts.
  12. Select One Garn/Pay Chk Cntr to use the same check number sequence for payroll, third party, and garnishment checks. Otherwise, the system uses separate counters for each type.
  13. The Next Check Number and Next Garnishment Number display. You cannot modify those values on this form, but the number can be modified using the Next Number Control form.
  14. Enter or select the Offset Account ID for the offset settlement checking account. (Use the same ACH originator as this bank account.)
  15. Enter or select the Rebate Bill Code if this account belongs to the client. The system uses this code to credit the client for net checks that have been drafted.
  16. Enter the MICR Account Number that prints on the MICR line of checks.
  17. Enter or select the Employer ID who is the owner of the checking account, from a general ledger point of view.
  18. Select Inactive Account if this account is no longer used.
  19. Select the ACH Options for this account, if appropriate.
  20. Select Use for Garnishments Only to indicate that the account is used only for garnishment payments. This ensures that the account does not stop processing due to XMit Day/Time rules.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 47 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

  1. In the Minimum ACH Window (Days) field, enter the minimum number of days prior to the pay date that your organization must process a batch in order for employees to receive direct deposits. This value overrides the global parameter.
  2. Enter the minimum number of days it takes to obtain ACH credit in the Min ACH Receipt Days field. This value adjusts the G/L receipt date to correspond with your bank’s practices. It also ensures that if you use a negative ACH adjust date for cash receipts, this date is never earlier than the selection made here. If the cash receipt is earlier than the time indicated, the G/L effect adjusts to be this date. This does not change the actual ACH file. For example, enter 0 if you get credit for the same date you send, and enter 1 if you always get credit on the next day.
  3. Select Show in Cash Receipts if this account should be available for cash receipts.
  4. If applicable, enter the Max Void ACH Days, which is the number of banking days this account allows to pass from the Pay Date to Void Date. After that number of days, PrismHR displays warnings.
  5. Enter Post Cutoff Time for posting to begin on a payroll batch that uses this checking account.
  6. Enable Same Day Processing if the bank account is used for same day processing. (If you enable this field, the system translates this information to the ACH file.) Positive Pay Setup Use the Positive Pay Setup form to set up the positive pay file for the bank account. To access the form, open the Actions menu in Bank Accounts and select Positive Pay Setup. The Positive Pay file is created by interpreting the specifications from the bank, entering the Header, File Header, Detail, and Trailer Record parameters, and entering the appropriate UniData Masking Codes.

Note: Enter the masks required for the fields using standard UniData masking parameters. For example, R%10 places the item on a field of 10 zeroes. See Table 2 for a list of commonly used parameters.

To set up positive pay: 1. Access the setup form: click the Back Office menu and select System|Change > Bank Accounts. Then, click the Actions menu and select Positive Pay Setup. 2. To copy existing positive pay information, click Copy From Another Bank Account. Enter the bank account ID and then click Copy. 3. Enter a File Stub code. The system can group all accounts with the same file stub together for downloading, and it appends the year, month, and day to create the file name. For example, if you have multiple accounts with the same financial institution, enter the same File Stub for each account. 4. Enter the positive pay File Extension that defines the file type, typically .txt. 5. Set up the header record information, which determines the format for the header information for each record included in the overall positive pay file your organization will send to the bank: • Select the Header Record parameter that matches the header specification from the bank. • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.

  1. Set up a detail record information, which specifies the format for the individual checks that are grouped under each header: • Select the Detail Record parameter that matches the detail specification from the bank. • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.
  2. Set up a trailer record information; trailer records indicate the end of a group of checks: • Select the Trailer Record parameter that matches the trailer specification from the bank. • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.

Related Topics

Suspense Accounts Rather than have ACH data update immediately against a cash account before it is transmitted to the bank, which can cause confusion when users attempt to reconcile the account, your organization might want to create a “suspense” account for any bank account that processes ACH transactions. Each voucher is posted in detail against the suspense account. During ACH file creation, the total of the vouchers transmitted in a batch comes out of the suspense account and hits the cash account. This allows for easier reconciliation, as the ACH suspense account should be zero each day or reconcilable. It is easier to balance the bank’s daily reports because the totals in the cash account should match the amounts directly.

Bank Account Setup Set up the bank account in PrismHR. 1. Either create a new bank account or edit an existing one using the Bank Accounts form in the Back Office menu. 2. Select the Use Suspense Accounting option in the ACH Setup panel.

G/L Template Setup Enter the suspense G/L accounts for the account in the appropriate G/L template. 1. Open G/L Setup Maintenance (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter the G/L Template. 3. From the G/L Type drop-down, select Checking Accounts. The form lists each Checking Account and Description in the system. 4. For the accounts that indicate they use a suspense account, enter the Suspense GL Account.

  1. Click Save.

Voucher Examples The suspense G/L account displays in the Accounting tab of each ACH Employee Voucher.

The standard G/L account displays in the Accounting tab of vouchers for any paper checks.

Once your organization posts the ACH batch, the money moves from the suspense account to the cash account. The Account Distribution on the vouchers does not change.

Working with ACH Impounding Use the Offset Impound Accounts form to work with ACH impounding, where the system creates offset transactions for various client fund types. You can designate impound bank accounts where client net-pays,

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 55 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

payroll taxes, and retirement contributions are deposited. The system deposits the remainder of the client invoice amount leftover after deducting for net-pays, taxes, and retirement contributions into the bank account designated by the Offset Account ID on the Bank Accounts form. Note: Historically, PrismHR has supported generating a single ACH transaction to offset the client invoice amount. For a typical payroll, this transaction would be an ACH credit transaction. For most PEO/ASO clients, the total invoice amount is the aggregate of the client fees, employee net pays, taxes, and benefits, such as retirement. The system uses this functionality to designate the impound bank accounts where client net-pays, payroll taxes, and retirement contributions are deposited. The remainder of the client invoice amount leftover after deduction for net-pays, taxes, and retirement are deposited into the bank account designated by the “Offset Account ID” on the primary bank’s account form.

Note: You must enable the ACHBREAKONPRBATCH custom feature code on the System Parameters form to access the Offset Impound Accounts form on the Actions menu for the Bank Accounts form.

To set up ACH impounding for an account: 1. Go to the Bank Accounts form on the System|Change menu. 2. Enter or select an Account ID. 3. Select Offset Impound Accounts on the Actions menu. 4. Select the Fund Type to designate the billing component for which the offset credit applies on the ACH file. (You can set multiple types.) 5. Enter or select the Bank Account to return records from the system-level Bank Accounts file. 6. Click Close. The Bank Accounts form re-displays. 7. Click Save.

Bank Routing Use the Bank Routing form to establish bank routing and contact information, as well as how to support debit card transactions. 1. Enter the Routing Code for the financial institution.

Use this to indicate that the account is for pay cards that can be replaced automatically by a checking account. Refer to “Pay Cards and Direct Deposit” in the Payroll User Guide appendix for details on this feature.

The financial institution becomes the “originating DFI” by submitting the transactions to the ACH network. If you process ACH transactions for clients, each client can have a different financial institution. Use the ACH Originators form to maintain records for each institution.

(System validation on the Reverse Wire Account field on the Account tab in the Client Details form will not allow users to make an entry in this field if the active client is set up for internal ACH processing on the System Parameters form.) Note: You cannot make changes to a reverse wire payroll whose payment has been marked as received because the funds were already sent. (These payrolls display with green checkmarks, marking them as locked Payment Received payrolls when viewing them in the SuperBatch and Process Payroll forms.) Creating Payroll Processing Schedules Use the Processing Schedules form to establish payroll processing information for your organization. The processing schedule is set for each client on the Client Details Control tab.

To set up a payroll processing schedule: 1. Enter the pay Processing Schedule ID. If you are creating a new schedule, enter something brief but descriptive, such as STD. 2. Enter a brief Description for this pay schedule, such as Standard. 3. Enter the Remote Entry Cutoff Days Prior to Pay Day, which is the number of days prior to the pay day when the client must submit time sheet information.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 68 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

  1. Enter the Remote Entry Deadline, which is the time when the client must complete time sheet entry on the cutoff day.
  2. Enter the Delivery Days Prior to Pay Day, which is the number of days prior to the pay day that your organization must deliver checks/advices to the client.
  3. Select Skip Weekends to skip weekend days. Any count that crosses a weekend goes back two additional days. For example, if the cutoff is five days before the pay date and the pay date is a Tuesday, then the cutoff day is the previous Tuesday (five days back, skipping the two weekend days). If the schedule does not skip weekends, the cutoff day would be Thursday (five days back, including the weekend).
  4. Click Save.

To define delivery method for shipping: 1. Enter the Code for the delivery method. If you are creating a new code, use something brief but descriptive, for example, USPS or FEDX. 2. Enter the Method description, which is usually the name for the service (for example, US Postal Service or FedEx). 3. Enter the Days In Transit, which is the delivery method’s number of days in transit. 4. Enter the Bill Event Code, which is the ID of the billing event that the system uses to track this delivery method. If there is no charge for the delivery method, leave this field blank. 5. Select Create Spec Sheet to indicate that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. Do not select this option if a special sheet is not necessary.

  1. If a special sheet will print:
    1. Enter the Special Message that prints on the sheet.
    2. Enter the Name that should appear on the sheet.
    3. Enter the Address to print on the sheet.
    4. Enter the City, State, Zip Code to print on the sheet.
  2. Select the Delivery Sheet Format, which ensures that the address on the printed delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses. You can select one of the following: • The Standard and Expanded options display no line or indent adjustment fields when selected, and the delivery sheet prints the entered data in a fixed position. • The Large Window, Large Window (Expanded), Large Window - 1 Page, and Large Window - 1 Page (Expanded) options display adjustment fields for Delivery Sheet Address Line and Deliver Sheet Address Indent. The delivery sheet prints the entered data using these specified adjustments. • The 2 Window, 2 Window (Expanded), 2 Window - 1 Page, and 2 Window - 1 Page (Expanded) options display adjustment fields for Delivery Sheet Address Line, Deliver Sheet Address Indent, Client Information Line, and Client Information Indent. The delivery sheet prints the entered data using the specified adjustments. • The 2 Window (Shipping on Page 2) and 2 Window (Expanded) (Shipping on Page 2) options, in addition to the adjustment fields described above, print the address on the first piece of paper and the Special Message on the second sheet. The purpose is that the person who is preparing the envelopes can insert the address into the envelope and then read the instructions on the second page (what type of envelope to use, which mail bin to place the envelope in, and so on). Note: If you select one of the 2 Window formats, you must enter the full address.
  3. Click Save. After changing these settings, you can rerun the delivery sheet report from the Payroll Summary form, if needed.

Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup There are items required for set up at the client level.

Defining Billing Rules Client billing can be bundled or unbundled: • Bundled billing charges a lump sum percentage of gross payroll per pay period. It includes FUTA, SUTA, FICA, and workers’ compensation. • Unbundled billing breaks out each line item charge for payroll taxes, workers’ comp premiums, and administrative fees.

Note: The billing method (bundled or unbundled) does not affect the invoice format. Both the bill format and the billing template are set on the Billing tab in the Client Details form.

After defining billing rules, you can begin to enter other billing settings on the Billing tab on the Client Details form.

Using Bundled Billing Rules Use the Bundled Billing Rules form to establish information for charging one fee per workers’ compensation class for FUTA, SUTA, FICA, and workers’ compensation. You can “bundle” benefit billing based on the workers’ compensation code. You can use the Bundled Billings Comp Class workers’ compensation code to reflect actual costs that are based on workers’ compensation classifications. You can also set up bundled billing so that each Comp Class has the same billing rate, such as when a client has a flat rate for all classes of employees.

To set up bundled billing: 1. Select Client. 2. From Client|Change, select Billing Rules (Bundled). 3. Fill in these fields as required.

Using Unbundled Bill Rules Based On Options You can use these options as the basis for calculating unbundled billing rules. Note the following: • If you define rules based on the Employee Minimums and Employee Maximum, the system uses only one rule per voucher. • If you define one rule with Invoice Minimum, and another with Invoice Maximum, the system uses only one rule per payroll.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 81 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

• If a Per Active Employee Per Month (PAEPM) rule is already active for a client, you cannot create another PAEPM rule for that client using the same rule dates. (A warning displays if you try to create another PAEPM rule using the same rule dates, which would make them active at the same time.) Use the Based On options as follows:

Based On Calculation Units Enter the flat amount to calculate per unit paid. For example, one unit of bonus pay with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00) generates a $10.00 admin fee. Hours Worked Enter the flat amount to calculate per hour worked. For example, 40 hours worked with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00) generates a $400.00 admin fee. Percent of Wages Enter the percent of wages to charge. For example, $1270.00 of gross wages with a Rate amount of 10 (10%) generates a $127.00 admin fee. Amt per Check (One Per Enter the flat amount to bill per check. For example, 100 vouchers Voucher will Fire) with a Rate amount of 1 ($1.00) generates a $100.00 admin fee. Flat Amount Bills the client this amount for each employee and each check. For example, two employees and three total checks (one employee receives two checks) with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00) generates a $30.00 Admin fee. Flat Amount / Invoice Bills the client this amount per invoice generated. For example, two invoices and a Rate amount of 50 ($50.00) generates a $100.00 Admin fee. Flat Amount / Paid EE (only Triggers the flat amount only once per employee in the payroll once per EE) batch. For example, if an employee receives a regular, supplemental, and vacation voucher on the same payroll, the billing rule triggers only once. If there were two employees and four total vouchers with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00), the system generates a $20.00 Admin fee.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 82 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

Based On Calculation Flat Amount / Paid EE sets Determines an invoice minimum based on an amount per employee. IMIN basis. For example, if the Rate amount is 7.5, then two employees, one (Must also have 0 IMIN) with $7.00 admin fee and another with $10.00 admin fee would not trip the value of $15.00. (If you selected Based On Employee Minimum, the first employee would generate a $0.50 fee, and there would be no fee for the second employee.) Note the following: • If you define one rule with Monthly Rate/52 weeks, and another with Monthly Rate/48 weeks, the system uses only one per voucher. • The Flat Amount / Paid EE sets IMIN basis. (Must also have 0 IMIN) and Invoice Minimum = Only One of these options must be the last billing rules that the system calculates. If either exists as a Billing Rule, the system will resort the rules so they calculate last.

Flat Amount / Benefit Plan Triggers the flat amount based on the classification selected from Class the Benefit Plan Class drop-down. Monthly Rate / 52 Weeks Enter the monthly rate to charge; the system divides it by pay period based on 52 weeks a year per employee. For example, if the Rate amount is 65, the system bills the client $15.00 per employee for a weekly payroll. This does not limit the billing to $65.00 per month. If an employee receives multiple vouchers and the voucher type is not limited, more than $65.00 can be charged in a month. Monthly Rate / 48 Weeks Enter the monthly rate to charge; the system divides it by pay period based on 48 weeks a year per employee. For example, if the Rate amount is 65, the system bills the client $16.25 per employee for a weekly payroll. Employee Minimum Bills the minimum amount on each voucher for each employee. For example, if the rule has a Rate amount of 25 and an employee receives three vouchers (regular, supplemental, and vacation), the system bills the client $75 for that employee. Employee Minimum, NO For example, if the employee minimum is $10.00, but a client pays Credit On Overbills only $7.50 because they had $2.50 in overlimit credits, the system assesses a $2.50 charge. (Employee Minimum would not assess a fee.)

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 83 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

Based On Calculation Employee Maximum The maximum per voucher per employee that will be billed. For example; a user could set up one rule as a percent of wages and a second rule with an employee maximum, and the system would limit the calculation to the employee maximum. If rule #1 is set up as 20% of wages, and the wages are $2000, then rule #1 calculates at $400. If rule #2 is set up with an employee maximum of $25, then the system limits the admin fee to $25 even though rule #1 was calculated at $400. Invoice Minimum Any admin fee below this amount increases to this amount. Invoice Maximum Any admin fee above this amount reduces to this amount. Invoice Minimum (incl Zero Can be used in conjunction with Invoice Minimum. Invoice) Per Employee Per Month Bills automatically the first payroll after the billing rule is set up and automatically bills on the first payroll of each month following. It only bills for employees that are paid within that pay period. • If there is a new hire on the next payroll, the system will bill for just that employee. • If an employee was not paid on the first payroll of the month but gets paid on the next payroll, the system will bill for just that employee. Percent of Listed Benefit Takes the benefit entered in Benefit Plan and charges this percent against the total amount. For example, 10% of a $1000 benefit (with employee paying $500) would be $100. Percent of Listed Benefit Net Takes the benefit listed and charges this percent against the net Billed to Client amount. For example, 10% of a $1000 benefit (with employee paying $500) would be $50. Percent of Retirement Match Charges a percentage of the Match Fees. Amount Percent to Not Shelter Percentage that will not be sheltered as a benefit from FICA. A Benefit Plan from FICA sheltered amount shelters the whole amount from FICA for billing purposes, so use this option when you want to pass some of the savings through, but not all of them. Flat Amount Based on Charges a flat amount once per Benefit Plan. Benefit Rule

This feature uses a special tier table with three columns: • Tiered From: Smallest number of employees in this tier • Tiered To: Largest number of employees in this tier • Tiered Rate: Admin fee to charge per employee in this tier Add a row to the table for each calculation tier. Flat Amt based on Count Use this method to charge a flat amount per voucher. Specify the rule limiters in the Additional Conditions form’s Rule Minimum and Rule Maximum fields. For example, you need to bill the client at two different rates, based on the number of employees. You would establish two rules using Flat Amt based on Count. Set up the first rule with a Rate of $35, the Rule Minimum set to 0, and the Rule Maximum set to 5. Set up the second rule with a Rate of $100, a Rule Minimum of 6, and a Rule Maximum of 99. When there are five employees or fewer in the batch control record, PrismHR uses the first rule: four employee result in a bill for $140. For a batch with 6-99 employees, the system uses the second rule: six employees result in a bill for $600. Flat Amt based on Count Per Use this method to charge the client a certain amount for the first X Tier number of vouchers and then a different amount for the next X number of vouchers. Specify the tiers for the rule in the Additional Conditions form’s Rule Minimum and Rule Maximum fields. For example, you need to bill one rate for the first five employees, and then at another rate for every employee after that. You would establish two rules using Flat Amt based on Count Per Tier. Set up the first rule with the Rate of $35, the Rule Minimum set to 0, and the Rule Maximum set to 5. Set up the second rule with a Rate of $100, with a Rule Minimum of 6, and a Rule Maximum of 99. The system calculates the first five employees using the first rule, and the sixth employee using the second rule, resulting in a bill for $275 ((5$35)+(1$100)).

If your organization would prefer that it run in January, set the Rule Start Date to a date in January of the next year. This rule generates a miscellaneous billing charge. Annual Fee per W-2 Use this method to generate a one-time yearly charge for W-2s as a per-employee fee. This billing rule is based on a count of generated W-2s. W-2s are generated in the first quarter of the following year (for example, your organization will generate 2024 W-2s in Q1 2025). If W-2s have not been generated yet (such as in early January), then the system processes the rule during each payroll until your organization generates the W-2s. This rule generates a miscellaneous billing charge. Minimum Bill for Code 005 Any amount below this value increases to this value.

Based On Calculation Per Active Employee Per This option calculates the admin fee based on the client’s employee Month count on the first regular payroll of the month, using a tiered charge format. (The second payroll captures any new employees.) The fee is based on the total number of active employees in the client associated with the first payroll of the month. This feature uses a special tier table with three columns: • Tiered From (smallest number of employees in this tier) • Tiered To (largest number of employees in this tier) • Tiered Rate (admin fee to charge per employee in this tier) Add a row to the table for each calculation tier. Enabling the Per Active Employee Per Month option bills active employees for the month. For example, if the first payroll of the month has 100 active employees, they will be billed for 100 employees. On the second payroll if there is a new hire and a termination, they will still be billed for one employee on that payroll, since the new hire needs to be billed and the termination was active for part of the month. Note: An edge case could occur that is currently not supported. When you calculate a payroll, the system determines the number of employees that are active at that time and once the payroll is posted, it commits counts to the employee records. If you calculate the payroll and add several employees or terminate employees and then post without recalculating, the system misses the new employees added/removed in the billing cycle. Note the following: • The billing rate calculates the tier rate for the employee count. • The admin fee bills the entire month at the same rate.

Establishing Pay Groups Use the Pay Groups form to set up a group of employees who are all paid on the same day. You must assign every employee in PrismHR to a pay group. Use the Actions menu to access other information and setup forms: • Audit. • Pay Schedule Report – runs the Pay Schedule Report. • Pay Schedules. • Show employees – lists employees enrolled in the pay group. • Time Sheet Defaults – defines default pay methods and pay codes for this group. When the timesheet is created, the system populates the default hours in the listed default pay code for employees assigned to that pay method. For example, if the pay method is Hourly and the pay code is REG2 in the Time Sheet Defaults panel, then employees with the Hourly pay method will have their default hours populated in the REG2 pay code in the timesheet. Note the following: • The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. • After you enable the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code and select the Variable Salary option, this update takes effect in the next regularly scheduled payroll.

Performing Pre-ACH Maintenance Use the Pre-ACH Maintenance panel to test ACH files a specified number of days before running payroll to ensure that all transactions can be completed.

Note: See the ACH User Guide for more information.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 101 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

To set up or maintain Pre-ACH settings for a pay group: 1. Make sure to specify the appropriate pay group. Its information populates on the form. 2. If appropriate, select the number of Pre-ACH Days. The system sends a pre-ACH file ahead of the regular ACH file by the number of days selected. This number must be less than the cycle length for the feature to work correctly. If your organization is not using pre-ACH processing for this pay group, you must set this field to –Select–.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 102 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

  1. The system can use either an average or a flat amount for the pre-ACH:

Pre-ACH Amount Details Type Average Use the pre-ACH invoice fields to specify an average for up to five invoices. You can enter any information in the Pre-ACH Invoice Number and Pre-ACH Invoice Amount columns, because the system does not verify it. For example, if you are setting up a pre-ACH prenote on the client for the first time and plan to use five invoices for the average that will typically be around $10,000, you can enter five “starter” invoices using any invoice number (for example, START1, START2, START3, and so on) and enter $10,000 for each. When the system processes a real payroll, it drops the first starter invoice from the list and inserts a real invoice at the end. After the first five payrolls, all the starter invoices are no longer on the list. The system sends pre-ACH prenotes using the average of the invoices in the list. After five payrolls, the average will be based on actual data. • The system lists each Pre-ACH Invoice Number in the chain for seeking the current average to pre-ACH. You can enter different invoice numbers. • The Pre-ACH Invoice Amount is each invoice’s contribution amount. You can enter a different amount to force a new average. The Current Average displays below the table. Flat Enter the Pre-ACH Override to use a flat amount rather than the Current Average of invoices and amounts. If you use the flat method, the system always uses that amount for pre-ACH for the client and this pay group. The system never checks nor averages the invoice amounts.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 103 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

  1. If setting up Pre-ACH for the first time, enter the batch number of any completed batch in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field. For each pay group, the daily Pre-ACH program compares the in-progress batch number with the batch number entered in this field. If these are identical, the system skips the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH processing. When you enter the ID of a previously completed batch, you indicate that PrismHR needs to process the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH. The system will evaluate the in-progress batch for processing, create the appropriate ACH entries, and automatically update this field with the in-progress batch number. This prevents double entries from occurring.

Note: In the case where Pre-ACH entries were already created for a batch, but this batch was later deleted and re-created (therefore giving it a new batch number), you must manually update this field with the new batch number. For example, assume a Pre-ACH prenote was sent for batch 202202, but for some reason you decided to delete that batch and create the next regular payroll batch to replace it. If the system assigns number 202205 to the new batch, you must change the value in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field from 202202 to 202205. This ensures that PrismHR does not re-transmit the Pre-ACH entry.

  1. Click Save.

Moving Employees from One Pay Group to Another Use this feature to change the pay group for the client’s employees at one time and update their standard default hours. For example, you can use this feature if the client changes from a semi-monthly pay period with 86.67 standard hours to a bi-weekly pay period with 80 hours. This feature also allows you to add employees to a payroll in progress for the To Pay Group. Before you begin, make sure the new pay group is set up for the client and that a payroll batch exists. see Establishing Pay Groups on page 99.

To move the client’s employees from one pay group to another, do the following: 1. Enter the From Pay Group ID that you need to change. One of two messages displays: • The system notifies you that employees will not be removed from an active payroll, and states that you will need to delete and recreate the batch in progress; you will do this in step 11. • The system notifies you that the employees are not in an active payroll and alerts you that they will not be added to a payroll automatically. You need to do this manually in step 12. 2. Enter the To Pay Group ID that you need to apply. The New Pay Period displays.

It displays additional information that also applies (for example, the system will not add new hires whose start date is after the pay period end date of the new payroll). Once the process is complete, there are additional updates that you need to make.

For each override: • Enter the When Prefix/Suffix term to override, for example, DEPARTMENT. • Enter the is equal to value, for example, ACCT. • Enter the replace with value to use instead, for example, 700. Account Overrides If the G/L account requires an account override, enter that information in the Account Overrides panel. 6. For each override: • Select the When Field Equals term to override, for example, LOCATION. • Enter the is equal to value, for example, MAIN. • Enter the replace account with value to use instead, for example, 6000.10. Copying ASO Accounting Setup Data To help reduce the manual labor and margin for error associated with a manual entry, you can copy all ASO accounting setup data from one client to another using the Copy G/L To Another Client section.

To copy ASO accounting setup data from one client to another: 1. In the Copy G/L To Another Client section, enter or select the Client ID. If you select the Client ID, the Select Client list displays. Search for the client by entering the Client ID or Client Name, then filter the selection further by selecting the Service Type and Status. The clients that match your entry display. 2. After you select a client, that entry displays back in the Copy G/L To Another Client section. 3. Select Copy G/L to Client. Note the following: • If the client you select contains any existing data in the ASO Accounting Codes, ASO G/L Account Setup, or ASO Global G/L Account Setup forms, when you select Copy G/L to Client the following message displays, “Client already has existing data for ASO Accounting Codes, ASO G/L Account Setup or ASO Global G/L Account Setup. Data cannot be copied over existing records.” Therefore, you cannot continue with this process. • If the client you select does not contain any existing data in the ASO Accounting Codes, ASO G/L Account Setup, and ASO Global G/L Account Setup forms, when you select Copy G/L to Client the following confirmation message displays, “You are about to copy the G/L setup from client to client <selected Client ID.> This will copy over any existing values from ASO Accounting Codes, ASO G/L Account Setup form, and ASO Global G/L Account Setup form. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to copy the ASO accounting setup data. • If you select Copy G/L to Client without selecting a Client ID the following message displays, “Select a client to continue.” • If you select the active client ID as the copy to client the following message displays, “Copy from and copy to client cannot be the same.” 4. After clicking Yes in the confirmation message, the copy process starts. Note the following: • The process copies all ASO Accounting Codes records, including all records set up on the ASO G/L Account setup form and all records set up on the ASO Global G/L Account setup forms for the active client to the selected client. • The process is only successful when there is no existing data for the three forms, ASO Accounting Codes, ASO G/L Account Setup, and ASO Global G/L Account Setup forms, in the copy to the client.

Setting Up Per Diem Wages This section describes how to set up driver per diem wages in PrismHR that are particular to the trucking industry. You can define per diem wages using one of three methods: • Percentage method: Total wages are entered as a whole and PrismHR breaks this information down into taxable wages and non-taxable per diem wages. The percentage used to calculate the non-taxable per diem amount is set up at the Position or Department level. • Mileage method: The client reports the total mileage. The pay rate per mile varies by tier and is broken into taxable wages and non-taxable per diem wages. Both the taxable and non-taxable per diem wages are defined as rate per mile. • Daily method: The client reports the total wages, along with the number of days each individual driver has been out. The system takes the number of days out that the user enters and multiplies it by the per day amount. The daily amount is set up on an individual employee basis.

Percentage Method Use the Pay Codes form to create a per diem Percentage method pay code. 1. Open the Pay Codes form (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Enter a per diem Percentage Pay Code and Pay Description for your organization. 3. Complete the fields in the Pay Code, Per Diem Method Rules, and Billing Code panels as appropriate.

  1. Click Save. Use the Payroll tab of the Client Details form to set up a client company for per diem.
  2. Open Client Details form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change).
  3. Select the Payroll tab.
  4. Select Department or Position from the Per Diem Rate Source drop-down for the per diem calculation.

• If you selected Department in step 7, use the Departments form to define a per diem percentage: a. Open the Departments form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). b. Enter the Department Code to which this per diem percentage applies. c. Enter the Per Diem Percent, which is the percentage of pay to allocate to non-taxable per diem for this department.

  1. Click Save. • If you selected Position in step 7, use the Positions form to define a per diem percentage.

O Method FLSA Calculation of D/T Hours In California, double-time (D/T) hours are paid at one times the regular rate of pay. When there are more than two rates of pay or non-discretionary income, the weighted average method is used for calculation premium pay or HALF pay. Your organization can set up the system to allow for the 50% premium pay calculation for the D/T pay code, thus including D/T in the weighted average at one times the regular rate, and the DT1 pay code (for straight double- time pay) then calculates at one time the weighted average rate. Your organization can use a DT1 pay code as the regular double-time pay code using the 1x pay rate, and DTPREM as the premium double pay code, with a rate that is 1x the calculated weighted average rate for the O- type FLSA Rulesets. 1. Set up the DT1 pay code so that the Add to D/T Hours (Threshold) option is selected.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 157 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

  1. Set up the DTPREM pay code as required.

  2. Set up an FLSA Ruleset where: • The Reporting Method is set to (O) Overtime Hours Reported Separately. • The Premium Pay Code is set to HALF. • The Double Premium Pay Code is set to DTPREM.

  3. In PrismHR, enter the ruleset ID in the FLSA Ruleset field of the Client Details Payroll tab.

  4. Enter the FLSA Work Week Ends On day.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 158 Chapter 3 Company-Level Setup

  1. The next payroll will calculate correctly.

Note: Note that the payroll’s period end date must coincide with the FLSA Work Week Ends On day.

This process includes: • Setting up Cachet as your ACH Originator • Creating a bank account for the client • Creating/adjusting your existing payroll checking account • Assigning the checking account to client companies

Setting Up Cachet as Your ACH Originator In order to set up Cachet as an ACH Originator, you must first confirm that consolidated ACH file processing is enabled.

To enable consolidated ACH file processing, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. Select System Parameters under System|Change. The System Parameters form opens. 2. In the Consolidated ACH File Processing Used field, select Yes, if it is not already selected. Once this setting has been confirmed, begin the process of setting up ACH Originators. 3. Click Back Office. Select ACH Originators under System|Change. The ACH Originators form opens.

(Note: Do not enter spaces in this field.) Processing Bank ID Enter or select the bank routing number for your bank. Processing Company ID Enter your Federal IRS Number (FEIN), beginning with the number 1. For example, if your FEIN number is “240000054,” then enter 1240000054. Processing Company Name Enter your company name as the PEO. ACH File Options Select the Put Company ID on ACH file detail lines position 40-54 option. Third Party Format Select Cachet.

Chapter 4 Import Definition Files You must set up definitions before you can import files.

WARNING: You cannot import native Microsoft Excel (.xls) files. Data errors will occur. You can import only tab-delimited, comma-separated values (.csv), or fixed format data files.

Setting Up Pay Import Definitions Use the Pay Import Definition form to set up pay data import definitions from tab-delimited, comma-delimited (CSV), or fixed-length data import files.

Note: After you create a pay import definition, you assign it to the appropriate client(s) in the Time Sheet tab of the Client Details form.

Defining Time Sheet Pay Import Definition Parameters Define the parameters required to import the pay data from the file in the Time Sheet Pay Import Definition panel.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 165 Chapter 4 Import Definition Files

To set up pay data import definitions: 1. Enter the Definition ID for the pay import. • If you are creating a new import definition, use something descriptive, such as the name of the client that generates the data import file; the ID cannot include spaces. Also enter a short Description in the second field. • You can copy an existing definition to use as the basis for a new definition. Open the Actions menu and select Copy. Note: You can only create and save a New Definition ID using the following characters: numbers zero through nine, lowercase letters a through z, and capitalized letters A through Z. Otherwise, an error message displays. 2. Select Hourly Only to load only hourly employees from the import file. The system reports any salaried employees included in the file as download exceptions. 3. In the File Format field, select a format for the data import: • Delimited—data is separated by a demiliter • Fixed-Length—data is grouped together without spaces If you select Delimited, select a delimiter from the Delimiter drop-down: • Tab—space between data • Comma—comma (,) between data • Pipe—pipe (|) between data 4. If necessary, enter the Number of Header Lines To Skip. This setting skips any header content lines in the import file, and begins the import after that. For example, if the first line in the file has the column headings, and the second line is the first record, enter 1. 5. Select Rates Have Four Decimal Places if the pay rates have four decimal places. 6. Select Allow Zero Pay On Time Sheets to pass zero amounts to the time sheet.

WARNING: Do not use the Special Processing Routine fields unless directed to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

  1. Enter the Special Processing Routine to use to convert the import file.
  2. Enter the Special Routine after Import for the system to execute immediately after importing the file from DOS; this can reformat the file.
  3. Enter the Post Processing Routine to execute at the end of the import process.

Note: You must select All Special Routines Using Message Format if this is a web-based import. If this parameter is not selected, do not select it unless directed to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

  1. Select All Special Routines Using Message Format if the system uses a routine to pass back status and message information.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 166 Chapter 4 Import Definition Files

  1. Select Show Original File Data in Error Report if the error report should show the complete line of data from the original file.
  2. From the Use STD Allocation On drop-down, select the standard allocation to use for time.

Indicating Outcome of Existing Data After Data Import Use the When Posting Imported Data to Time Sheets panel to indicate what happens to any existing data after a data import.

  1. From the Clear Existing Pay From Time Sheets for drop-down, select how to manage existing information: • All Employees: Clears all pay information for all employees in a batch when the file imports. • Employees in Import File Only: Employee data in the import file overwrites any existing data only for those employees. If other employee data exists in the payroll batch, their data is preserved. • None: No data is cleared.

Note: If you chose to clear existing pay (All Employees or Employees in Import File Only), you can only select Overwrite existing amounts from the Update existing pay on time sheets drop-down. If you chose not to clear existing data (None), then you can choose a method for how to handle existing pay.

  1. From the Update existing pay on time sheets drop-down, select whether the imported data overwrites any existing pay data or adds to it.
  2. Select Auto Add Option (when employee is in file import but not on payroll) to have the system automatically add active employee time sheets. • Auto Add Active Employees to Payroll: The system automatically adds the time sheets for all active employees. There are some instances where employees will not be added: • The employee’s onboarding is still in progress. • It is a regular or special batch and the employee’s pay group is not included. • It is a manual batch. • Auto Add All Employees to Payroll: The system automatically adds all employees to the time sheet. This affects employees who were terminated and re-hired. They need to be paid but have not yet been re- hired in the system. They must also be assigned to the pay group in the import. • Do Not Auto Add: The system will not automatically add active employees.

Payroll Setup Guide © 2026 PrismHR 167 Chapter 4 Import Definition Files

  1. Select Recalculate Overtime Pay Rate to have the system recalculate overtime pay rates (based on the rate multiplier) on imported overtime hours that use the definition. For example, an employee is included in the import with a pay rate of $10. If this option is not selected, then the employee will be paid $10. If this option is selected, then the employee will be paid at the overtime rate (such as $15 for a 1.5 multiplier). Note: If you enable Recalculate Overtime Pay Rate, make sure the import file has a pay rate for the corresponding overtime pay code. Otherwise, an error message displays, “Recalculate Overtime Pay Rate is checked for Import Definition but the overtime Pay Code does not have a corresponding Pay Rate on line which will result in an incorrect pay calculation.”

Defining Standard Pay Imports There are two methods for defining the pay import: • Mapping Data Import File Fields (page 168): Map pay codes from a time-keeping system to existing pay codes in PrismHR. • Mapping Data Import File (page 168): Import the pay data that has been prepared to match the client’s existing time sheet column headings in PrismHR.

Mapping Data Import File Fields Use the Import Field Definitions table to map the fields of the data import file to those in PrismHR.

To map the data import file fields: 1. Specify the fields in the file: • If the import file is tab- or comma-delimited, enter the Field #. • If the import file is fixed-length, enter the Start and End positions. 2. Select the Field Name of the field into which the data imports. The system skips any missing fields or applies a default value. 3. Use the Conversion Mask field only with direction from the PrismHR Customer Support Team. The system uses this value when data in the import file is in a non-native format.

Mapping Data Import File Use the Import Translation Table to map the data import file codes to those in PrismHR.

Chapter 1 Default Client Reporting Parameters The Report Parameters feature allows you to specify run-time parameters for some of the reports that print for this client when a user processes the payroll. The reports in the list are specified in the Client Details Payroll tab. Not all reports allow you to specify default parameters. The reports that do are listed below. The other reports have set parameters that you cannot customize for the client. • Defining Benefits Billing Report Parameters (page 10) • Setting Calculate Checks Report Parameters (page 12) • Setting Client Allocation Report Parameters (page 13) • Setting Deduction Register Report Parameters (page 26) • Setting Employee Check Acknowledgement Parameters (page 12) • Setting Fax Back Report Parameters (page 28) • Setting Payroll Allocation Report Parameters (page 31) • Setting Payroll Check Journal Report Parameters (page 33) • Setting Payroll Register Report Parameters (page 35) • Setting Payroll No Earnings Report Parameters (page 34) • Setting Workers’ Compensation Report Parameters (page 37)

Note: If a report is set at the global level, users can edit the default parameters from the main Client menu.

Related Topic Client Details in Client Administration User Guide Global Payroll Reports in System Administration Guide

Payroll Reports © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Default Client Reporting Parameters

Defining Benefits Billing Report Parameters Important! The Benefits Billing Report Parameters form, which was accessible from the Client|Change menu, has been retired. Instead, we recommend using the Benefits Billing Detail Report form, which provides helpful sorting options and filters to determine what displays in the Benefits Billing Detail Report.

Defining Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters You can set up the Certified Payroll Report to automatically run with payroll. Use the Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters form to define the format parameters for this report.

Note: This report executes only for regularly scheduled, weekly payrolls (AUTORUN version), and displays information about wages and payroll for all employees. It does not execute for the ON-DEMAND version.

To define the Certified Payroll Report format parameters: 1. Go to the Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters form and complete the following fields.

 Field Name                        Description
 Format                            Select the Format from the drop-down.
                                   Note: Currently, this report only supports the Federal Government
                                   version.
 Include Gender on the Report      Select Include Gender on the Report, if needed.
 Include Ethnicity                 Select Include Ethnicity, if needed.
 Include Employee Address          Select Include Employee Address, if needed.
 Employee Identifier               Select an Employee Identifier you want to use in the report: (Full Social
                                   Security Number, Last Four Digits of Social, Employee ID, or None).
 Show zero work weeks              Select this field to include projects that did not have any work to display
                                   in the Certified Payroll Report, essentially providing you with a zero
                                   report (all amounts listed in the report display as zero). If you do not
                                   select this field and there was no project work during the requested
                                   date, an error message displays.
 Show extended rate of pay up      Select this field to display the pay rate in the same format that displays
 to 4 decimal places               on vouchers, which display up to four decimal places.
 Allocate Deductions/Taxes by      Select Allocate Deductions/Taxes by Project to calculate deductions and
 Project                           taxes. Selecting this field sets the calculation to allocate by project total.
                                   When unchecked, the allocation is based on gross pay.
  1. Click Save.

Setting Calculate Checks Report Parameters Use the Calculate Checks Report Parameters form to determine the order in which information prints on the report.

Note: These are the settings for the reports that the system generates during payroll processing as well as the defaults for users running the report. When running the on-demand version of the report, users can select other options at runtime (depending on their user role security settings).

To set the Calculate Checks Report parameters: 1. Use the Sort Parameters to determine the primary and secondary sorts for the report. 2. Use Employee Sort to determine whether the report should sort the employees by name or ID. 3. Click Save.

Setting Employee Check Acknowledgement Parameters Use the Check Acknowledgement Report Parameters form to specify the default parameters that the system should use when printing the Check Acknowledgement Report for this client.

To set the employee Check Acknowledgement parameters: 1. Select the field that the report should Sort By. 2. Select Include Direct Deposit Advice to include the advice for direct deposits. 3. Select Include Hours to include the hours employees worked on the report.

Setting Client Allocation Formats You can use the Client Allocation Formats form to set the presentation of each column in the Client Allocation Report (see Client Allocation Report). Formatting options include: • Selects the applicable client bill format if tied to a client bill or another format describing the allocation columns. • Specifies whether to include an employee totals column. • Adds, inserts, and deletes columns and shows them as tabs in the header area. • Adds text for up to two header lines for each column. • Creates and deletes allocation codes and descriptions.

Note: If you try to delete an existing client allocation report format, a warning displays and prompts for confirmation. If your user role has Inquiry access to the form, all options except for Summary Report and Cancel are disabled. However, you can still select a format code and click a header to show the various allocations associated with it.

Formatting a Report To access this form and format a report:

  1. Click Back Office .
  2. From System|Change, click Client Allocation Formats.
  3. Set a Format Code in either of the following ways: • Enter a value in the text box. • Click the Format Code link to open the Select Allocation Format selector. Then type a code to search or select an existing code from the list.
  4. Enable Include Employee Total Column to add a column titled Employee Total as the last column in the report. The value is the total of all appropriate columns for each employee.
  5. From the Report Columns panel, click + Add Column. Column Header fields and an Allocation Code grid appear. Generally, up to 10 columns can fit in a page in Landscape orientation. Additional columns appear in the exported report but may not be visible in a print-out. When a column is first added, its tab is associated

with a number, such as Column 1, Column 2, and so forth. You are directed to the new column once it's
created.

Copying an Existing Format Code You can duplicate an existing format code and its formatting using the Copy feature. Note: The Copy button is disabled until you enter or select a Format Code.

To copy an existing format code: 1. Enter or select a Format Code. 2. Click Copy. The Copy Client Allocation Format form displays. 3. Enter a new format code in the Enter a code for the new format field. Note: If you enter an existing format code an error message displays, “Format code already exists. If appropriate, update the new format code’s information, then click Save.

Setting Overtime Report Parameters Use the Overtime Report Parameters form to determine the data to be included in the Overtime Report, including specific pay codes. (See Overtime Report on page 136.) For example:

Payroll Reports © 2026 PrismHR 29 Chapter 1 Default Client Reporting Parameters

Note the following: • This feature is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Overtime Report Parameters form. • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Overtime Report Parameters form displays the form in read-only format. • This form does not use Client Access Group security. • This form does not produce an Audit log.

To set up overtime report parameters:

  1. Click Back Office .
  2. On the System|Change menu, select Overtime Report Parameters. The Overtime Report Parameters form displays.
  3. Enable Include Expense Reimbursements in Regular Earnings to include expense reimbursements in the YTD Regular column in the report.
  4. Enable Include Fringe Benefits in Regular Earnings to include fringe benefit pay amounts in the YTD Regular column in the report.
  5. Enable Include Salaried Employees on Report to include salaried employees in the report.
  6. If necessary, enter each pay code in the Overtime Pay Codes (Optional) field to include in the Batch Overtime column amount in the report. The pay code description displays.
  7. If necessary, enter each earnings pay code in the Earnings Pay Codes (Optional) field to determine what pay and hours will be included in the report. The earnings pay code description displays.
  8. Click Save.

Viewing the Job Control Status Report When a process is complete, you may have the option to access a Job Control Status report. This report shows the Job Number, the date and time when it started and stopped, and the job status. It also shows the date and time that each step in the process was executed. To open the Job Control Status report, click Report in the message that informs you that processing is complete. You have the following options: • Navigate through multiple pages using arrows to move forward, back, to the beginning, or to the end. • Go directly to a page by typing the page number in the Page box. • Enter search text in the Search box. Click Search Next to find the next occurrence. • In the Actions menu, select Print, Convert to PDF, or Print/PDF Pages. • Click XLS to export the report to Excel format and save it in your Downloads folder.

During reconciliation and quarterly tax processing, use the Client Federal Entity Tax Register Report to output client entity tax registers and identify whether or not values are spread across one or more employers. To access this report, go to Payroll|Report|Client Federal Tax Register Report.

Procedure To run the report: 1. Enter a Year. 2. If necessary, select a Quarter to view data from that quarter, or select YTD Only to display all data from the start of the year to the current date. 3. Enter a Tax Code: • 00-10: Federal Income Tax • 00-11: Medicare – Employee • 00-12: Social Security – Employee • 00-15: Medicare – Employer • 00-16: Social Security – Employer • 00-17: FUTA – Employer 4. In the Include SBEA Wage Code Breakout field, select: • No: does not display F codes on the report • Yes: displays F codes on the report 5. Specify an Employer ID to restrict the report to Client Federal Entities under that employer. 6. In the Report Type field, select either Employee Detail to generate the full report, or Summary to generate only the F code subtotals by tax code. 7. In the Client Federal Entity (CFE) field, enter specific CFE IDs to include in the report. If this field is blank, the report includes all CFE IDs. 8. Select Run. The report displays.

Employee Period Pay and Hours Audit Report Use this form to generate a global report for any employee that has Standard Hours/Annual Hours or Period Pay/Annual Pay that doesn’t match to their Pay Period Standard hours or logical annual pay rate.

Example: If hourly employee pay period is Weekly so they should have 40 standard hours and their hourly rate should equal an annual rate of hourly rate times 2080. If an employee’s standard hours are something different than 40 or their annual or period pay does not equal the appropriate hourly rate times annual hours, then they appear on this report with Yes in the Review column to indicate review of that item.

FLSA Classification Analysis Report Your organization would use this report to determine whether employees are classified correctly. FLSA types are intended only to indicate which FLSA test employees in this position are subject to. This is for the purpose of reporting and, in the future, warning purposes. An FLSA type of “exempt” indicates that there is no compensation test for this position. In other words, any employee with such a position satisfies the FLSA compensation tests regardless of their compensated. This selection does not replace or alter the FLSA Exempt field functionality.

Payroll Reports © 2026 PrismHR 97 Chapter 2 Reports

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report. If left blank, all employees display: • Enter each Position Classification in the order you want them to display on the report. The Description displays. • Select each FLSA Type in the order you want them to display on the report. • Standard: The position satisfies standard duties test, or is exempt from duties test but still subject to standard salary test. • Highly Compensated: The position satisfies the highly compensated duties test only. • Exempt: The position is exempt from the duties and salary tests (such as teachers, doctors, and lawyers). FLSA Exempt must be selected on Position Classification. • Select a Pay Group. The Description displays. • Select Yes for FLSA Exempt to show employees that are FLSA exempt. If you have not selected FLSA exempt and an FLSA type on Position Classification, the report applies Standard type. • Select Yes for Salaried to show employees whose pay method is Salary or Variable Salary. Note: The Variable Salary pay method option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. • Click the Payroll Number field to select posted (COMP) payrolls. The Show only employees with zero pay field displays after selecting a payroll number. Click this field to ensure the report only displays employees who had zero pay for the selected payroll number.
  2. If you want to treat commissioned employees like salaried employees on the report, select Treat Commissioned as Salaried.
  3. Click Run. The following report example displays all employees associated with a position classification:

The following report example displays all employees associated with a payroll number:

The report columns are: • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first. • ID: Employee ID • Position Classification: The employee’s classification for reporting purposes • Salaried (Y/N): Pay method is salary • Pay Group: The employee’s payment sequence. • FLSA Type: • S = Standard: The position satisfies the standard duties test, or is exempt from the duties test but is still subject to standard salary test. • H = Highly Compensated: The position satisfies the highly compensated duties test only • E = Exempt: The position is exempt from the duties and salary tests (such as teachers, doctors, and lawyers) • FLSA Exempt: FLSA Exempt must be selected on Position Classification • Annual Pay: Total pay for the year • FLSA Threshold: The annual compensation amount necessary, per FLSA type, to qualify as an exempt employee • Difference: Annual Pay subtracted from FLSA Threshold when Annual Pay is less then FLSA Threshold • Pct% Difference: Percent difference between FLSA Threshold and Annual Pay • Misclassified: Displays Y for employees who might be misclassified, N for employees who are classified correctly, or B if the FLSA standard can only be met if the employee is also compensated with non- discretionary bonus or incentive pay in addition to their base salary in the system. Displays O (Over Threshold) if the position earns enough to be flagged as FLSA exempt, but is not. This may or may not be an error, depending on your system setup.

FLSA Exempt Compensation Report As of December 1, 2016, the Department of Labor has increased the compensation thresholds necessary for FLSA exemption. For employees subject to the standard compensation test, these regulations allow employers to make up as much as 10% of the FLSA exemption requirement in any quarter with non-discretionary bonus, incentives, or commission pay within the quarter or first pay period thereafter.

Payroll Reports © 2026 PrismHR 99 Chapter 2 Reports

This report tests whether an FLSA exempt employee was sufficiently compensated or if additional compensation is necessary to meet the respective FLSA standard. You can use it for single pay periods, quarterly, or yearly analysis. The report applies either the standard compensation or highly compensated employee test. The standard test applies to any employee with a job / position classification without an FLSA exemption test type set (“FLSA Type”), as well as those set to standard.

  1. Enter the Selection Parameters to determine what displays on the report: Enter either the Pay Periods Ending Date range, a Quarter, or a Payroll Number. It is critical to capture scheduled pay periods in a quarter to know how much the employee should have been compensated. • Enter a Pay Periods Ending On or After date for the pay periods start date you want to review. Enter a Pay Periods Ending On or Before date for the pay periods end date you want to review. • Select a Quarter for the pay periods you want to review. • Click the Payroll Number field to select posted (COMP) payrolls. The Show only employees with zero pay field displays after selecting a payroll number. Click this field to ensure the report only displays employees who had zero pay for the selected payroll number.
  2. Select an FLSA Type, either Standard or Highly Compensated.
  3. State - Select the Work State of the employee/s from the drop-down for the Pay Period, Quarter or the Payroll Number. Leave this field blank if you want to display employees from all states for the Pay Period, Quarter or the Payroll Number.
  4. Minimum Standard Salary - For Standard FLSA Type, enter the minimum salary here.
  5. Minimum Highly Compensated Salary - For Highly Compensated FLSA Type, enter the minimum salary here.

Note: Depending on whether the employee is paid weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly or monthly, PrismHR will divide this Minimum Salary by 52 or 26 or 24 or 12 to get the Period Minimum. The Period Minimum multiplied by Pay Per Date Range (5 for a 5 day work week) will provide the Total Compensation Expected on the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report. The difference between the Total Compensation Expected and the Actual Total Compensation is the Deficiency on the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report.

  1. Select a Pay Group. (The Description displays after making this selection.)
  2. Click Run to display the report on-screen.
  3. Click Close to close this form at any time. The report columns are: • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first. • ID: Employee ID • Hire Date: The date the employee was hired.

Payroll Reports © 2026 PrismHR 100 Chapter 2 Reports

•    Status: Employee status; the report lists any employee who was active for any portion of the date range.
•    Position Code: The employee's job.
•    Work State: The state where the employee works.
•    Pay Group: The employee's payment sequence.
•    FLSA Type: Either S (standard) or H (highly compensated)
•    FLSA Exemption Category: If an employee's Position is marked as FLSA Exempt on the Employee Details
     form and has an associated FLSA Exemption Category indicated therein, it will now reflect in this report.
•    Pay Period: The employee's pay cycle, whether that is weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, or monthly.
•    Period Salary: The employee's annualized salary, as entered in PrismHR, per the appropriate pay cycle.
•    Period Minimum: The amount of compensation required each pay cycle for an employee to retain
     exemption.
•    Pay Per in Date Range: The number of scheduled, regular pay periods, that the employee was included
     in, with a period end date falling in the date range selected.
•    Total Compensation Expected: The period minimum multiplied by the number of pay periods in the date
     range.
•    Actual Total Compensation: Gross pay amount from all vouchers multiplied by the number of pay
     periods in the date range.
•    Deficiency: The total compensation expected minus actual total compensation; any employee that is at
     or over the FLSA threshold will have a 0 in this column.

Important notes about this report: • When run over multiple pay periods, this report will not indicate if an employee was appropriately compensated in a specific pay period. • The report does not validate when a payment is made. The non-discretionary bonus or incentive pay should be paid in a timely manner (for standard employees that would be by the first payroll after the end of the quarter). In order for “makeup compensation” to reflect accurately in this report, it must be issued in a separate payroll batch with a period end date in the quarter to which payment is attributed. If it is paid in a subsequent scheduled payroll batch after quarter end, it will not display in this report.

Filtering Client and Employer Data You can use the Include/Exclude panel to configure the client and employer data that displays on the PFML download. If you do not select an option, the default is Include. 4. In the table, enter the Employer IDs you want to include in, or exclude from, the download. 5. When you finish, you can Run the download.

Note: The Invoice Line Items and Bill Codes that display in the report are based on the client’s current Bill Format, which is set on the Billing tab on the Client Details form.

The following conditions have an effect on page breaking in the report: • The Invoice Break on Invoice One affects the Page Break option in the report; for example, if Invoice One has Invoice Break set to Department, then the Page Break on Department option will be available or, if Invoice One does not have an Invoice Break, then the Page Break option will not be available (or display). • If the Invoice Break for Invoice One is not one of the Invoice Sorts in Invoice One, the Page Break option will not be available (or display). • If Invoice One and Invoice Two have different items set for Invoice Break, the item on Invoice One will be the break item used in the report and displayed as the Page Break option. • Invoice Sort(s): A list of the Sort Items being used on the invoice for allocating amounts. Obtaining Time Off Carryover Loss for Employees You can use the Employee Carryover Loss form to produce a report that displays time off carryover lost for each employee from the previous year. For example, if employees can carryover up to 40 hours of time off and an employee has 60 hours available at the end of the year, the report would display 20 hours of lost time off carryover. Note: The report that the Employee Carryover Loss form produces does not apply to global time off.

To obtain time off carryover lost for each employee: 1. On the Reports menu, select Employee Loss Carryover under Payroll|Reports. 2. Select the Accrual Schedule. 3. Select the Time Off Plan. 4. Enter or select the As Of Date. 5. Click Run. The Time Off Carryover Loss Report displays. For example:

Payroll Reports © 2026 PrismHR 135 The report columns are: • Employee ID: Employee ID. • Employee Name: Employee name. • Accrual Schedule: The Time Off accrual schedule. • Time Off Plan: The Time Off plan. • Carryover Lost: Amount of employee’s time off carryover lost since As Of Date.
