Payroll Audit Report You can use the Payroll Audit Report to review a payroll before it is finalized and posted. After payroll has been initialized/calculated, the report compares the current payroll against the prior payroll and displays changes, outliers, and potential issues that warrant review. The Payroll Audit Report helps reduce the amount of time spent on manual payroll review and also helps payroll processors quickly identify what may have changed since the last pay period. Important! The output recorded in the Payroll Audit Report is generated using artificial intelligence (AI), so ensure you review all output for accuracy, completeness, and appropriateness before using it.

Accessing the Payroll Audit Report You can access the Payroll Audit Report on two forms after a payroll has been initialized/calculated:

• SuperBatch: The report displays with the other reports in the SuperBatch review workflow. (Click in the batch row. Payroll Audit is the first item in the payroll review menu that displays.) • Process Payroll: In the Selected Payroll panel, select Payroll Audit Report. (This button displays when the selected payroll status is INITCOMP, INITOK, or INITWARN.)

Records Select Records to display an Overview of issues the system has identified

Working with Archived Payroll Reports When payroll reports are created for a posted payroll they fall into two types, those that are “set in stone” and those that are created “on the fly” from the stored data. In both cases, the system stores the User ID of the payroll processor with the report information. When reports are accessed after they have been archived, the system makes the “set in stone” reports accessible again and recreates the “on the fly” reports. However, in

Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries Special situations require special handling options. Users can make special adjustments to process unique and temporary payroll situations. Be sure you fully understand the implications before using these features.

Payroll Option Templates Overview Payroll option templates (also known as calculation templates) allow your organization to change the processing options for one or more employees within a particular payroll batch.

Note: This is different from the Payroll Options in Payroll Control, which applies the settings to all employees in a batch.

  1. Maintain the templates that your organization uses: see Managing Payroll Option Templates on the next page.
  2. Your organization might specify templates at the client level: • If your organization has not chosen to always use payroll option templates at the global level, you must assign templates to each client that will use them; see Client Setup on page 8. • If your organization has opted to use payroll option templates at the global level, then you need to set a custom feature code; see Global Management on page 9. If a client does not have any templates specified in Client Details, users can select any template for employees in that client’s payroll batches.
  3. Users can apply templates to employees in Payroll Control; see Applying Payroll Option Template in Payroll Control on page 10.

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

  1. Users can also apply templates to employees in Summary Time Sheet Entry; see Applying Payroll Option Template in the Time Sheet on page 11.
  2. After the payroll is processed, users can see which template was used by looking at the employee’s voucher; see Payroll Option Template in Employee Voucher on page 11.

Managing Payroll Option Templates You can manage the payroll option templates that your organization uses to override specific calculations for one or more employees in a payroll batch using the Payroll Option Templates form. For example:

To manage payroll option templates, do the following: 1. Enter or select the Template ID. When creating a new template, use something brief but descriptive such as SUPRETDED. You are limited to 10 characters so that it displays cleanly on the Summary Time Sheet Entry form. 2. Enter the Description of the payroll options template that explains its purpose; for example, Suppress Retirement Deductions. 3. Select ACH in the Suppress ACH field to prevent the generation of direct deposit transactions. (Employees normally paid by direct deposit will receive paper checks instead.) For example, you might select this option when the client wants to deliver live checks for year-end bonuses. Note the following: • This field applies only to employee ACH processing. It does not suppress electronic billing.

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

•    If you select Suppress ACH with Pay On-Demand selected, an error message displays stating that they
     cannot be enabled for the same payroll.
•    If you create a manual payroll with Pay On-Demand selected and then apply a Payroll Option Template
     with Suppress ACH selected within a timesheet, an error message displays stating that they cannot be
     enabled for the same payroll and the system does not apply the Payroll Option Template.
  1. Select the ACH Earn Type Limiter to specify the voucher types that will be processed as ACH transactions. Voucher types that you do not specify will be processed as paper checks. This overrides the settings defined in the Employee Details Deposit tab. • Blank: All checks (regular, vacation, and supplemental) • R: Only regular checks • V: Only vacation checks • S: Only supplemental checks • RV: Only regular and vacation checks • RS: Only regular and supplemental checks • VS: Only vacation and supplemental checks
  2. Select Suppress Other Earnings from the Suppress Earnings drop-down to prevent payment for other earnings.
  3. From the Suppress Deductions drop-down, select what payroll deductions (other than payroll taxes) to suppress for this payroll batch, if any. For example, you might need to suppress retirement deductions from bonus pay if employees opt not to have it deducted. Note the following: • When you run a supplemental batch, the system ignores voluntary deductions. • The system sends benefit deductions to arrears.
  4. Select Suppress Arrears to prevent the deduction of any amounts in arrears.
  5. Select Suppress Garnishments to prevent garnishment deductions.
  6. Select Suppress Benefits Calculation to suppress withholding of any benefits deductions and benefit accruals/arrears calculations. If you suppress benefits for this payroll batch, the system does not calculate benefits for the pay period, and therefore no benefit deductions go to arrears.
  7. Select Suppress Benefits Update to suppress the benefit update step that updates benefit-related deduction amounts on employee standard deduction records. The system normally updates the benefits on the employees’ standard deduction schedules according to the parameters set at the system level. For example, if you change the amount of the employees’ contributions on the Group Benefit Plan, the system updates the employees’ standard deduction schedule to reflect the change. Use the Suppress Benefits Update option to suppress that update.
  8. Select Suppress Benefit Adjustments to suppress the processing of benefits adjustments.
  9. Select Suppress Loan Payment to prevent the loan payment from processing in the current payroll when the template is applied.

Entering Multiple Fixed, Pre-calculated Payments The Batch Payments form allows you to quickly enter multiple fixed, pre-calculated payments to be paid during a specific payroll batch. These payments include bonuses, sales commissions, expense reimbursements, and so on. For example:

Note the following: • You can upload batch payment information into the form instead of entering it manually if you have a file in the correct format (see Importing Payments File into a Payroll on page 14. • You can use the BATCH-PAYMENTS-CHANGE-DEFAULTS (system level) and BATCH-PAYMENTS-CHANGE- DEFAULTS-C (client level) custom feature codes to allocate batch payments (see Using Custom Feature Codes and Specifying Client Custom Feature Codes). Note: If you do not set these custom feature codes at the system and client levels, the Edit Employee Details column does not display in the Batch Payments form.

To enter multiple fixed, pre-calculated payments into a payroll: 1. Enter the Payroll Number of the payroll batch within which to pay the additional amounts. This must be an active payroll in the system.

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

Note: If you enter batch payments after the payroll processor has calculated the batch (INITOK or
INITCOMP), the processor must recalculate the payroll to include the payment after you save the batch
payment record.
  1. Enable Recalculate Overtime to automatically enable the Recalculate Overtime field on the Payroll Options form. (This field defaults to disabled.) Note the following: • You can access the Payroll Options form by selecting Options on the Actions menu in the Payroll Control form after selecting a Payroll Number. • The Recalculate Overtime field does not display for payrolls set to the Regularly Scheduled payroll type on the Payroll Control form.
  2. For each employee:
    1. Enter the Employee ID for the line; the employee’s Name displays. It must be an employee that belongs to a pay group included in the payroll batch; it can be a terminated employee. You can enter more than one line for an individual employee, if needed.
    2. Enter the Pay Code for this payment. It must have a fixed calculation method. The Description prints on the pay stub or direct deposit advice.
    3. Enter the Pay Amount. It can be a negative number, but it cannot be zero.
    4. Enter the number of Hours Worked.
    5. Indicate whether to Suppress Allocation. If you select Yes, the system allocates the line only to the employee’s home data fields, instead of basing it on the employee’s allocations set on the Pay tab in the Employee Details form. After selecting Yes, you can select the Edit Employee Details ( ) icon to display the Time Sheet Allocation form, where you can assign the Department, Division, Location, Shift, Position, Project, and Phase allocations. After entering the allocation types, click Accept to apply the values to the batch payment. Note: If you override the home data fields in the Time Sheet Allocation form, a checkmark displays in the Edit Employee Details column in the Batch Payments form.
    6. Indicate whether to Add to Retirement, and how. • No: Does not take the amount as a retirement deduction. • Yes: Takes the pay amount as an extra retirement deduction. • Yes - less FICA: Takes the pay amount as an extra retirement deduction, less the FICA percentage.
  3. Click Save. When the payroll processor calculates the payroll, the payments will be included in the employees’ vouchers. This also increments the employees’ hours by 1; it equates to one unit.

Note: Clicking Delete only deletes the batch payment information for the payroll. It does not delete the payroll batch.

Format Description # Description 1 Employee ID Yes N##### Must be the ID of an employee that works for the client and belongs to a pay group included in the payroll batch; it can be a terminated employee. Overriding Employee Tax Calculation Use the Tax Calculation Overrides form to temporarily override the way the system calculates taxes for an employee.

Working with Income Tax Overrides Using the Income Tax Overrides panel, you can: • Add a fixed amount to the amount already withheld. • Block the tax withholding altogether. • Indicate a new percentage rate to be used in calculating the tax. • Enter a new fixed amount.

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

To override income taxes for an employee: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. Enter the Tax Auth ID to which this tax calculation override applies. The Authority Name displays. 3. Select the Override Type to use in the override for this tax authority:

Override Type Description Add to Amount Withheld Increases the employee’s income tax withholding by a fixed Amount. Percentage Rate Withholds a percentage Amount of net taxable pay. Fixed Amount Withholds the Amount.

Block Withholding Blocks withholding of income tax from the employee’s pay. Supplemental Tax Rate Withholds a percentage Amount of supplemental pay.

Supplemental Tax Amount Withholds a fixed Amount of supplemental pay. Supplemental Block Blocks withholding from supplemental pay.

  1. Enter the override Amount that corresponds with the Override Type. If you blocked withholding, leave this field blank.
  2. Enter the Starting Pay Date when this temporary tax override goes into effect. The tax override applies to payroll batches if the pay date falls within the date range. For the tax override to work, this field is mandatory.
  3. Enter the Ending Pay Date when this temporary tax override is no longer in effect. For the tax override to work, this field is mandatory.
  4. Select the Status to control how the system handles overrides during payroll processing: • Active (default): Processes overrides as they were originally done. • Inactive: Ignores overrides during payroll processing. (You can later reactivate an inactive override by changing this status.) • Onetime: Applies the override to one payroll processed within the entered date range. Note: After a payroll processes with the Status set to Onetime, the override status changes to Inactive and the voucher number displays in the Voucher field. (You cannot edit or reactivate a onetime override after it is used. However, you can enter a new override for the same tax authority.)
  5. Repeat for each tax authority.
  6. Set up any miscellaneous overrides as needed. Otherwise, click Save.

Blocking and Suppressing Taxes • The tax is suppressed, but the resident tax is still not taking enough If you want to suppress a tax and not have the reciprocity taken into consideration, what you would want to do is both block the tax and suppress the tax. This will act like the suppression (i.e., no wages will accrue), but will block the tax from reciprocity. In the following example, the employee lives in Norwalk, OH and works in Sandusky, OH. The tax rate for Norwalk is 1.5% and the tax rate for Sandusky is 1.25%. The following conditions are applicable to wages taxes for Ohio residents who live and work in different Ohio municipalities: • Withhold tax for city employment, and

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 36 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

•    Withhold tax for the city of residence, reduced by the credit amount allowed by the city of residence.

With no suppressions or blocks, the employee’s tax will calculate at 1.25% for Sandusky and will calculate at .25% for Norwalk. This is because Norwalk allows a 100% credit up to 1.50% for the tax paid to the city of employment (which was 1.25%).

If the Sandusky location is suppressed, it will suppress both the tax and the wages. Reciprocity is still taken into consideration when using suppress, so the Norwalk taxes will still be reduced by what would have calculated for Sandusky.

If the Sandusky tax is blocked, it will just block the tax from calculating but the wages will still accrue. Reciprocity is also blocked here.

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 37 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

But, if you do not want the wages to accrue either, if you block and suppress the tax, it will act like a suppression but will block the reciprocity.

Resetting Blocked Filing Status This process resets the employee tax filing status of blocked to single with zero exemptions. The filing year for the Form W-4 must be prior to or equal to the applicable tax year.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To reset the employee tax filing status:

  1. On the (Back Office) menu, select Operations|Action > Reset Federal Withholding Blocked Override.
  2. In Year, enter the tax year applicable to the most current federal Form W-4 on file for this employee.
  3. Click Process.
  4. Click Yes when prompted to continue. A progress window opens and notifies you when the Federal Withholding Blocked Initialization has completed along with the number of employees updated. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled number of employees while the report is being generated.
  5. Click Close to close the window.
  6. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window.
  7. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Overriding Vacation Pay In addition to an employee’s regular pay, some clients issue a separate vacation payroll voucher on the pay date prior to the employee’s actual vacation. Because a lump sum total of multiple weeks would prompt a

Payroll Overrides Guide © 2026 PrismHR 38 Chapter 1 Payroll Overrides and Other Entries

disproportionately higher tax rate than if the tax was determined according to weeks worked, PrismHR allows you to override the vacation vouchers. To override vacation voucher calculations, perform the following steps before you initialize the batch in which this employee will be paid.

To override vacation voucher calculations, do the following: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. Select the Existing Pay Date for the override, or enter a New Pay Date to create a new override. 3. You can specify up to ten vacation vouchers: a. Enter the Start Date of the period paid on this vacation voucher. b. Enter the Ending Date.

Note: Be sure the Ending Date is correct; PrismHR uses this date to update the Benefits Thru Date field on the Employee Details Work tab. The Benefits Thru Date indicates the last date that benefits were calculated for this employee. During payroll processing, the system refers to the Benefits Thru Date to determine whether a benefit deduction is due. For example, when the system processes a check for an employee whose Benefits Thru Date is in the future, it does not calculate benefits.

c. Enter the Deduction Periods (1-5) that correspond to the pay periods paid on the vacation voucher.
   These override the periods on the Batch Control Record.
  1. Click Save.

Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing Special situations require special handling options, such as one-time or temporary adjustments to payrolls. Be sure you fully understand the options before using them.

Processing Tax Adjustments to Tax Register Each tax register contains a running total of amounts deducted from an employee’s paycheck. You can process an adjustment to a client’s tax register when necessary using the Tax Adjustment form. For example, you can process an adjustment when an employee is incorrectly assigned a withholding tax or you are starting in the middle of a year.

Use the tax adjustment process with care. When you process an adjustment to a tax register, be aware that you are making changes to the system’s permanent and only record of taxes withheld for the employee. Important! Do not use the Tax Adjustment feature unless you completely understand the implications of adjusting tax registers.

To set up a tax adjustment: 1. Click New Adjustment to create the new entry. 2. Enter the Employee ID for this adjustment entry. 3. Enter the Adjustment Date. The system uses this date to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to adjust. 4. Enter the Employer ID that should be affected by this adjustment. 5. Select Adjust Client Tax Register if you want the system to update the client’s register for client-based taxes. 6. Select Suppress Billing if you do not want to bill the client for this adjustment.

Payroll Adjustment Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 4 Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing

  1. Enter the School District ID if you are adjusting a school district tax. Note: You cannot enter more than one line for a school tax in the same state.

  2. If you do client reporting by location and need to adjust that type of register, enter the worksite Location.

  3. Select a Special Options Code to modify the tax adjustment process. • Group-Term Life: adjustment to group-term life • Sick Pay Adjustment: adjustment to sick pay • Uncollect Tax Adjustment: uncollected Medicare or OASDI tax adjustments

  4. If you are making an adjustment that affects Pennsylvania local taxes, enter the Residential Geocode Override that the system should use to determine the resident PSD code. If you do not enter a value, the system will use the employer’s value.

  5. Enter the information for each tax code in the table.

    1. Enter the Tax Code that represents the deduction for the tax you need to adjust. You can only enter a code once in the table. The Tax Description displays, as well as the Pre-Adjust Tax Code Register Entry pane.
    2. Enter the Exempt Pay, which is any non-taxable pay.
    3. Enter any Sheltered Earnings, such as retirement amounts.
    4. If you need to adjust it, enter the amount to adjust the Gross Taxable by.
    5. Enter the Taxable Over Limit amount, if needed. This has more to do with employer taxes than employee taxes, the amount of pay that has gone over a limit; for example, the value over the FUTA or SUTA limit.
    6. The system displays the Net Taxable amount. You cannot edit this value.
    7. Enter the Tax Amount that was over-withheld as a negative number. The negative amount in this field represents the money to be paid to the employee. You cannot adjust for tax that was under-withheld.

  6. The system displays any quarter or year entries for the selected Tax Codes in the Pre-Adjust Tax Code Register Entry panel.

  7. Click Save. If the total tax amount is a negative amount and it is an employee-paid tax, the system automatically attempts to refund the amount to the employee. You can choose whether you want the system to print a check

Payroll Adjustment Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 5 Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing

immediately or create a scheduled payment using the tax refund code (defined in System Parameters). If the amount should not be paid to the employee, you can delete the entry in Scheduled Payments. If the employer is SBEA certified, the tax adjustment updates the Federal Entity Tax Register.

Tax Summary Click Tax Summary to view a summary of the employee’s taxes before the adjustments.

Importing Tax Adjustments Tax registers contain a running total of amounts deducted from employee paychecks. You can process tax adjustments when required, such as when an employee has an incorrectly assigned withholding tax.

Note: Proceed carefully with the tax adjustment process. When you process a tax register adjustment, you are changing the only record of taxes withheld for employees in the system.

Transfer Tax Basis Entry You can transfer an employee’s tax basis in the case of a successorship. This allows you to “pick up” where the previous employer “left off” in paying employer-based taxes. Important! Do not use the Transfer Tax Basis feature unless you completely understand the implications of making adjustments to tax registers.

Payroll Adjustment Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing

  1. Click Create new transfer to create the new entry. The fields are enabled for entry.
  2. Enter the Employee ID for this tax basis transfer entry.
  3. Enter the Employer ID for this tax basis transfer entry.
  4. Enter the Tax Year within which this transfer is being made.
  5. Enter the Reason for the transfer.
  6. From the Billing Only drop-down, select the method for updating the PEO Tax Billing Register. • Yes: Update only the PEO Tax Billing Register; the system continues to accrue to the cost side with no regard for these entries. • No: The successor wages that you entered impact both the cost and the bill; complete all fields and enter the appropriate tax code. • Suppress: Suppress the update of the billing register with successor wages.

Note: When filling in the Tax Basis and Tax Amt fields, be sure to fill in the actual tax amount paid thus far. Otherwise, if you leave the amount as zero, the calculation begins at zero.

  1. For each tax code:
    1. Enter the Tax Code. The Tax Description displays.
    2. Enter the Tax Basis, which is the taxable wage base to transfer from another state (SUTA) or from a successor employer. Enter it as either the limit if the employee has met the threshold or the year-to- date amount if they have not quite met the limit. For example, if the employee has earned $10,000 YTD and the limit on that tax code is $7,000, you would enter $7,000 (not $10,000).
    3. Enter the Tax Amt, which is the amount of employer-paid tax liability or employee-paid withholding to transfer from another state or successor employer. It is the bill rate multiplied by the wage basis you are entering.
  2. Click Save.

Adjusting Third Party Sick Pay Records You can adjust an employee’s year-to-date records to reflect sick pay from a third party. Sometimes referred to as disability pay, the Third-Party Sick Pay Adjustment form allows your organization to enter information that is

Payroll Adjustment Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 17 Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing

required for tax purposes. The typical scenario is that the third-party already withheld the taxes and will provide a W-2 to the employee, but your organization would need to collect for the employer taxes. For example:

Employer tax amounts are calculated and billed to the client via the Client Bill Pending feature.

WARNING: Your organization must set up the OASDI and FUTA limits to use the third-party sick pay feature. The system will not let you use the functionality unless these limits are defined in System Parameters.

Note: You can directly access the Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment import template in the Data Import Tool by clicking the link.

To adjust an employee’s year-to-date records: 1. Click New Adjustment to create the new entry. 2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 3. Enter the Adjustment Date. The system uses this date to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to adjust. 4. Enter the Bill Date to use for any billing transaction. If you leave this field blank, the system uses the Adjustment Date. 5. Enter the Employer ID that should be affected by this adjustment.

Payroll Adjustment Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing

Note: If the Employer is not assigned to the Client or as an Alternate Employer for the Client an error
message displays, Invalid Employer ID," and you cannot save the information in the form.
  1. Enter the amount of Federal Taxable Sick Pay, which is the total amount paid to the employee by a third- party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness.
  2. Enter the amount of Federal Non-Taxable Sick Pay, which is sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums.
  3. Enter the Federal Income Tax Withheld, which is the amount of federal income tax withheld by the third- party insurer.
  4. Enter the FICA Taxable Sick Pay, which is the amount of taxable sick pay paid to the employee by a third- party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness.
  5. Enter the FICA Non-Taxable Sick Pay, which is sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums.
  6. Enter the amount of Social Security Tax Withheld by the third-party insurer.
  7. Enter the amount of Medicare Tax Withheld by the third-party insurer.
  8. Select Adjust Client Tax Register if you want the system to update the client’s register for client-based taxes.
  9. For each state to which this adjustment applies (if any):
    1. Enter the two-character postal code for the state that might have miscellaneous state taxes, such as Hawaii employee disability tax.
    2. Select the Tax ID for the state tax withheld from the employee by the third-party insurer.
    3. Enter the Taxable Pay applicable to that state.
    4. Enter the Tax Withheld by the third-party insurer for that state.
  10. Click Save.

Fringe Benefit Pay Entry Use the Fringe Benefit Pay Entry form to enter fringe benefit pay adjustments.

WARNING: This function was designed specifically to exclude FICA (Medicare and OASDI) in the tax basis. Adjusting Incorrectly Posted Pay and Deduction Amounts Do not use the Pay/Deduction Register Adjustment form unless you completely understand the implications of making adjustments to tax registers. If you are unsure how to use it, contact the System Administrator.

The Pay/Deduction Register Adjustment form is designed for adjusting pay and deduction amounts that have been posted to the incorrect pay or deduction code. When entering pay and deduction amounts, the amounts you enter must balance. For example, if you enter in $100 against pay code REG, you must enter a corresponding -$100 against another like pay code. The net effect of the adjustment must balance to zero. You cannot use this feature to increase or decrease an employee’s overall YTD net paycheck. To do so, you must process a pay event. Note: This process is intentionally designed to not generate any accounting or tax consequential entries. As such, the amounts you enter must balance within pay classes and deduction types. For example, you cannot enter $100 to REG and -$100 to an expense reimbursement pay code. To do so would have tax and accounting entries. Similarly, the deduction amounts you enter must balance within deduction types. The deduction type categories are however broader than the total of all system deduction types. The amounts must balance within three categories: • Section 125 Benefit Plan Deductions (including Client voluntary that are coded as such) • 401(k) Deductions (including Client voluntary that are coded as such) • All other deduction types

Note: This adjustment feature does not generate any accounting entries.

Payroll Adjustment Processing Guide © 2026 PrismHR 26 Chapter 1 About Adjustment Processing

To use this option: 1. Click New Adjustment. 2. Enter the Employee ID or click the link to display a list of employees. 3. For each adjustment: a. Enter the Adjustment Date. The system uses this date to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to be adjusted. b. Enter the Weeks Worked. This is the adjustment to the year-to-date balance of the number of weeks worked. c. Enter the Days Worked. This is the adjustment to the year-to-date balance of the number of days worked. d. Enter the Pay Code or click the link to display a list of pay codes. The Pay Code is the pay to be adjusted. e. Enter the Hours Worked. This is the adjustment to the number of hours worked in association with the code in the Pay Code field. f. Enter the Amount of the adjustment. This is the adjustment amount in association with the code in the Pay Code field. The total of the values in this column must equal zero (0). For example, an employee was originally slated to be paid for 42 hours using the REG pay code. You want to adjust their pay to reflect 2 hours paid using the SHIFT pay code. You type the values REG, -2, and -20.00 in the first line’s Pay Code, Hours Worked, and Amount fields and SHIFT, 2, and 20.00 in the second line. g. Enter the Deduction Code or click the link to display a list of deduction codes. This is the deduction to be adjusted. h. Enter the Amount. This is the amount to be adjusted in association with the code in the Deduction Code field. It works in a similar fashion to the Pay Code and the total of the values in this column must equal zero (0). i. Enter the Reference Number. If the adjustment is an employee or 401(k) loan, enter the loan number. If it is a garnishment, enter the docket number. 4. Click Post to save the information .

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction The Accounting User Guide explains the functions and features related to accounting in PrismHR, which consists of the following: • Setup - The tasks and steps involved in defining and setting up codes, values, and definitions that are used for accounting. Authorized users set up these values and definitions at the global and company level, and might perform these tasks periodically when new values or definitions are required. • Administration - The tasks and steps involved in the day-to-day maintenance and administration of accounting tasks.

Intended Audience Your organization should already have set up the initial defaults, files, and preferences required for system administration, as well as client information. You should also have general knowledge of accounting practices. Explaining industry-specific topics other than the use of this software product is outside the scope of this document.

Note: Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot set global accounts receivable information.

PrismHR strongly recommends that you follow the setup steps in the order they are presented in this guide. Be sure to complete the entire accounts receivable setup while no one is using PrismHR to initialize and post payrolls or other accounting processes, as this could cause unexpected results.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 7 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup Your organization must set up accounting parameters and general ledger information at the system level.

Setting Global Accounting Parameters Before setting up your general ledger accounts, configure the accounting parameters that your organization plans to use throughout the system.

To set up the global accounting information: 1. Open System Parameters (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change). 2. Scroll down to the Global Accounting panel.

  1. Select the Accounting Interface Type, which represents the type of accounting program you use with PrismHR. • No Accounting: No accounting interface. • Great Plains/Dynamics: Use Great Plains/Dynamics. • Great Plains/Dynamics - Build Account #s: Automatically create accounts for your Great Plains/Dynamics chart of accounts. • Intacct: Use Intacct. • Intacct - Build Account #s: Automatically create accounts for your Intacct chart of accounts. • Peach Tree/Sage: Use Peach Tree/Sage. • Peach Tree/Sage- Build Account #s: Automatically create accounts for your Peach Tree/Sage chart of accounts. • QuickBooks: Use QuickBooks. • QuickBooks - Build Account #s: Automatically create accounts for your QuickBooks chart of accounts.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 8 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

•    Custom Layout: Create a custom layout.
•    Custom Layout - Build Account #s: Automatically create accounts for the chart of accounts for your
     custom accounting layout.

Note: Automatically building the chart of accounts can be useful. If a G/L account is not in the Chart of Accounts, it does not stop payroll processing; it simply adds the G/L number to the chart. However, the system can also add “bad” G/L numbers, and not all accounting programs can handle these errors. You can remove account numbers that were added in error.

  1. Enter the complete Export Path For Cash Receipts.
  2. Enter the complete Export Path For Receivables data.
  3. Enter the Export Path For Journals, which is the complete export path for general journal data.
  4. Enter the Export Path For CustMast, which is the complete export path for customer data.
  5. Enter the Export Path For CompanyAcctng, which is the complete export path for download files produced by client accounting.
  6. Enter the Import Path For Chart, which is the complete import path for chart of accounts data.
  7. Select Consolidate Cost Accounting to consolidate costs by date.
  8. Select Use PrismHR Accounts Receivable if your organization is using PrismHR Accounts Receivable and you want it to be the primary accounts receivable. (If you select this option, the system will not track accounts receivable information in your accounting software.)
  9. Select Suppress File Transfer Message to suppress the dialog that appears when accounting files are successfully transferred to your computer.
  10. From the W/C General Ledger by State/Policy drop-down, select whether to set up workers’ compensation general ledger accounts by State or Policy. If you do not specify, the system assumes state.
  11. Using the Require Prepay Benefit Account No.field, determine how PrismHR handles prepaid benefits: • Yes: Send liability amounts for prepaid benefit plans to another account. This forces the use of the prepaid account; appropriate fields display in the Group Benefit Plans form. • No: Use the same account for all benefit plans. • Setup: Allow setup transition. For example, if a single plan has clients prepaying, you would put the current clients into the liability and prepaid clients into a prepaid account that you would manually “sweep” at the end of the month into the liability account for the next month.
  12. Click Save.
  13. Click Yes to confirm that you want to save the system parameters.

Creating Multiple G/L Templates Use the G/L Template Maintenance form to create multiple templates for use in the system. These different templates allow you to assign different G/L account numbers to the same codes (benefit codes, pay codes, deduction codes, and so on). Your organization assigns G/L templates to the clients in the system.

To set up G/L templates: 1. Locate the G/L Template Maintenance form in the Back Office menu under System|Change. 2. In the Template ID field, enter the unique identifier for the template. 3. Enter a Description of the template as needed. 4. For this template, enter the value of the Natural Account Number Position in the G/L account definition format. 5. If you are using a multi-part G/L account number, select the account number Position Delimiter. 6. Select Obsolete to prevent the template from being used. Note: Obsolete G/L template IDs display Y in the Obsolete column on the Select GL Template list when you select Template ID. 7. Click Save.

G/L Template Copy Use the G/L Template Copy feature to copy the account codes from an existing template to another template that you have created. For information about setting up G/L templates, see Creating Multiple G/L Templates above.

To copy G/L account codes from one template to another: 1. Locate the G/L Template Copy form in the Back Office menu under System|Change. 2. In the Copy From field, enter the ID of the existing template, which contains the account codes to use as the basis for the newer template. 3. In the To field, enter the ID of the newer template, which receives the copied account codes. The Template Types table populates with the existing types. 4. If you do not need to copy a type, remove it from the list by clicking the x at the left-hand side of the row.

G/L Chart of Account Maintenance Use G/L Chart of Account Maintenance to add, maintain, or delete accounts from your general ledger chart of accounts. What you might need to do with this form depends on whether your system is set to build account numbers; see also Setting Global Accounting Parameters. • If the Accounting Interface Type in System Parameters includes “Build Account #s”, then the chart of accounts is in the auto-build mode. This means that if a G/L number is added into the system in one of the G/L code file setup menus, then at the time the payroll is initialized it will create that number within the chart of accounts. If it is not a valid account, use this form to delete it. • If “Build Account #s” is not indicated and the G/L number is not in the G/L chart of accounts, then the system will give the payroll processor an error during initialization telling the user that it has not been set up. You would then need to use the G/L Chart of Account Maintenance form to add the G/L number.

The G/L Chart of Account Maintenance form is found in the Back Office menu under System|Change.

To set up the G/L chart of accounts: 1. Enter the Account Number. This is the chart of account number that the system uses for validation of accounts that will be sent to your third-party accounting system. 2. If appropriate, enter the Account Description. • To create the account in your chart of accounts because it was missing, click Save.

• To remove the account from the chart of accounts because it is not valid, click Delete.

G/L Account Numbers in PrismHR You can establish G/L account numbers for each of the codes that exist in the system for pay, deductions, benefits, retirement, workers’ compensation, taxes, checking, billing, and other items.

Overview of G/L Account Number Usage This section describes how G/L account number coding affects the accounting for your organization and how these numbers are used in the system’s payroll process.

Benefit Plans When a user sets up a benefit plan, there are four items that affect the accounting process. Each item has a G/L account number assigned to it, so your organization should ensure that they are coordinated together. The four items are: • Benefit Plan ID • Deduction Code • 125 Deduction Code • Bill Code

To set up the G/L account codes for the benefit plan, ensure the accounting information is set up for the benefit plan and each of the codes referenced on the plan: 1. Benefit Plan Accounting (page 20) 2. Deduction Code Accounting (page 26) 3. Billing, Revenue, and Sales Accounting (page 16)

Payroll Processing Examples The following is an example of what the system generates during payroll processing. If the pay period amount for the total premium is $200, then the system creates entries:

                                              Benefit Plan Debit

                                   $200.00

                                              Benefit Plan Credit

                                                                    $200.00

If in this example the premium was split equally between the employee and the employer, then the entries for the deduction from the employee would be:

                                             Deduction Code Debit

                                   $100.00

                                                 Cash Account Credit

                                                                           $100.00

The entries for the billing to the client would be:

                                                    Bill Code Credit

                                                                           $100.00

                                             Accounts Receivable Debit

                                       $100.00

If this was a plan paid by the PEO (either PEO- or client-sponsored), then the PEO would have a liability of $200, which is owed to the plan provider. Depending on how your organization wants to set up accounting, the debits and credits will offset each other in different ways. Here are some options. Liability, Cost, and Income If you want to record the entries to show a liability, cost, and income, the accounting entry would be like those shown in Table 1. Table 1: Entries to Show Liability, Cost, and Income

                   Account                                 Debit                               Credit

   Payroll Cash                                          $100.00
   (portion of net pay credit)
   A/R                                                   $100.00

   Liability                                                                                  $200.00

   Income                                                                                     $100.00

   Cost                                                  $100.00

Liability Only If you want to net all of the entries and not show cost or income but only the liability, then the accounting entry would be like those shown in Table 2.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

                                            Table 2: Entries to Show Liability Only

                   Account                                   Debit                                Credit

   Payroll Cash                                             $100.00
   (portion of net pay credit)
   A/R                                                      $100.00

   Liability                                                                                     $200.00

Zero Liability If you have a plan that is sponsored and paid by the client, your organization would have a liability of zero (Table 3). Table 3: Entries to Show Client-Paid and -Sponsored Plan

                    Account                                    Debit                               Credit

   Payroll Cash                                                $0.00
   (net pay paid from client’s account)
   A/R                                                                                             $0.00
   (nothing due from client because it
   is offset to zero)
   Liability                                                                                       $0.00
   (net amount between the liability
   and deduction code)

Setting Up the Billing Code and G/L Account Associations Use the G/L Setup form to set up the billing code and general ledger account associations.

To set up the billing codes/general ledger account associations: 1. Enter or select the GL Template for the general ledger distribution template. (This template was previously defined.) Note the following: • CLID wildcards do not work with the GL Template set to GL and the GL Type set to Miscellaneous. • Your organization might have different templates for PEOs and ASOs. You can assign different account numbers to each template. • An error message displays if you enter or select an obsolete GL Template, and the system will not process a payroll when a client assigned with an obsolete G/L template tries to initiate payroll calculation or finalization. 2. From the GL Type drop-down, select Billing Code. The form lists each Billing Code and Description in the system. 3. Enter or import the G/L account number used for the billing code in the Account field. Note: You can enter simple account segments or full account numbers with wildcards. 4. Click Save. Repeat the procedure for each general ledger template you need to edit.

Billing, Revenue, and Sales Accounting You must set up an association between billing codes and general ledger accounts for the billing, revenue, and sales portion of accounting.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

To set up an association, do the following: 1. Enter the G/L Template for the general ledger distribution template. This template was previously defined. Your organization would have different templates for PEOs and ASOs. You can assign different account numbers to each template. 2. From the G/L Type drop-down, select Billing Code. The form lists each Billing Code and Description in the system.

  1. For each code that requires account information, enter the full Account number of the associated general ledger account. You can enter a simple account segment or a full account number with wildcards. When payroll is processed for a client, the system generates the accounting based on the setup of the different plans, the client, and the employees. In the case of benefit plans, for example, generating the employee payroll voucher creates the entries for the benefits plans, retirement plans, workers’ compensation, miscellaneous deductions, and so on. Once the voucher process is complete, the system then generates the billing vouchers and those in turn generate income entries, accounts receivable entries, and the invoice to the client.
  2. Click Save. Repeat the procedure for each general ledger template you need to edit.

Benefit Plan Accounting If you have created global group benefit plans, you must create the association of each group benefit plan ID with a general ledger account.

To setup the group benefit plan code/general ledger account associations: 1. Enter the G/L Template for the general ledger distribution template. This template was defined previously. Your organization would have different templates for PEOs and ASOs. You can assign different account numbers to each template. 2. From the G/L Type drop-down, select Benefit Plan. The form lists each Benefit Plan ID and Description in the system.

  1. For each code that requires account information, enter the full Debit Account and Credit Account numbers of the associated general ledger accounts. You can enter a simple account segment or a full account number with wildcards. The debit and credit accounts represent the premium amount to be paid to the plan provider. You can use a different G/L code for Debit and Expense if the benefit plan uses the One Month Prepay option (bill the client and deduct the amounts from the employees for the next month in the current month).
  2. Click Save. Repeat the procedure for each general ledger template you need to edit.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

In the system, group benefit plans have accrual accounting attached to them. (Many other systems only track employee contributions to group benefits as they are deducted from employee checks.) The system performs accrual accounting on a per-batch accounting basis, so that the costs associated with benefit plans are waiting in the liability accounts by the time the invoice arrives from the benefit provider. Using the per-batch method is especially useful for a company that performs complex cost accounting using cost centers. The costs are broken out at the source level, which means there is less chance for accounting errors— not to mention less work. PEO/Client Provided and PEO Paid Benefit Plan In this case, the PEO (service provider) or client provides the benefit plan and the PEO pays the plan provider for the benefit. The PEO has an accrual to their liability account for the amount of the check to be paid to the benefit provider. The system prompts for the debit and credit accounts for the benefit plan. It accrues the entire benefit payable while deciding which employees are eligible for the benefit—in other words, whether or not the employee makes a contribution against the benefit, the entire balance accrues. The system is capturing the total due to the plan provider. With this in mind, the selection of the Premium Debit and Premium Credit accounts should ultimately charge the cost of sale account for the debit and the liability account for the credit. The following table shows benefit plan accounting for a $150.00 plan:

                          Benefit Liability Accrued (or    Cost of Sales - Benefit Plan
                              Accrued Payable)                      Expense

                                               $150.00     $150.00

The deduction code referenced on the benefit plan should be set up to credit the expense. Remember that anything the employee pays towards the benefit plan does not affect your liability; it simply decreases your cost. The following image shows the Group Benefit Plans form in PrismHR. (Click Back Office. Select Group Benefit Plans under System|Change.) This figure highlights the Deduction Code.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 21 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

Since the same amount deducted from the employee will also be credited back to the client, the sales account will also be reduced by the same amount. The P&L effect will not change. For example, if the employee contributes $50.00, the bill to the client will go down by $50.00, as will your cost for providing this benefit. Table 8 shows the effect of the deduction code: Table 8: Deduction Code Example

                                                            Cost of Sales - Benefit Plan
                           Payroll Cash Account
                                                                     Expense

                         $50.00                                                        $50.00

Table 9 shows the effect of the deduction on the billing side: Table 9: Benefit Plan Accounting Example

                              Accounts Receivable                 Sales - Benefit Plans

                                              $50.00          $50.00

Even if the benefit is 100% paid by the PEO, the amount paid by the employee serves to lower the PEO’s costs. As an option, the system can update an expense account instead of a revenue account so that an employee deduction towards a benefit serves to negate the reduction of expenses; however, this method never completely ties your invoiced amounts into your revenues. The PEO has to include revenues that were accounted for within your General Journal costs to get the complete picture of revenues; in this case, no invoice register would contain complete revenue data. Some clients wash all these elements through a clearing account if there is no mark-up on the plans. Client Provided and Paid Benefit Plan In this case, the PEO has no cost associated with the plan and has all monies deducted from the employee, decreasing the invoice. PrismHR users frequently handle these kinds of plans as simple voluntary deductions with a client rebate code attached (for example, see Table 10). This reduces the client invoice by the amount deducted from the employees. There are some issues handling these benefits as simple deductions, though. Since the PEO does not administer the plan, the client has to notify the PEO how and when to update the amounts to be withheld from each employee’s check. However, if your client is unable or does not desire to keep up with the balances due, you might want to build an “Other” group benefit plan. Building the “Other” group benefit plan automatically activates PrismHR’s built-in arrearage system and allows you to keep track of contributions. The accounting issue with benefit plans is making the Cost accounting side “go away.” With client sponsored/client paid benefits, the PEO has no liability or cost accounting requirements because the PEO is rebating all the money deducted from employee checks through invoice credits.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 22 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

For this case, the PrismHR Customer Support Team recommends that PrismHR users create a liability account that is assigned the function of washing through zero value journals. In this case, the Benefit Plan would have both the debit and credit transactions assigned to this zero account. Also, the premium cost sides of the plan should be set to zero (0.00) costs, as should the billing sides of the plan. You would do this by building a Benefit Plan in Benefit Plan maintenance that showed the premium costs for each plan level (single, single plus one, family, and so on) as zero. In the event some money ever ended up in the account accidentally, the fact that it would exist on the balance sheet would bring immediate attention to the problem. Table 10 shows benefit plan accounting for a $150.00 plan: Table 10: Client Rebate Code Example

                                                    Zero (Wash) Liability

                                                    $0.00            $0.00

Table 10 shows the cost side of the benefit plan hitting the books. This example assumes the plan is built with zero costs, as recommended above. Likewise, the deduction code used in either case (Voluntary Deduction with Rebate Code (see Voluntary Deduction Rebated to the Client on page 27) or Benefit Plan with Deduction (see PEO/Client Provided and PEO Paid Benefit Plan on page 21)) would be coded into the same wash account. The Bill Code associated with the Deduction/Benefit Plan would also be coded against the same account so that monies withheld from employees would be washed against the credit issued on the invoice, the net effect of which would be none, as shown in Table 11. Table 12 shows the credit from the billing transaction. Table 11: $50 Deduction an from Employee Check

                                   Payroll Cash                       Zero (Wash) Liability

                         $50.00                                                          $50.00

The credit is the “sales” effect, sent to the Zero (Wash) Liability account. The desired effect is net zero. As you can see, once both are complete, the net effect in the Zero (Wash) Liability account is zero.

Voluntary Deduction Not Rebated to the Client Before implementing this setup, your organization would decide whether your want to earn revenue off your employees. If these deductions are considered revenue streams, then you would code the charges for items such as stop payment check fees and other service charges to credit a revenue account. Most service providers find this revenue stream to be so small or unimportant that they choose instead to show these transactions as either a reduction of expenses for office or bank service fees or other income below the line. Whatever account your organization selects will be credited for any amount withheld from an employee’s check. Do note that, if this type of transaction is coded to revenues, these revenues will not show on the invoice and may cause issues in reviewing invoice and billing reports for total revenues. To handle this, some service providers build special expense accounts to receive the money instead of lumping it into “office expense”; for example, “office expense reimbursed from garnishment or fees” as a contra-account to “office expense”.

Taxes If you have created global tax codes, you must create the association of each tax code with a general ledger account. Tax G/L accounts are entered into the system based on state code and tax ID. To set up the tax code/general ledger account associations: 1. Enter the G/L Template for the general ledger distribution template. This template was previously defined. 2. From the G/L Type drop-down, select Tax. 3. In the State Code field, enter FG for federal government or the two-character state code (second example below). The system lists each Tax ID and Description in the first two columns. These taxes are either at the federal level (federal income tax), state level (state income tax, SUTA, and so on), or lower (county and local taxes). For employer-paid taxes, you need both a credit (liability) account and debit (expense) account. For employee-paid taxes, you need only a credit account because there is no expense to an employee-paid tax. When a tax is computed, the system looks at the state record to find the G/L codes. If they are not found there, it looks at FG (federal government). Therefore, you should only enter general ledger numbers at the state level if they are different from the ones used for the federal government. If you want to use only state-level accounting, then leave the FG record entirely blank. That way, the system will inform you if the state is missing codes rather than accepting the federal-level defaults.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 30 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

  1. For each code that requires account information, enter the full Debit Account and/or Credit Account numbers of the associated general ledger accounts. You can enter a simple account segment or a full account number with wildcards. For a state, the FG? column indicates how the system uses G/L account numbers for each tax ID. (This column does not apply to FG.) • No FG: There is no number entered on the FG template. • UseFG: The state template uses the value from the FG template. • OvrFG: The template uses the number indicated in the Debit Account or Credit Account column.
  2. Click Save. Repeat the procedure for each general ledger template you need to edit.

Importing G/L Account Codes You can use the G/L Import Entry form to quickly import account codes to the G/L setup by uploading a file for import and then viewing any errors that occurred during the import or viewing successfully imported rows.

To import G/L account codes: 1. Enter or select the GL Template. The template name displays. 2. Select the GL Type. 3. Enable Overwrite Existing Account Codes to replace previously imported account codes. Otherwise, leave this field blank and the system will only import new codes. 4. Select Download Template File to download a .txt file to your computer that contains the headings that match the selected GL Type. A separate window displays the downloaded file link. 5. Click Open File. The spreadsheet template displays, where you can enter the G/L account codes information. 6. Select Find File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload. 7. Click Close. A progress window displays. Note: If an error occurs a message displays, “It may be possible to recover from this error. Do you want to repeat your last action?” Click OK. 8. Click Close. The import process extracts account codes from the external file. Note the following: • The import process skips any lines that contain invalid codes in the first column and reports them in the error report. • If you did not enable Overwrite Existing Account Codes, the import process skips any lines that would overwrite an existing account code and reports them in the error report. 9. A preview of imported G/L account codes displays in the G/L Import Data panel. Note: You can download a .csv version of this information by clicking Preview Report. 10. If the import process encounters errors, you can select one of the following: • Done With Errors: Performs the import even though it contains errors.

Defining Periods for Your General Ledger Use the G/L Periods form to define the periods for your general ledger.

To define periods for your general ledger: 1. Enter the Period code, ensuring that it conforms to the format used by your general ledger. 2. Enter a Description of this G/L period. 3. Enter the calendar Year. 4. Enter the Month or G/L period within the year. 5. Enter the External G/L Period to be passed to an external general ledger. 6. Click Save.

Defining Global G/L Accounts Use the Global G/L Account Definition (Corporate) form to define global G/L accounts.

To define global G/L accounts: 1. Select the Prefix Values that you want to attach to the beginning of G/L account codes that allow prefixes. 2. Select the Suffix Values that you want to append to the end of G/L account codes that allow suffixes. 3. Enter the Segment Delimiter to use. Valid delimiters are: *, - , ., or ! If you leave the field blank, there will be no mark or spaces between the account number and any prefix or suffix. 4. Enter the Code Acct Segment No, which is the segment where the “core” account number is found. 5. Enter any Account Value Overrides: a. Select the When Field Equals term. b. Enter the is equal to term. c. Enter the Replace Account # With value to append to the account number instead. 6. Click Save.

Defining Codes for Corporate Payroll Accounts Use the Payroll Account Codes form to define codes for your corporate payroll accounts.

To define codes for corporate payroll accounts: 1. Enter the unique payroll Account number. 2. Enter a short Account Name, such as Payroll Tax Expense or FICA Liability. 3. Select Prefix/Suffix Allowed if the G/L account code can take prefixes and suffixes using the variables set up in the account definitions.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 39 Chapter 2 System and General Ledger Setup

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 40 Chapter 3 Accounts Receivable Code Files

Chapter 3 Accounts Receivable Code Files These topics describe how to set up and manage your codes and aging buckets for accounts receivable.

Configuring AR Terms Your organization can define different terms for dealing with different customers or vendors, such as Net 0 or Net 10th Prox. Each term is represented by a terms code.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 41 Chapter 3 Accounts Receivable Code Files

To define AR terms codes: 1. Access the AR Terms form (found in the Back Office menu under Accounts Receivable|Change). 2. Enter the Terms Code. If you are creating a new code, use a code or ID that best represents the accounts receivable terms used by your organization. For example: • Net0 for a net zero term (due immediately) • Net10P for net 10th prox term (due by the tenth of the month) 3. Enter a clear and concise description of the term in the A/R Terms Desc field. 4. Select the A/R Terms Due Type: • Days - Terms due after a certain number of days • Prox - Terms due on a day of the following month 5. If you selected Prox, enter the cutoff day in the field that begins “What is the last day of the month…”. This defines the cutoff date for the due date. Payments for invoices through this date are due by the specified day of the following month. If the due day is 10, the due date is the 10th of the following month. The cutoff day is the 25th of the current month, therefore: • Invoices dated between June 1 through June 25 are due on July 10. • Invoices dated between June 26 and June 30 are due on August 10. 6. In the Number of days or day of the month field: • For Days, enter the number of days when the invoice is due. • For Prox, enter the day of the month when the invoice is due. 7. Click Save.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 42 Chapter 3 Accounts Receivable Code Files

About A/R Aging Buckets PrismHR supports data aging and uses two sets of buckets. The buckets represent aged accounts receivable data. Many organizations have a different set of rules for their operational use (operations) than what is required by financial standards (finance).

Note: If your organization uses more than five buckets, you must print the reports on legal-sized paper. The system supports up to seven total buckets.

Example Setup For example, consider an organization that mostly uses cash. An open balance over seven days old is a cause for concern and review. The organization’s banking relationships, however, want to review the receivables in standard increments of 30-, 60-, and 90-days. To facilitate reporting, the organization built two sets of buckets: • Operations records • Standard financial records The organization has these Operations buckets: • Current (0) • 1–7 • 8–14 • 15–21 • 22+ The Finance buckets are standard: • Current (0) • 1–30 • 31–60 • 61–90 • 91+

Maintaining Aging Buckets Your organization can define AR aging buckets for your own use (operations) and for reporting purposes (finance) in the Aging Bucket Maintenance form. You can create up to seven buckets.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 43 Chapter 3 Accounts Receivable Code Files

To maintain AR aging buckets: 1. Access the Aging Bucket Maintenance form (found in the Back Office menu under Accounts Receivable|Change). 2. Select the Bucket code: • Operations: aging bucket for use by your organization. • Finance: aging bucket for reporting to financial institutions. 3. Select the Age based on, either Invoice Date or Due Date. The system calculates the actual due date based on the AR term code. Next, define each bucket. You must define the buckets in order, with the newest at the top and the oldest at the bottom. 4. Enter the number for each of the Buckets, for example, 60. • This must be an integer, and the number represents the aging; any document this age or newer will go in this column. • Define the last bucket as 99999. The system recognizes that value as the final tier. 5. Enter the first line of the stacked heading for the aging report in Desc Line1, for example, 31 - 60. 6. Enter the second line of the stacked heading for the aging report in Desc Line2, for example, Past Due. On the report, this example would display as: 31 - 60 Past Due

  1. Click Save.

Setting Cash Receipt Rules Use the Cash Receipt Rules form to enter the posting types for the cash receipts that your organization processes, along with the G/L account to use for each cash receipt posting type.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 44 Chapter 3 Accounts Receivable Code Files

Note: When you enter a debit invoice that is greater than the deposit amount, you must enter credit invoices first. Otherwise, the system generates an error.

To configure cash receipt rules: 1. Access the Cash Receipt Rules form (found in the Back Office menu under Accounts Receivable|Action). 2. For each of the G/L accounts: • Enter the Posting Description. • In Post to GL Account: enter INVOICE for the posting type used to process invoices. Otherwise, enter the G/L account number for other types of cash receipts transactions. 3. Click Save.

Chapter 4 Customer-Level A/R Setup Customer Details contains the address and contact information for collection purposes, a current representation of the aging for the customer, and the ability to edit the credit limit rules (with authorization).

Configuring AR Customer Details Use Customer Details to maintain the customer address and contact information for collection purposes, view the current representation of aging for the customer, and edit the credit limit rules. The form displays the information for the currently selected client. To access this form, open the Back Office menu and select Customer Details under Accounts Receivable|Change.

To set up basic customer details: 1. Locate the Customer Details panel at the top of the form. The Customer number displays. 2. Edit the customer name and address as needed. 3. Enter the Customer Group used to prepare agings to which this customer belongs, if any. 4. Select the A/R Terms Code.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 46 Chapter 4 Customer-Level A/R Setup

Aging The Aging panel displays your organization’s operations aging information for the customer.

•    The Bucket Desc column shows the descriptions for each of the buckets.
•    The Aging Buckets column displays the amount in each bucket.

Credit Details Use the Credit Details panel to maintain credit rules, if that applies to this customer.

  1. The panel displays the customer’s current Credit Limit, Balance Due, and Available Credit.

  1. Enter the Max Credit, which is the maximum credit limit allowed. If you leave this field blank, there is no credit limit.
  2. Select Client On Hold if this customer is on a credit hold. The option indicates a manual hold, not the automatic hold.
  3. Set the limit rules: • Select each of the Limit Rules that determines what the credit limit should be and how far the client is allowed to go outside those limits, if at all. • Enter the Limit Amt that applies to the limit rule.
  4. For each limit review: • Enter the Limit Review Date when you conducted the review of the credit limit. • Enter the Limit Review By name or user name. • Enter the Limit Review Description/Override. If the customer is put on credit hold, enter OVERRIDE and then any additional comments. Otherwise, enter any comments about the limit review.
  5. Click Save.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 48 Chapter 5 Working with Cash Receipts and Balances

Chapter 5 Working with Cash Receipts and Balances At times, your organization will need to post non-automatic cash receipts. You can use the Cash Receipts form to: • Enter corrections to prior automatic functions (for example, a bounced ACH) • Write off balances that cannot be collected • Distribute cash to a specific general ledger account (for example, you receive a rent check)

Note: When you enter a debit invoice that is greater than the deposit amount, you must enter credit invoices first. Otherwise, the system generates an error.

Entering Cash Receipts Use the Cash Receipts form to enter new batches of cash receipts or edit existing ones and upload a file for import.

Note: When you enter a debit invoice that is greater than the deposit amount, you must enter credit invoices first. Otherwise, the system generates an error.

Using Post and Clear Buttons • Post: Click to post the cash receipts batch when the deposit is complete. • Clear: Click to save the cash receipts batch. The system adds it to the list of open batches at the top of the Cash Receipts form.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 49 Chapter 5 Working with Cash Receipts and Balances

  1. Use the form to edit a new or existing cash receipts batch and upload a file for import: • To open an existing batch, click the Batch ID in the Cash Receipts panel. • To start a new cash receipts batch, click New deposit in the Receipt Entry panel. • To open the Cash Receipts Import form to upload a file for import and view errors that occurred during cash receipts imports or view successfully imported rows, click the Import icon ( ). (See Importing and Posting Cash Receipts on page 55.) Note the following: • This feature is only available for service providers. • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the Cash Receipts form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Cash Receipts Import form cannot view the Import icon ( ) on the Cash Receipts form.

      •    Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Cash Receipts form can select the Import icon (        ), but

Importing and Posting Cash Receipts You can use the Cash Receipts Import form to quickly import and post cash receipts in the system. For example:

To perform an import using the Cash Receipts Import form, simply upload a file for import and then view any errors that occurred during the import or view successfully imported rows. Note the following: • This form is only available for service providers. • You can access this form by selecting Cash Receipts Import on the Accounts Receivable|Action menu or by selecting the Import icon ( ) on the Cash Receipts form. • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To import cash receipts: 1. Select Download Spreadsheet Template to download a .csv file to your computer that contains the cash receipts import headings in row 1. A separate window displays the downloaded file link.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 55 Chapter 5 Working with Cash Receipts and Balances

  1. Click Open File. The spreadsheet template displays, where you can enter the cash receipts information. Note: All columns in this spreadsheet are required except for the Description 1 and Description 2 columns. The spreadsheet template contains the following columns:

     Column                    Description
 Client Number             The client number associated with the deposit.

 Bank ID                   The bank ID associated with the deposit.
                           Note: The system uses the Bank ID from the first row in the import file for all
                           Cash Receipts imports on the file.
 Deposit Date              The deposit date associated with the deposit.
 Description 1             The description associated with the deposit (optional).
 Description 2             The description associated with the deposit (optional).
 Deposit Number            The deposit number associated with the deposit.
 Line Type                 The line type associated with the deposit.
 Deposit Type              The type of deposit.
 Deposit Amount            The total amount that was deposited.
 Deposit Reference         The unique reference ID associated with the deposit, which can include
                           alphanumeric characters, but not spaces.
 Posting Type              The posting type associated with the deposit. (Posting types are established
                           on the Cash Receipt Rules form.)
 Invoice Number            The invoice number associated with the deposit.

 Amount                    The amount that is applied to the deposit.

  2. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

  3. Click Close. The uploaded filename displays.

  4. Select Preview Data. Information displays on the following tabs: • Errors: Any cash receipts errors from the import process display on this tab. Click Error Report to view them. (A browser window opens where you can download the .csv file that contains the errors.) • File Content: Any successful rows from the import process display on this tab. Note: If you select Preview Data before uploading the file, no information displays.

  5. Click Import Cash Receipts to post the cash receipts that display on the File Content tab. The “File content successfully imported” message displays. Click OK. Note: Any additional errors that occur during the posting display in the existing errors list on the Errors tab.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 56 Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation

Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation Users can reconcile or unreconcile checks in PrismHR.

Automatically Reconciling Checks Three different forms are involved in the automatic check reconciliation procedure. The overall procedure is as follows: 1. Receive the reconciliation data from the financial institution. 2. Use Auto Check Reconciliation Load to import the reconciliation data into a temporary file. 3. Run the Reconciliation Report for Auto Recon to review any checks that the system could not reconcile. 4. Run Post Auto Reconciliations to clear the reconciled checks from the temporary file.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 57 Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation

You can use the automatic reconciliation feature if your organization’s financial institution provides an electronic file format supported by PrismHR. The currently supported formats are:

  •    Tab Delimited                  •   Bank of The West             •    M&T Bank
  •    Arch Format                    •   Chemical Bank                •    National Bank
  •    Amcor                          •   Chase Bank                   •    ARP
  •    Bank of America                •   First Union                  •    Regions Bank
  •    Alternate Bank of America      •   Fleet/Baybank                •    SunTrust Bank
  •    Bank of America                •   Hancock Bank                 •    SunTrust Alternate Format
  •    Bank of America BAI Format     •   KeyCorp Bank                 •    Wells Fargo
  •    Bank of America pos34 12-      •   Merrill Lynch                •    Wells Fargo CSV
       digit acct#                                                     •    Wells Fargo Fixed Length

Importing Auto Reconciliation Data Once your organization receives the reconciliation data file from your financial institution, use Auto Check Reconciliation Load to import the reconciliation data into PrismHR.
