  3. If there are any accounts that you do not want to reconcile at this time, enter them in the Exclude Account# table. The system will not display error messages for those accounts during processing.

  4. Click Import.

  5. In the Upload a File window, click Choose File.

  6. Navigate to the location where you saved the reconciliation data file, and then click Open.

  7. Click Submit in the Upload a File window.

  8. Click Close in the successful upload message. The Uploading Check Reconciliation Data form displays the processing steps.

  9. When the import is complete, click the Close button. The summary of the reconciliation report displays on the right side of the Auto Check Reconciliation Load form.

Reviewing Auto Reconciled Checks Use the Reconciliation Report for Auto Recon to review the reconciled checks in the reconciliation data file your organization is currently processing see Importing Auto Reconciliation Data on page 58.

To run the Reconciliation Report for Auto Recon: 1. Open the report parameters form (found in the Back Office menu under Operations|Report). 1. Enter the Checking Account No. you entered in Auto Check Reconciliation Load when you started the process. 2. Enter the appropriate dates in the Beginning Date and Ending Date fields. 3. Click Run. The Check Reconciliation Edit Report displays.

The report displays all the checks in the data file with pay dates that were in the specified date range. The report displays the reconciliation error. Some examples of discrepancies are: • A Check number that does not match an open check number in the system. • An Amount Cleared value that does not match the value in the system.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 66 Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation

Notes About Common Issues • If the wrong file was loaded accidentally or if the file is loaded with the wrong format, the Check Reconciliation Edit Report will display garbage data, possibly including references to check numbers that do not exist. If that is the case, return to the Auto Check Reconciliation Load and begin again. Be sure to select the option to clear out the existing in the reconciliation file. • The automatic reconciliation process does not allow a check to be reconciled more than once. If you attempt to use a check number that has already been reconciled, the report displays the error Invalid Check Status: R. • If you know a check listed in the report with an error is actually correct and should be reconciled, use the manual reconciliation feature.

Checks that were included in the reconciliation data file that do not have errors will be reconciled when you post them.

Posting Auto Reconciliations Once you have loaded the reconciliation data file, reviewed the report, and addressed any issues, you can post the reconciliations to the system.

To post auto reconciliations: 1. Open the Post Auto Reconciliations form, found in the Back Office menu under Operations|Action. 2. Enter the Checking Account No. you previously entered for the previous steps of the process, Auto Check Reconciliation Load and Reconciliation Report for Auto Recon. 3. Enter the appropriate dates in the Beginning Date and Ending Date fields.

Note: It is especially important to enter these dates before posting. If you post the bank reconciliation files without entering the Beginning Date and Ending Date, the process still completes, but the system will continue to list the checks as outstanding in the check register.

  1. The Reconciliation Date defaults to the current date, but you can change it if appropriate.

  2. Click Run. The system displays the Posting Check Reconciliation form, which details the processing steps.

  3. When the posting is complete, click the Close button.

Manual Check Reconciliation Use the Manual Check Reconciliation feature to reconcile checks that cannot be reconciled by the automatic reconciliation feature.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 67 Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation

To perform manual check reconciliation: 1. Open the Manual Check Reconciliation form, found in the Back Office menu under Operations|Action. 2. Enter the Checking Account ID. This is the number that represents an account in PrismHR and may not match the actual bank account number. The Bank Name and Account Number display. 3. Enter the Recon Date. The default is the current date. 4. Enter each Check Number that you want to reconcile. The Check Date, Paid To (payee), and Check Amount display. You must enter a valid check number. You cannot enter the number of a check that has already been reconciled. 5. When you are ready, click Update. The system sets the status of those checks to reconciled (R).

This is the number that represents an account in PrismHR and may not match the actual bank account number. 2. Enter the Check Number to unreconcile. The Status Code, Status Date, Check Amount, and Pay to Name (payee) display. 3. Verify that this is the correct check and then click Unreconcile Check.

Positive Pay Positive pay is an automated fraud detection tool offered by the cash management department of most financial institutions. In its simplest form, it is a service that matches the account number, check number, and dollar amount of each check presented for payment against a list of checks previously authorized and issued by the company. All three components of the check must match exactly or the bank will not honor the check. The main tasks related to positive pay are: • Setting up positive pay on each bank account, which is maintained in the backend system for PrismHR. • Creating a positive pay file; see Create Positive Pay Files below. • Recreating positive pay files as needed: see Recreate Positive Pay Files on page 75. • Producing a positive pay report: see Positive Pay File Report on page 76.

Create Positive Pay Files Use the Create Positive Pay Files form to create the file that you will send to the financial institution.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 73 Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation

  1. Before you begin, disable the pop-up blocker on your browser.

  2. You can generate a positive pay file for one checking account, or for multiple accounts: • To generate a positive pay file for only one bank account, enter the Checking Account ID; this is the number that represents an account in PrismHR and might not match the actual bank account number. The account name displays. • To generate positive pay files for all bank accounts, leave the Checking Account ID field blank.

  3. If you are creating one positive pay file for multiple accounts, enter the File Stub ID for the accounts that you want to include in the file. The file stub is specified in Positive Pay Setup, accessed through the Actions menu of the Bank Accounts form.

  4. Typically, you would enter the Starting Check Date and Ending Check Date to create the positive pay file for a specific range of dates. If you do not enter dates, the positive pay file will include all available data.

  5. Select Include Voided Checks to include voids in the positive pay file.

  6. Click Create Positive Pay Files.

  7. Click Yes in the confirmation message. The Starting CREATE Positive Pay Files form displays the processing steps.

  8. When the creation process is complete, click the Close button. The system prepares to download the file (or the first of multiple files) to your computer. This process depends on the browser you are using and its settings.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 74 Chapter 6 Check Reconciliation

  1. Some browsers open a blank window when they process the download file. Close this window when the download is complete; in the case where you have created multiple positive pay files, that window would prevent the additional files from downloading.
  2. If your browser is set to prompt you for the location to save the file, use your computer’s Save As window to navigate to the location where you want to save the file. Otherwise, the system saves it to your default file location. Make a note of the directory and file name.
  3. Go to the location where you saved the file and open it in a text editor such as Notepad. Check the file format; if it is not correct, open Positive Pay Setup for the account and make corrections.
  4. Send the positive pay file to the financial institution.

  5. When the creation process is complete, click the Close button. The system prepares to download the file to your computer. This process depends on the browser you are using and its settings.

  6. Some browsers open a blank window when they process the download file. Close this window when the download is complete; that window can prevent other files from downloading.

  7. If your browser is set to prompt you for the location to save the file, use your computer’s Save As window to navigate to the location where you want to save the file. Otherwise, the system saves it to your default file location. Make a note of the directory and file name.

Chapter 7 Accounting System Integration Using the External Invoice Post and External Journal Post features, your organization can create the files that you will use to import data into your financial accounting system. Examining External Journal Posts and External Cash Transfer Posts When users process a payroll batch, the system looks at the pay date and the employer ID or cash transfers and adds it to a file of transactions. All payrolls processed with the same pay date and employer ID or cash transfers are compiled into one entry in the Export Journal Update panel and the Export Journal Update Cash Transfers panel (part of the External Journal Posting and External Cash Transfer Posting features, respectively). When you look at the data in the import file or report, however, it is broken down by the client and pay date or by cash transfer. Note: You can capture Third-Party Check Reporting for Corporate clients using the External Journal Post (Corporate/Staffing) form. The Export Journal Update panel displays: • Select: Use these checkboxes to select individual line(s) to process • TranDate: Date of the payroll (transaction date) • Co No: Employer ID • Debit Amt: Total debit amount • Count: Debit count for date and employer • Credit Amt: Total credit amount • Count: Credit count for date and employer • Debit Total: Totals of the Debit Amt and Count columns

Chapter 9 Troubleshooting ACH Issues These are procedures for uncommon situations:

ACH Build Errors Users can rebuild the ACH file if needed. The following list provides example cases where an ACH rebuild is required. • A user was in the process of building the ACH file, but they were kicked out of the system before they could get the file. • The file includes incorrect data. • The file contains both debits and credits, but they need to be separated. • A user built the file before updating the client’s bank account number. • An employee’s bank account number changed but was not updated in the system, so the ACH file has the wrong account number. Several features are available that allow users to save and rebuild the ACH file.

Downloading ACH Files to Your PC Use the Transfer ACH File to PC form to download ACH files to a user’s system, from the server’s download directory generated by the PrismHR system. Note the following: • This form is only available for service providers. • This process does not use Client Access Group security.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu> Operations|Action > Transfer ACH File to PC.

To download an ACH File to a user’s PC: 1. Click the Filename link. A separate Select Field window opens.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 103 Chapter 9 Troubleshooting ACH Issues

  1. Scroll and select the ACH File that you want to download from the list. You can also search for the ACH File using Filename Description and Date. The File View displays the first 15 lines of the selected ACH File. For example:

  2. Click Download.

ACH Lock Errors There are two possible error messages that can prevent a user from running an ACH process in PrismHR due to the processes being locked.

Error 1: ACH Is Locked at a Different Session ACH is locked by {user’s name} at a different session. Locked on {date} at {time} Continue? This error occurs when a user is disconnected while running an ACH process and attempts to continue after logging back in. It also displays if the user is logged into two or more different sessions (such as having PrismHR open in two windows or tabs at the same time) and they attempt to run any of the ACH processes in both of them. Solution: The user can regain control of the ACH processes by clicking Yes. • If the user had only one session open, they can continue with the ACH process they wanted to run. • If the user had more than one session open, they can continue in the active session and they will lose control of the ACH process in any other sessions.

Error 2: ACH Is Locked ACH is locked by {user’s name} Locked on {date} at {time} This error occurs when another user is (or was) running one of the ACH processes.

Accounting User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 104 Chapter 9 Troubleshooting ACH Issues

Solution: Make sure that the user named in the error message is not actually engaged in an ACH process or working in any ACH menu option. If they are, do nothing.

Note: If they were disconnected while running one of the processes and did not attempt to continue where they left off, then it is safe to clear the lock.

If they are not working in an ACH process: 1. Open ACH Clear Lock (found in the Back Office menu under Operations|Change). If you do not have access to ACH Clear Lock, work with another user at your organization who does. 2. Click Clear Lock. 3. Click Yes to confirm that you want to clear the lock. 4. Click OK.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 6 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction The ACH User Guide explains the functions and features of ACH processing in PrismHR.

Intended Audience The contents are for users who are: • Involved in ACH processing • Familiar with the use of an internet browser

Note: Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot set global ACH information.

Your organization should already have set up the initial defaults, files, and preferences required for system administration, as well as client information. You should also have general knowledge of ACH processing. Explaining industry-specific topics other than the use of this software product is outside the scope of this document. This document does not cover the specifics of transmitting your ACH files to financial institutions. Your organization and the financial institution should have an established procedure for this.

Important Considerations for Processing ACH in PrismHR The ACH processing in PrismHR requires that your organization be set up to use ACH originators and consolidated ACH processing.

Note: Non-consolidated ACH will not be supported in the near future.

The ACH processes bypass the normal security filters. Any user who has access to the external or internal ACH processes must be someone who can have access to all relevant clients and employees. (External processing is for your organization’s clients while internal processing is for your organization’s employees.) Some forms expose pay amounts, therefore you must only grant access to the ACH features in user roles for users who ought to be allowed to see them. Access to processing for internal payrolls is separate from processing for external payrolls, and user access to each feature is controlled separately. Only one user at a time can access the ACH processing options. This ensures that data is not accidentally duplicated.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 7 Chapter 1 Introduction

Service Providers with access to System|Change|User Roles can only be assigned Full or Deny access options for the following ACH Processing forms:

Using ACH Network The Automated Clearing House (ACH) Network is a nationwide system that uses electronic payments exclusively, rather than physical checks or forms. The electronic transactions are passed between financial institutions, corporations, and consumers throughout the country. The following illustration is based on a figure published by the National Automated Clearing House Association (NACHA), that explains the basic transaction flow within the ACH network.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 8 Chapter 1 Introduction

To make the illustration about ACH participants more specific: 1. Your organization is the originator of the ACH transactions. These include payroll transactions and commercial transactions. 2. You create your ACH files for your clients (or your own company) and send them to the Originating Depository Financial Institution (ODFI) for each client (or your own bank). In PrismHR, the ODFIs to which you send the ACH files are known as “ACH originators,” which is a simpler way to describe them—even though, technically speaking, your organization is the originator. 3. Each ODFI transmits their ACH transactions to an ACH operator. There may actually be two ACH operators involved—one for the ODFI, one for the RDFI (Receiving Depository Financial Institution)—if both institutions do not use the same operator. 4. The ACH operator sends the ACH transactions to the appropriate RDFI.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 1 Introduction

  1. The RDFI transmits the ACH transactions to the receiving employees (for payroll direct deposits, usually) or companies (for commercial transactions).

ACH Processing in PrismHR PrismHR can create the ACH files you must send to various financial institutions. A simplified version of the ACH process in PrismHR is illustrated below.

To make the illustration about ACH participants more specific: • PrismHR processes your payroll and writes records to a repository known as the ACH Journal. • You periodically (once a day or perhaps more often) “build” your ACH, which creates a file according to the ACH rules set forth by the National Automated Clearing House Association (NACHA). In addition, when you build your ACH, PrismHR also creates reports and backs up the ACH Journal and the NACHA directory. The replicas are the ACH History and NACHA Archive, respectively. • When PrismHR builds the “NACHA file”, it automatically clears out the records from the ACH Journal.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Chapter 1 Introduction

• The NACHA file is the file you send to one or more financial institutions, known as ACH originators. • If, for whatever reason, you need to resubmit an ACH transaction, PrismHR uses the ACH History to create a resubmittal file you must edit before you build your ACH. Specific information concerning NACHA formats, records and files are beyond the scope of this guide. For more information about NACHA’s ACH record format specifications, please refer to the latest ACH Rules, one of the documents published by NACHA.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

Chapter 2 System-Level Setup Your organization can define ACH transaction information at the system level and then administer it individually at the client level, depending on their accounts and needs.

ACH Settings in System Parameters Settings in System Parameters control some ACH features for all clients.

ACH Processing Method PrismHR processes ACH information using the consolidated method, which sends one file for multiple checking accounts. This method works well for organizations that process payrolls with the client’s checking accounts.

Note: The non-consolidated method is not supported in PrismHR.

To set the ACH processing method: 1. Open System Parameters (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change).

  1. Select the appropriate option from the Consolidated ACH File Processing Used drop-down: • Yes: Use the consolidated method, which processes multiple checking accounts for one ACH originating bank. Your organization will process ACH using the features in PrismHR.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

•    Company: Use the consolidated method with company batching, which processes multiple checking
     accounts for one ACH originating bank and sorts by client.

Other Controls These settings control other basic ACH behaviors in PrismHR.

  1. Enter the Maximum ACH Batch amount to process in a single ACH transaction batch. The system moves any amount in excess of this amount to the next batch in the file.
  2. Enter the Minimum ACH Window, which is the minimum number of days required to process ACH transactions. Any payroll batch with an ACH transaction must be at least this many days in the future; if it is not, then the system will generate paychecks to print instead of ACH transactions.
  3. Enter the ACH Billing Days Offset, which is number of days to offset ACH for invoicing. If the system should draft the ACH the day before the payroll, for example, enter -1 in this field.
  4. Enter the number of Days Into Future for ACH Selection after which PrismHR selects ACH transactions to submit to the ACH originating bank.
  5. Click Save.

Using ACH Originators An ACH originator is a financial institution to which a client sends ACH files. The financial institution becomes the “originating DFI” by submitting the transactions to the ACH network. If you process ACH transactions for clients, each client can have a different financial institution. Use the ACH Originators form to maintain records for each institution.

Maintaining Financial Institution Information Use the ACH Originators panel to maintain the financial institution information.

To maintain financial institution information, do the following: 1. Go to the ACH Originators form on the System|Change menu. 2. Complete the following fields in the ACH Originators panel:

  3. If the service bank requires you to provide a different account number for offset transactions, enter the Immediate Destination Identification # (Offset).

When selected, ACH transactions are tracked in a “suspense” account and do not move to the cash account until the ACH batch file is created. ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 28 Chapter 2 System-Level Setup

  1. Select Suppress EOT Character to suppress appending the end-of-transmission character (Char(26)) at the end of the ACH deposit file.
  2. Enter the Slash Replacement Character that PrismHR replaces with a slash when it builds the ACH file. For example, ^.
  3. Select Use Suspense Accounting if this bank account should use suspense accounting. When selected, ACH transactions are tracked in a “suspense” account and do not move to the cash account until the ACH batch file is created. That allows users to easily reconcile account balances based on transactions processed by the bank. See Suspense Accounts on page 29.

Suspense Accounts Rather than have ACH data update immediately against a cash account before it is transmitted to the bank, which can cause confusion when users attempt to reconcile the account, your organization might want to create a “suspense” account for any bank account that processes ACH transactions. Each voucher is posted in detail against the suspense account. During ACH file creation, the total of the vouchers transmitted in a batch comes out of the suspense account and hits the cash account. This allows for easier reconciliation, as the ACH suspense account should be zero each day or reconcilable. It is easier to balance the bank’s daily reports because the totals in the cash account should match the amounts directly.

For the accounts that indicate they use a suspense account, enter the Suspense GL Account.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 40 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing ACH file tasks involve building the ACH file and sending it to your ACH originators. They can also include any review or maintenance you need to perform on the ACH files. The features you use for processing ACH are found in the Back Office menu under Operations|Action. When a user opens a form, that feature is locked and no other users can access it until the user is finished. This prevents multiple users from processing the same files, which would result in erroneous duplicate ACH transactions. This locking feature is called “concurrency control”.

External Payrolls External payrolls are for the clients managed by your organization.

Processing ACH for External Payroll Processing ACH for external payroll (your organization’s clients) involves two forms: • ACH Processing: View a summary of ACH transactions ready to send to the bank and create or process batches of transactions. • ACH Batch Control: Complete processing for the selected batch.

Note: The first time you open the form each day, you might see a warning message. Click Continue to proceed.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 41 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

ACH Processing The ACH Processing form lists all unposted batches (unless you use the filters at the top). • The first column indicates the Actions you can take, either to start or finish processing the ACH. Note: To process multiple ACH files, select the checkboxes that only display for the following actions: • Start ACH Process • Finish ACH Process • Retry ACH Process When you select at least one action checkbox for processing, Build File displays and the Actions links are disabled. (Click Select All to select all files for processing.) Important! During multiple file ACH processing, the system locks the ACH forms and displays one of the following warnings when users try to access them: • If accessing locked files using the ACH Clear Lock form:

     Click OK to continue, then after one hour users can try accessing the ACH Clear Lock form again to
     unlock the forms. However, if the system has not finished processing the files another warning displays,
     "Multi-File ACH has not completed processing. If you clear the lock you could interrupt the creation of
     ACH files. Are you sure you want to clear the lock?" Click Yes to clear the lock.
•    If accessing locked files using the ACH Processing form:

     Click OK to continue and try again later.
Note: See Performing Multiple ACH Processing for detailed information.

• The Status indicates whether the files are available or if the batch is in process. • The other columns display the ACH Originator Names, the ACH Batch ID (if the batch is in progress), the total number of journals included in that batch, and other relevant totals. • If you do not assign an ACH Originator to a bank account and transactions are processed through that bank account, a message displays at the bottom of this form for each missing ACH Originator. For example:

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 42 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

These messages list the number of journals that would be available for processing, if the ACH Originator was
assigned in the Bank Accounts form.
Clicking the ACH Originator Missing link opens the Bank Accounts form where you can add the ACH
Originator for the bank account in the ACH Processor ID field on the ACH Setup panel.

Note the following: • Once a user creates a batch, you can process the transactions included in the batch into a file and send it to the financial institution. • Creating the batch locks the transactions in the batch; any new transactions created when users post payrolls will not be added to the ACH batch, which allows payroll processors to continue working while you work on the ACH batch. Those new transactions wait for a future ACH batch. The buttons at the top right are available to users who can access the associated forms. • Completed ACH Transactions is for reprinting reports, downloading the original ACH file, or reopening the ACH batch to rebuild the file; see Viewing and Rebuilding Files for External Payroll ACH Batch on page 45. • Hold Management enables you to place direct deposits on hold before sending them to the financial institution, or to release direct deposits from hold so they can then be sent; see Holding/Releasing Direct Deposits (External Payroll) on page 47.

To process ACH for external payroll: 1. Specify which transactions to include in the ACH file build using the following filters: a. Use the File Type Limiter to indicate whether you want to build the ACH file with Debits and Credits, Debits Only, or Credits Only. The default is to include both debits and credits. Note: If your organization has specified an offset account on any of the bank accounts included in the ACH batch, the system creates the offset entry regardless of the selection in the File Type Limiter drop- down. If your bank requires strict credit-only or debit-only files (files with no offsetting entries), then you must ensure that there are no offset entries defined for those accounts. b. Use the Child Support Filter to indicate whether you want to build the ACH file with Child Support and Other, Child Support Only, or Not Child Support transactions. The default is to include all transactions. c. Click Refresh to filter the list to show only the selected transactions. It might take a brief moment for the list to update. For example:

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 43 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

  1. Click the Action link or the checkboxes (for multiple ACH file processing) on the left for the originator and ACH transactions you need to process. Note the following: • When you click Start ACH Process, the system creates an ACH batch and assigns the journals to that batch. The ACH Batch Control form then opens. • When you click Retry ACH Process or Finish ACH Process, the ACH Batch Control form opens. • If the batch was put on hold, you can click Review Holds to manage the hold (see Holding/Releasing Direct Deposits (External Payroll) on page 47). • To start the multiple ACH process, select your files and click Build File, which locks the files. The following message displays, “The Multi-File ACH process will now start. You will receive an email when the process has been completed. Do you want to continue?” Click Yes to run the ACH process. (The ACH Processing form closes.) • PrismHR is responsible for defining and setting up the SFTP server for clients when processing multiple ACH files.

ACH Batch Control The ACH Batch Control form summarizes the transactions included in the batch.

  1. Click the appropriate button to proceed as needed: • Build Review Reports: When you click this button, the system generates the report(s) that you use to review the ACH information for the batch. Once they are ready, you can click the link(s) to view, print, or export the report(s). The reports are available only while you remain in the ACH Batch Control form. If you exit the batch after running the reports and then you return to it later, you must regenerate the reports to see the output. The data in the reports will not change because the transaction list is locked once you create the batch.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 44 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

•    Build ACH File: After you build the report(s) and then review them to confirm that the information is
     correct, click this button to build the ACH files. The system generates the ACH Build Detail Report, any
     other reports as appropriate for the batch, and the text file(s) for you to download. After a batch posts,
     the total number of detail lines in the ACH file displays, along with the total number of debits and
     credits.
     Note: There is at least one text file; there may be more depending on the format and the transactions.
     Send all text files to your financial institution.

Note: Text files can have either the .txt or .csv extension, depending on their format.

•    Reset Batch: This button is available until you build the ACH file. Click this button if there is an issue with
     the ACH batch and you want to delete it. The transactions in the original batch are released and made
     available for inclusion in a new batch.
•    Close: Click this button to close the ACH Batch Control and return to the Pending ACH Transactions form.
•    Exit ACH Processing: Click this button to close both of the windows.

Viewing and Rebuilding Files for External Payroll ACH Batch Viewing and rebuilding files for an external payroll ACH batch involves two forms: • Completed ACH Transactions: View a summary of completed ACH batches. • ACH Batch Control History: Reprint reports or reopen an external payroll ACH batch to rebuild the file.

Completed ACH Transactions 1. By default, the ACH Originator ID field displays All and the list includes all completed batches. You can enter an ACH Originator ID and then click Refresh to see only the completed batches that have been posted for the specified ACH originator. 2. You can filter the list by dates; the default Start Date is one week before the current date, and the End Date is the current date. Enter different dates and then click Refresh to see only the completed batches posted during that date range. For example:

Note: You can select multiple ACH transactions by selecting the ACH Batch ID checkboxes.
  1. Click the ACH Batch ID of the ACH batch you want to work with. The ACH Batch Control History form opens.

ACH Batch Control History The ACH Batch Control History form summarizes the transactions included in the posted batch.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 45 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

  1. Click each link under ACH Files for Download to download the original ACH file(s). You would typically do this when the original ACH file was misplaced. There is at least one file; there may be more depending on the format and the transactions. Send all files to your financial institution.
  2. Click one of the buttons to proceed as needed: • Build Review Reports: Rebuilds the report(s) as they were at the time the original batch was posted. The number of reports depends on the financial institution’s format. Note: The Build Review Reports button is disabled for completed ACH transactions. (This button is still enabled for any ACH batch that is not completed, including reopened batches.) Instead, you can use ACH reports in the Report Center for these transactions. One of the following messages displays when you click this button for completed transactions, depending on the form you are accessing: • ACH Batch Control History form: When you click Build Review Reports for a completed ACH batch the following message displays, “ACH reporting for completed ACH batches is now available in Report Center.” • ACH Batch Control form: After creating the ACH file, when you click Build Review Reports for a completed ACH batch the following message displays, “Build Review already completed, you can access the reports by clicking the links on the screen.” In place of this disabled functionality, you can use the following ACH reports in the Report Center for completed ACH transactions: • ACH File Cash Receipt Audit: Includes details of ACH cash receipt transactions. (Data from ACH history.) • ACH History: Includes detail and summary views of the ACH File History (see pivot). Now includes columns for Child Support and Garnishment Deposits. (Data from ACH history.) • ACH Reconciliation Net: Includes net ACH amounts for payroll invoices, child support, and electronic garnishments. (Data from ACH history.) • ACH Resubmission by Transmit Date: Includes details of ACH resubmission transactions. (Data from ACH history.) Note: See the Report Center documentation for information on how to build report views. • Reopen: Reopens the batch if there was an issue with the original file. It becomes available in the ACH Processing form for external payrolls, where it will be available as In Process and locked down to any changes. You can finish the ACH process again for the external payroll.

Performing a Mass Download of Created Bank Files After processing multiple ACH files, you can download the created bank files by selecting at least one ACH Batch ID checkbox to display Download File. For example:

Select the checkboxes and click Download File. A message displays, “Download ACH Files?” Click Yes to download the files. A new window opens displaying the downloaded ACH files in a .zip file, which you can open and save to another location. Note: You can use this method in case the system did not automatically download the files to the SFTP server.

Holding/Releasing Direct Deposits (External Payroll) Use the ACH Hold Review and Maintenance form to place direct deposits on hold before sending them to the bank, or to release direct deposits from hold so they can then be sent to the bank. After selecting the filter settings and then selecting Find Journals, the form displays direct deposits that are already on hold, not on hold, or both, according to the selected filter settings. You can also filter your view to debit or credit transactions only, or filter to view records for a specific client, bank ID, batch, pay date, or employee.

To place direct deposits on hold: 1. Set the filter options to see the transactions you need: • On Hold Status: Select the status you want to view from the drop-down (Yes, No, Both). The default is Yes. • Pay Date: Select a date to see transactions from that pay day. • Client: Select one client to see transactions associated with that client. • Employee ID: Enter an employee’s ID to see transactions associated with person. • Payroll Batch: Select a payroll batch ID to see transactions from that payroll. • Bank Account: Select a bank account ID/name to see transactions originating from that financial institution. • Debit/Credit: Select which transactions you want to see from the drop-down (Debit, Credit, Both). 2. Select Find Journals. The list populates with transactions that match your filter settings, displaying the following information: • Hold: The hold status for the transaction. If selected, the transaction is on hold. • Journal ID: The ACH journal for the transaction. • Bank Account: The bank account ID where the money will be either debited or credited. • Type: The account type (checking or savings). • Company: The client ID associated with the transaction.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 47 Chapter 4 File Tasks and ACH Processing

•    Payroll: The payroll ID for the payroll that included the transaction.
•    Pay Date: The date of the payroll that included the transaction.
•    Employee ID: The employee ID, if any.
•    Name: The employee name, if any.
•    DB/CR: Specifies whether the transaction was a debit or a credit.
•    Routing: The ABA routing number (also called a transit number) for the checking account where the
     money will be either debited or credited.
•    Amount: The amount of the transaction.
  1. You can change the Hold status for individual transactions as needed by selecting or deselecting the Hold setting. You can also: • Click All On Hold to place all transactions in the list on hold. • Click All Off Hold to remove the hold status from all transactions in the list.

Note: You cannot place a transaction on hold if it is in an ACH batch.

  1. Click Save to save any changes, then click OK in the confirmation message that notifies you of the number of records that changed.

  2. When you are finished, click the Close button or to exit the form and clear the ACH Lock.

Deleting a Hold You can remove holds on direct deposits in the system. Note: The Delete button only displays when the On Hold Status is set to Yes.

To remove a hold from the system: 1. Set the On Hold Status to Yes, then select Find Journals. The list of journals on hold displays. 2. Select a journal that displays in the list. 3. Click Delete. A warning displays:

  1. Select Yes to remove the hold on the selected journal.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 67 Chapter 5 Pre-ACH Processing

Chapter 5 Pre-ACH Processing Pre-ACH processing allows your organization to send a file days before you run a payroll to ensure that all transactions can be fulfilled.

Overview of the Pre-ACH Process in PrismHR Typically, you use pre-ACH processing to protect your organization from unacceptable situations with high-risk clients. You transmit a prenote—a non-dollar entry to alert the receiving bank that an ACH transaction is forthcoming—that allows you to verify that there are no problems with the forthcoming transaction, or resolve any issues that might be revealed by the pre-ACH process. This assures that your organization does not lose money on transactions that would not be fulfilled by a client. The system sends the pre-ACH file a number of days (usually 5–7) ahead of the regular ACH file. The amount you transmit in the pre-ACH can be equal to either: • An arbitrary figure, or • The average of the last n regular payrolls run (for example, the average of the last 5 regular payrolls).

Pre-ACH and Floating Deposit The system uses the pre-ACH amount to “settle out” on the invoice. For example: The average of the last five invoices for a client is $1120.50. Your organization processes regular payroll runs on Thursday for Friday pay days. You elect to perform pre-ACH processing five days before the payroll runs, therefore, you transmit a pre-ACH on Mondays. When you process the actual payroll on Thursday, for Friday’s pay date, the system then “settles” the balance. If the client’s actual payroll is $1100.00, the system sends them a $22.50 credit. If it is more, the system sends an ACH charge to them for the balance due. Essentially, the pre-ACH processing allows your client companies to have a “floating deposit” of their average payroll, which is always in transit. However, they get to use that floating deposit each week.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 68 Chapter 5 Pre-ACH Processing

Bounced Transactions As part of the process, your accounting department must ensure any pre-ACH that does not clear (or “bounces”) is marked immediately. After they check the bank’s list of bounces each morning, the accounting department must then: 1. Handle any “bounced” ACH accounts. 2. Set the value of the Payroll Processing Through Date field to reflect that the accounting department has handled/entered all of the bounced ACH files received from the bank that day.

After the accounting department sets the Payroll Processing Through Date field, you can process or post any pre-ACH prenote.

Timing of Pre-ACH Process PrismHR runs the pre-ACH process once a day, the first time a user opens the ACH Processing or the ACH Processing (Internal Payroll) form. While this process runs, users will typically see a message that reads “Please wait - processing Pre-ACH.” The pre-ACH process will not run again on the same day unless a user sets up pre-ACH on a pay group that did not have it before. The system will run it again the next time a user opens one of the forms. The system will not duplicate any transactions if it runs the process more than once in a day; it only creates new transactions.

Important Considerations for Pre-ACH Processing You would not want to send a pre-ACH on Monday when the payroll department is likely to complete the payroll processing on Tuesday for the Friday pay day. If the pre-ACH processing exposes on Wednesday that the transaction will not be properly fulfilled, it is too late to recover from that. • If the financial institution is delayed in notifying you of an upcoming problem identified by the pre-ACH process, you run the risk of processing a payroll that will ultimately bounce. In such cases, you will have only collected (or refunded) the difference from what you thought you were getting in the pre-ACH run. • If you administer the process carefully, however, you can limit your risk, especially where ACH bounces are predictable at two days or fewer.

Your organization must decide when each pay group should use pre-ACH processing. The process is a rule based on pay groups, not clients. You must select the One Payroll/Pay Group option in the Client Details Payroll tab so that the system correctly assigns the credits for pre-ACH processing. (Selecting this option ensures that PrismHR always processes weekly and biweekly payrolls separately, even on weeks where they pay on the same day.) If your organization decides to implement the pre-ACH processing feature for the first time, you should begin slowly to ensure that it behaves as desired.

Pre-ACH Process This figure illustrates the flow of pre-ACH processing.

Pre-ACH Amount Details Type Average Use the pre-ACH invoice fields to specify an average for up to five invoices. You can enter any information in the Pre-ACH Invoice Number and Pre-ACH Invoice Amount columns, because the system does not verify it. For example, if you are setting up a pre-ACH prenote on the client for the first time and plan to use five invoices for the average that will typically be around $10,000, you can enter five “starter” invoices using any invoice number (for example, START1, START2, START3, and so on) and enter $10,000 for each. When the system processes a real payroll, it drops the first starter invoice from the list and inserts a real invoice at the end. After the first five payrolls, all the starter invoices are no longer on the list. The system sends pre-ACH prenotes using the average of the invoices in the list. After five payrolls, the average will be based on actual data. • The system lists each Pre-ACH Invoice Number in the chain for seeking the current average to pre-ACH. You can enter different invoice numbers. • The Pre-ACH Invoice Amount is each invoice’s contribution amount. You can enter a different amount to force a new average. The Current Average displays below the table. Flat Enter the Pre-ACH Override to use a flat amount rather than the Current Average of invoices and amounts. If you use the flat method, the system always uses that amount for pre-ACH for the client and this pay group. The system never checks nor averages the invoice amounts.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 72 Chapter 5 Pre-ACH Processing

  1. If setting up Pre-ACH for the first time, enter the batch number of any completed batch in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field. For each pay group, the daily Pre-ACH program compares the in-progress batch number with the batch number entered in this field. If these are identical, the system skips the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH processing. When you enter the ID of a previously completed batch, you indicate that PrismHR needs to process the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH. The system will evaluate the in-progress batch for processing, create the appropriate ACH entries, and automatically update this field with the in-progress batch number. This prevents double entries from occurring.

Note: In the case where Pre-ACH entries were already created for a batch, but this batch was later deleted and re-created (therefore giving it a new batch number), you must manually update this field with the new batch number. For example, assume a Pre-ACH prenote was sent for batch 202202, but for some reason you decided to delete that batch and create the next regular payroll batch to replace it. If the system assigns number 202205 to the new batch, you must change the value in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field from 202202 to 202205. This ensures that PrismHR does not re-transmit the Pre-ACH entry.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 73 Chapter 6 Troubleshooting ACH Issues

Chapter 6 Troubleshooting ACH Issues These are procedures for uncommon situations:

ACH Lock Errors There are two possible error messages that can prevent a user from running an ACH process in PrismHR due to the processes being locked.

Error 1: ACH Is Locked at a Different Session ACH is locked by {user’s name} at a different session. Locked on {date} at {time} Continue? This error occurs when a user is disconnected while running an ACH process and attempts to continue after logging back in. It also displays if the user is logged into two or more different sessions (such as having PrismHR open in two windows or tabs at the same time) and they attempt to run any of the ACH processes in both of them. Solution: The user can regain control of the ACH processes by clicking Yes. • If the user had only one session open, they can continue with the ACH process they wanted to run. • If the user had more than one session open, they can continue in the active session and they will lose control of the ACH process in any other sessions.

Error 2: ACH Is Locked ACH is locked by {user’s name} Locked on {date} at {time} This error occurs when another user is (or was) running one of the ACH processes.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 74 Chapter 6 Troubleshooting ACH Issues

Solution: Make sure that the user named in the error message is not actually engaged in an ACH process or working in any ACH menu option. If they are, do nothing.

Note: If they were disconnected while running one of the processes and did not attempt to continue where they left off, then it is safe to clear the lock.

If they are not working in an ACH process: 1. Open ACH Clear Lock (found in the Back Office menu under Operations|Change). If you do not have access to ACH Clear Lock, work with another user at your organization who does. 2. Click Clear Lock. 3. Click Yes to confirm that you want to clear the lock. 4. Click OK.

Clearing the Lock on ACH Processing Features Do not clear the lock on ACH processing features until you have verified that no one at your organization is engaged in processing any ACH files. If they are, do not use the ACH Clear Lock feature.

To clear the lock: 1. After ensuring that no users are actively working in any ACH forms, click Clear Lock. 2. Click Yes to confirm that you want to clear the lock. 3. Click OK.

Processing Company Name Enter your company name as the PEO. ACH File Options Select the Put Company ID on ACH file detail lines position 40-54 option. Third Party Format Select Cachet.

  2. In the Cachet panel, do the following:

Creating a Bank Account for the Client To continue the ACH setup process, you must create a bank account for each client. For example, if there are 100 clients, then you need to create 100 client bank accounts.

To create a client bank account, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. Select Bank Accounts under System|Change. The Bank Accounts form displays.

Note: Enter the same information as found on the Billing tab in the Client|Change > Client Details form, specifically in the Electronic Billing panel.

  1. Complete the following fields to continue the bank account setup for each client you want to include in the Cachet file. See the Payroll User Guide for information about the other fields.

    Field Description Account ID Enter or select your checking number, which must be an integer. Reference Enter the client’s name. Bank Name/Bank Address Enter the bank’s name and address that the client uses. Offset Account ID Enter or select the ID of your bank where you deposit or withdraw funds. Rebate Bill Code Enter NETPAY. Employer ID Enter or select the employer ID, which is the same ID on the Client Details record for that client, or enter the employer ID on your bank account, if the client is assigned a bank account with a different employer.

  2. In the ACH Setup panel, enter the following information:

    Field Description ACH Processor ID Enter or select the same ACH Processor ID that you created earlier. Company Name (Batch Header) Enter the client’s company name.

Creating/Adjusting Your Existing Payroll Checking Account Cachet requires two checking accounts to perform ACH processing: one account for direct deposits to employees, and a second account for withdrawals from your client.

ACH User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 83 Chapter 8 Setting Up ACH Deposits with Cachet Financial Services

Note: These steps may vary depending upon your payroll checking account set up. Please log in to the Customer Resource Center and click Request Customer Support, if you have any questions. A support representative will contact you as soon as possible.

Making Adjustments to Your Checking Account If you have an established checking account for payroll, and you want to have Cachet process your ACH, then you need to input an Offset Account ID in the Bank Accounts form and change the ACH Processor ID to Cachet in the ACH Setup panel.

To make adjustments to your bank account, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. Select Bank Accounts under System|Change. The Bank Accounts form opens. 2. In your bank account, in the Offset Account ID field, enter or select the ID of the account you set up earlier. 3. In the ACH Setup panel, enter the following information:

 Field                             Description
 ACH Processor ID                  Enter or select the ACH Processor ID that you created earlier.
 Company Name (Batch Header) Enter your company name.
  1. Click Save.

Creating a New Checking Account for Client Withdrawals To create a new checking account for client withdrawals, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. Select Bank Accounts under System|Change. The Bank Accounts form opens. 2. Enter the new Account ID and the same bank information as your established checking account. 3. In the ACH Setup panel, enter the following information:

 Field                             Description
 ACH Processor ID                  Enter or select the ACH Processor ID that you created earlier.
 Company Name (Batch Header) Enter your company name.
  1. Click Save.

Note: If you do not have an account established for payroll, then you need to create a new checking account for employee deposits and employee withdrawals.
